2610.34356.tldr: RynnLAM learns 3D-grounded continuous latent actions from 30K hours of videos to pretrain a 4B flow-matching VLA.
2610.34356.summary: Action-labeled data is scarce and embodiments differ, limiting VLA scaling. RynnLAM extracts continuous latent actions using residual future-feature prediction, camera-compensated 3D-flow supervision and camera-motion decoupling over 30.1K hours of human/robot/sim video; the VLA predicts latent-action chunks via flow matching before embodiment adaptation. Reaches 98.8% on LIBERO and 84.7% on LIBERO-Plus.
2610.34356.why: Latent-action pretraining from human video is a relevant VLA data recipe, though gains are shown mainly on saturated sim benchmarks.

2610.34186.tldr: HuGe pretrains humanoid VLAs on 2,000+ hours of egocentric human and robot data, predicting latent motion tokens for a whole-body controller.
2610.34186.summary: Humanoid VLAs need costly whole-body demos. HuGe uses three VLA architectures that output latent motion tokens plus hand signals, trained in three stages (egocentric pretraining, humanoid adaptation, fine-tuning) with pseudo-proprioception via sim playback and arm re-rendering to bridge embodiment gaps.
2610.34186.why: Egocentric human-data transfer is relevant, but the focus is humanoid whole-body control, not dexterity.

2610.34453.tldr: ARPG pretrains an action-representation encoder on human manipulation data, then trains a compact 130M generative policy in that latent space for dexterous hands.
2610.34453.summary: Scarce dexterous robot demos must learn both action representations and conditional distributions. ARPG decouples these: an action encoder is pretrained on large-scale human hand data and frozen, and a small generative backbone models task-conditioned actions in its latent space. Reports state of the art on the DexJoCo benchmark.
2610.34453.why: Directly about leveraging human hand data to improve generative dexterous policies.

2610.34593.tldr: Adds a training-only future-video prediction expert as an auxiliary loss when fine-tuning pretrained VLAs, discarded at inference.
2610.34593.summary: VLA action objectives lack visual-future supervision. A randomly initialized video expert conditioned on the VLA's vision-language features predicts future video latents; its loss co-trains the backbone, then it is removed, keeping inference cost unchanged.
2610.34593.why: Cheap way to get world-model-style supervision into VLA fine-tuning; relevant to unified video-action ideas.

2610.34564.tldr: FlockWorld is a Boids-based testbed for multi-agent action-conditioned video world models, with a flow-matching DiT baseline.
2610.34564.summary: Most video world models handle one agent. FlockWorld renders synchronized egocentric views of a configurable boid population; FlockDiT jointly generates multi-agent videos, finding joint generation helps detection and diffusion forcing improves rollout fidelity.
2610.34564.why: Toy multi-agent video world model testbed; tangential.

2610.34108.tldr: RoboDuo uses a coding agent to check VLA task completion and invoke an atomic-skill VLA to recover failures, on LIBERO variants.
2610.34108.summary: VLAs do not detect failed steps in long-horizon tasks. RoboDuo has an LLM agent write code that runs a full-task VLA, checks completion, and calls an atomic VLA to finish remaining steps, without retraining the base VLA; trained with new LIBERO-Atomic/Code/Judge datasets.
2610.34108.why: Agentic recovery wrapper for VLAs; mostly system-level, sim-only.

2610.34105.tldr: X-World transfers a pretrained video diffusion backbone to multi-view robot control via a Q-Former and shared action expert with async chunking.
2610.34105.summary: Video priors must handle variable cameras and action interfaces. X-World adds residual cross-view attention to a video backbone, aggregates features with a layer-aligned Q-Former into a shared action expert, and uses staged training. Gets 98.5% on LIBERO and 76.5% zero-shot on LIBERO-Plus.
2610.34105.why: Another video-prior-to-policy recipe; relevant to video-action models but benchmark-driven.

2610.34519.tldr: TRIAGE accelerates VLA inference by choosing per-token between KV-cache reuse and pruning based on visual token drift.
2610.34519.summary: Onboard VLA inference is prefill-bound. A diagnostic shows reusing cached KV is fine for low-drift tokens but up to 4.4x worse than pruning for high-drift tokens; TRIAGE combines both via a drift threshold, training-free.
2610.34519.why: Useful practical VLA speedup insight; tangential to core interests.

2610.34051.tldr: BEHAVIOR-Spatial benchmark measures spatial QA, grounding, and action on BEHAVIOR-1K to relate VLM spatial understanding to VLA behavior.
2610.34051.summary: Task success alone cannot show spatial instruction following. The benchmark has 3,256 questions, 1,240 grounding queries and 24 action tasks; baselines get 41.6% on held-out configs but 16.1% under changed instructions, while oracle target cues raise these to 60.3%/38.0%.
2610.34051.why: Diagnostic benchmark for VLA spatial grounding; moderately relevant.

2611.18666.tldr: ReMoVe refines a video model's own coarse human motion into 3D meshes and depth to condition coherent human video generation.
2611.18666.summary: Generated human videos drift in body shape and identity. ReMoVe treats coarse output as a motion hypothesis, recovers and refines it as a mesh with depth, and re-conditions the generator for consistency.
2611.18666.why: Human video generation quality; not relevant.

2610.34303.tldr: EditDistill distills an image-edit transformation into a descriptor that steers a video diffusion model for video editing.
2610.34303.summary: Video editing lacks image editing's controllability. EditDistill edits the first frame with an image editor, encodes the edit into a descriptor, and injects it into a video diffusion model with alignment and DINO structure losses.

2610.34251.tldr: CogMemory adds a 3.45M-parameter variational memory module with state-space encoding and gated retrieval for long-horizon VLAs.
2610.34251.summary: VLAs lack effective long-term memory. CogMemory compresses trajectories into latent memory slots via a selective SSM encoder and variational compression, retrieved by gated cross-attention during action generation.
2610.34251.why: Touches history-conditioned policies, but appears incremental.

2610.34163.tldr: SAC agent learns dynamic crowd-barrier placement in a crowd simulator built from segmented scenes.
2610.34163.summary: Fixed barrier layouts cause congestion. A simulation reconstructed from real crowd scenes trains SAC to move barriers, generalizing to unseen crowd sizes.
2610.34163.why: Applied RL for crowd control; not relevant.

2610.34370.tldr: ThinkLocoManip is an LLM agentic harness interleaving reasoning and tool calls for legged loco-manipulation.
2610.34370.summary: Long-horizon loco-manipulation needs error recovery. The harness orchestrates perception, navigation, manipulation and locomotion tools in a ReAct-style loop with cross-domain skills.

2610.34060.tldr: A LiDAR-only GNN learns interaction-aware path corrections from unlabeled trajectories for construction robots.
2610.34060.summary: Construction robots must anticipate workers. A GNN predicts residuals over constant-velocity extrapolation to offset planner waypoints, reducing path irregularity 39.2% and raising min TTC 38.3%.

2610.34208.tldr: CORMA uses a constraint-routed Decision Mamba for offline safe RL with multiple cost constraints.
2610.34208.summary: DT-based safe RL handles single constraints and scales poorly. CORMA routes multiple cost-to-go tokens through a Mamba backbone to generalize to unseen budget combinations efficiently.
2610.34208.why: Offline safe RL sequence modeling; tangential.

2610.34092.tldr: Leta distills autoregressive video diffusion with direct score-difference estimation and cross-chunk future credit via VJPs.
2610.34092.summary: DMD estimates the full student score indirectly and detached-history training ignores future chunks. ScoreDelta estimates the teacher-student correction directly from denoising residuals and FutureCredit learns cross-chunk credit from next-chunk teacher VJPs.
2610.34092.why: Few-step distillation ideas for AR video diffusion; relevant to video generation interests.

2610.34501.tldr: Empirical study of non-monotonic RL training showing common final/best-checkpoint selection misestimates the best policy visited.
2610.34501.summary: RL performance oscillates during training. The paper introduces diagnostic metrics for performance degradation and evaluates policy-selection criteria with an on-policy actor-critic on continuous control, finding widely used strategies unreliable.

2610.34384.tldr: AndroidFlux benchmarks failure recovery of mobile-use agents from controlled error checkpoints and releases offline RL data.
2610.34384.summary: Clean-start success does not measure recovery. AndroidFlux restores trajectories to checkpoints around errors and adds a reward-modeling benchmark; recovery only partially correlates with clean success.

2610.34466.tldr: IntNet is a MARL framework sharing predicted intents with scheduled communication for cooperative autonomous driving.
2610.34466.summary: Cooperative driving MARL needs safe coordination. IntNet forecasts policy outputs, shares intents over V2V with a GAT and a bandwidth scheduler.

2610.34575.tldr: Cumulative Marginal Matching trains few-step generators by matching base and few-step marginal distributions along the whole flow.
2610.34575.summary: Few-step distillation objectives usually enforce point-level alignment at one time. CMM views flow matching as a sequence of marginals and optimizes the cumulative discrepancy between base and few-step marginals across the trajectory, improving on Shortcut-style cumulative objectives.
2610.34575.why: One-step generation theory directly in the reader's generative-modeling interests.

2610.34052.tldr: EISep RNN implements Dale's principle via learnable excitatory-inhibitory separation, improving stability and modularity.
2610.34052.summary: Dale-constrained ANNs often train poorly. EISep learns E/I separation and shows stable training and competitive performance on multi-task, continual and RL settings.

2610.34045.tldr: Proves the minimax regret rate for Sobolev-RKHS kernel RL with continuous states/actions and gives a matching algorithm SOVI.
2610.34045.summary: Characterizes regret Θ(T^max(e_A,e_B)) with exponents capturing action selection and cross-state learning difficulty; SOVI attains the rate.
2610.34045.why: Rigorous RL theory but far from practical robot learning.

2610.34527.tldr: LLM4Robot-Bench evaluates GPT-6 Astra zero-shot on 16 paired sim-real contact-rich tasks across three difficulty levels.
2610.34527.summary: Real success falls from 80.0% (contact selection) to 47.6% (force regulation) to 0% (contact reconfiguration); sim and real results closely match. Failures stem from spatial reasoning, contact selection and force regulation.
2610.34527.why: Shows frontier LLMs fail at contact-rich manipulation; mild relevance.

2610.34280.tldr: AdaPolicy instills foresight in chunked policies by a training-only cascaded head that predicts the next action chunk.
2610.34280.summary: Anticipatory policies usually need future-observation supervision. AdaPolicy's online head outputs the current chunk and an evolved latent; an unrolled head predicts the next chunk and backprops through the latent, adding no inference cost.
2610.34280.why: Directly about action chunking and what makes chunked policies work.

2610.34609.tldr: Audio-R1 RL-post-trains audio-language models using self-supervised tasks as verifiable rewards.
2610.34609.summary: Uses self-supervised audio tasks' automatic answers as rewards, improving reasoning across audio benchmarks beyond SFT.

2610.34137.tldr: SEPO uses label-guided self-teacher distillation to improve LLM reasoning exploration beyond RLVR.
2610.34137.summary: Elicits correct reasoning from the policy conditioned on labels and distills it back on-policy, iterating to escape exploration bottlenecks.

2610.34121.tldr: BE-CTDE adds a blockchain token economy and anomaly detection to multi-agent RL training in IoT settings.
2610.34121.summary: Uses behavioral verification and slashing to weight agents' policy-update contributions, with incentive and exclusion-time bounds.

2610.34538.tldr: Dual Gradient Consensus adapts online residual learning step sizes to reject transient out-of-distribution disturbances in quadrotor control.
2610.34538.summary: Compares residual gradients against long/short-term memories to suppress unreliable updates; achieves lowest RMSE in four simulated disturbance cases.

2610.34147.tldr: PS-DLO conditions a manipulation policy on inferred cable properties and SAM3-distilled future mask features for deformable linear objects.
2610.34147.summary: DLOs are hard to localize and property-dependent. PS-DLO uses contrastive image-text property descriptions and distills future mask features into the action expert; 68.9% average success over nine real single-arm and bimanual tasks, +20 points over the best baseline.
2610.34147.why: Real-robot deformable manipulation with a policy-learning angle; moderate relevance.

2610.35462.tldr: DEX-PHD is an untethered handheld device with a dexterous hand, per-finger control, and tactile/proprioceptive/video logging for data collection.
2610.35462.summary: Teleoperation gives accurate robot state while vision-based methods are portable; DEX-PHD combines both by having the operator directly drive a dexterous hand via joint mapping while logging proprioception, fingertip contact and wrist video. Demonstrations replay open-loop on a humanoid for contact-rich multi-finger tasks.
2610.35462.why: A UMI-style data collection tool for multi-fingered hands, directly in the reader's area.

2610.35862.tldr: FLORE learns force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation with a diffusion policy outputting actions and per-hand force commands from force-sensing UMI data.
2610.35862.summary: Many tasks need force control coordinated across body and hands. FLORE collects robot-free demos with force-sensing UMI grippers and body trackers, trains a diffusion policy on vision, proprioception and wrenches to predict actions plus force commands, executed by a hybrid compliance whole-body controller with integral force tracking.
2610.35862.why: Contact-rich diffusion policy with explicit force prediction; strong real-robot recipe transferable to manipulation.

2610.35010.tldr: JevVLA learns a differentiable energy over actions on top of a frozen VLA to rerank discrete candidates and refine continuous action chunks.
2610.35010.summary: Adapting VLAs while retaining pretrained skill is hard. JevVLA trains a scalar energy conditioned on observation, task and action from execution feedback, corrections or preferences; its values rank candidates and its action gradients refine chunks.
2610.35010.why: Energy-based steering of frozen generative policies relates to steering and RL fine-tuning of VLAs.

2610.36378.tldr: Data-Driven Hamiltonian replaces analytic dynamics in Hamilton-Jacobi optimal control with a data-driven bound requiring only a Lipschitz constant.
2610.36378.summary: RL is sample inefficient; DDH evaluates the Hamiltonian from data with principled uncertainty handling in unvisited regions, and incorporates extra priors when available, scaling to higher dimensions with neural solvers.

2610.35852.tldr: DiffContact provides smooth analytic contact gradients via central-path relaxation of the friction SOCP, used for policy learning and contact-implicit trajectory optimization.
2610.35852.summary: Exact contact sensitivities give no information about neighboring contact modes. DiffContact replaces only the backward-pass sensitivity with a relaxed one evaluated on the central path via Newton iteration, keeping hard-contact forward rollouts feasible; demonstrated on legged locomotion.
2610.35852.why: Contact-implicit optimization and differentiable contact are relevant to contact-rich manipulation control.

2610.35594.tldr: Self Flow Forcing adds a predictive representation loss to DMD to preserve structure and temporal coherence in few-step video distillation.
2610.35594.summary: DMD supervises only outputs, which degrades with very few steps. SF² adds a self-supervised internal representation objective without changing the output loss, improving spatial detail and dynamics.
2610.35594.why: Few-step video generation; moderately relevant to video interests.

2610.34717.tldr: VLA-HWBench profiles 18 open VLAs on Jetson Thor and AMD edge hardware with a seven-stage latency breakdown.
2610.34717.summary: Finds action-generation strategy matters more than model size, dominating 14 of 19 Jetson configurations, with latency varying 82x on Jetson and 157x on AMD.
2610.34717.why: Useful data on real-time VLA inference costs, including diffusion vs autoregressive heads.

2610.35636.tldr: OpTTA adapts latent world models at test time with an optimistic, reward-biased objective rather than pure prediction loss.
2610.35636.summary: Prediction-only TTA fits only the outcomes of the planner's own actions and can stay wrong about goal-reaching actions. Inspired by reward-biased MLE, OpTTA adds an optimism term, improving planning under distribution shift.
2610.35636.why: World-model adaptation for planning; secondary interest.

2610.34650.tldr: Dream2Assist extends an RSSM world model with intent inference for shared vehicle control trained via fictitious co-play.
2610.34650.summary: Assistive agents must anticipate human goals without overriding them. The world model infers discrete intents and trains an assistive policy, with a deployment pipeline addressing sim-to-real-human gaps.

2610.35491.tldr: S²-RL uses sample- and set-level RL on a text-to-image diffusion model to distill semantic segmentation datasets.
2610.35491.summary: Formulates segmentation dataset distillation as diffusion generation optimized with dual RL rewards for informative, novel scenes.

2610.35626.tldr: Uses robot-aligned 3D Gaussian Splatting to render wrist-camera data for adapting VLAs to precise reaching in e-waste disassembly.
2610.35626.summary: Reconstructs the workspace with 3DGS and renders diverse wrist views paired with structured reaching trajectories for VLA fine-tuning.
2610.35626.why: Synthetic data via 3DGS for reaching; modest relevance.

2610.36419.tldr: SpeeDiff jointly trains a VAE and latent diffusion model end-to-end, using a Tweedie pixel reconstruction loss to prevent latent collapse.
2610.36419.summary: Naive end-to-end latent diffusion collapses the latent space. A Tweedie Pixel Reconstruction loss decodes the predicted clean latent from noisy states to give pixel-level feedback, enabling stable joint training and faster convergence.
2610.36419.why: Generative-modeling method of general interest; not policy-specific.

2610.35813.tldr: A world-model RL framework optimizes beamforming and metasurface weights for energy efficiency in wireless networks.
2610.35813.summary: Learns latent channel dynamics to plan digital beamforming and DMA weights under constraints, more sample-efficiently than model-free RL.

2610.35563.tldr: An 864-node tactile glove recording 14,000+ badminton strokes reveals hand-force control mechanisms that distinguish expertise.
2610.35563.summary: A two-layer mechanics-grounded framework infers object-driving and grip-stabilizing control from tactile history; higher skill shows selective control, anticipatory regulation and focal distal modulation.
2610.35563.why: High-resolution tactile human data and analysis of hand control; inspirational for dexterity.

2610.35832.tldr: Profiles GPT-6 Astra on EBench as a robot agent, both via direct waypoint control and invoking VLA/WAM policies.
2610.35832.summary: Under direct control the agent is competitive with post-trained policies, leading short-horizon tasks; combining it with policies via a harness is analyzed across manipulation demands.
2610.35832.why: Useful snapshot of frontier-model robot control vs VLAs.

2610.35103.tldr: Position paper arguing semantic failure analysis is a prerequisite for dexterous deformable-object manipulation.
2610.35103.summary: Catalogs deformable failure modes (buckling, plastic deformation, tearing) and supports the claim with proof-of-concept experiments.

2610.35656.tldr: Proposes a sample-efficient asynchronous Q-learning algorithm for TV-robust MDPs with Markovian data and sample complexity bounds.
2610.35656.summary: Gives a model-free robust RL method with provable efficiency for distributionally robust MDPs.

2610.35817.tldr: ZAP teaches small open VLMs motion control purely in simulation on primitive tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra on real robot tasks.
2610.35817.summary: Argues agentic robot control decomposes into semantic reasoning (which small VLMs have) and motion control (which they lack). ZAP trains motion skills in sim from the model's own successes with no real data; 96.7% real success, matching GPT-6 Astra at 3x speed and 17x lower cost, and 74.0% on bimanual RoboLab-120.
2610.35817.why: Interesting decomposition and zero-real-data recipe for VLM-based control.

2610.36374.tldr: HIDRA uses hierarchical dual-routing attention and geometric key regularization for replay-free lifelong imitation learning.
2610.36374.summary: Sequential updates distort expert routing; HIDRA decouples instruction-level retrieval from context refinement and regularizes keys for alignment/separation.

2610.35342.tldr: Visual geometric servoing with MPC-corrected adaptive PID for UAV tracking of vibrating pipes.
2610.35342.summary: Uses YOLOv5 label detection and an MPC-RCAPID controller for dynamic pipe tracking.

2610.35756.tldr: VidEdit3D edits 3D Gaussian scenes by recasting camera trajectories as videos edited with video diffusion.
2610.35756.summary: Uses trajectory-guided rendering and video diffusion priors for consistent structural 3D edits.

2610.36285.tldr: ASPEN predicts when a navigation VLA would repeat its command to skip reasoning calls.
2610.36285.summary: Reduces NaVILA calls 9.5% and inference time 8.1% with comparable performance.

2610.34674.tldr: OSMA-Bench tests whether navigation policies adapt clearance and speed to obstacle semantics.
2610.34674.summary: Finds VLM and VLA policies distinguish obstacles but fail to translate it into motion adaptation.

2610.34649.tldr: RobotAgentBench evaluates open-world robot agents across 50 real-to-sim household layouts and multi-level tasks.
2610.34649.summary: Constructs layouts via a human-in-the-loop real-to-sim pipeline with 90 atomic and longer tasks to test discovery, reasoning, execution and recovery.
2610.34649.why: Benchmark for robot agents; low relevance.

2610.36247.tldr: Shows offline-to-online fine-tuning of flow policies without retained data improves by freezing the BC prior instead of continuing behavior cloning.
2610.36247.summary: Without offline data, continued BC refits the behavior model to scarce nonstationary online data, an actor-side failure. Freezing the pretrained expressive prior substantially improves IFQL, FQL and action-chunked QC across seven OGBench domains.
2610.36247.why: Clear insight on RL fine-tuning of expressive (flow, chunked) policies, a core interest.

2610.35518.tldr: S3AC provides a stable critic-training recipe and difficulty-aware sampling for actor-critic RL on long-CoT LLM reasoning.
2610.35518.summary: Trains a critic for token-level advantages and prompt baselines, used for difficulty-aware prompt sampling.

2610.36068.tldr: Rollback rewinds action-conditioned world models to critical decision points, branches alternative actions, and distills counterfactual outcomes into policy supervision.
2610.36068.summary: World models are usually used forward-only. Rollback exploits their rewindability to attribute success to individual decisions, yielding action-level supervision without a learned value model, with a scalable distributed training system.
2610.36068.why: Interesting use of video world models for policy improvement.

2610.35494.tldr: Combines critic-layer transfer and staged reward redesign with TQC for obstacle-aware manipulation in PyBullet.
2610.35494.summary: Gains of 6-11 points on obstacle Push and Slide tasks with three seeds.

2610.34893.tldr: MMGNet injects multi-scale image features into 3D representations and models rotational graspness for cluttered 6-DoF grasping.
2610.34893.summary: Combines RGB and point clouds hierarchically with grasp-shaded grouping for better grasp synthesis.

2610.34789.tldr: ISB-NMPC couples spherical-bearing prediction with nonlinear quadrotor MPC for camera-based drone interception.
2610.34789.summary: Achieves 86.7% interception success in 30 simulated trials.

2610.36539.tldr: CARD retargets human hand demonstrations from video, mocap, or tactile gloves to robot actions while preserving explicit contact-force targets.
2610.36539.summary: Kinematic retargeting ignores contact dynamics crucial for dexterous success. CARD unifies human data sources via a shared hand-contact representation, outputs contact force targets alongside kinematics without simulator or object models, and uses a tactile tracking controller to maintain contacts during open-loop hardware replay.
2610.36539.why: Contact-aware retargeting of human data to dexterous hands is squarely the reader's core interest.

2610.37652.tldr: A sim-only recipe trains LEAP hand policies for long sequences of in-hand object pose reaching at any wrist orientation, with learned safety filters, transferring zero-shot.
2610.37652.summary: In-hand skills are usually limited to rotation and drops are rarely measured. The recipe combines diverse resets and goals from generated grasp datasets, an adaptive friction curriculum, and careful system identification, plus learned safety filters to avoid drops; policies transfer zero-shot to a real LEAP hand.
2610.37652.why: Sim-to-real in-hand reorientation beyond rotation with safety analysis; core dexterity work.

2610.36791.tldr: RynnWorld-Latent is a cross-embodiment video world model conditioned on universal 3D-grounded latent actions, pretrained on 553.5M frames.
2610.36791.summary: Robots have incompatible action spaces and human videos lack labels. Using RynnLAM latent actions as a shared interface, the model pretrains on human, robot and sim video across 23 datasets and post-trains for target robots, supporting data generation routes such as digital teleoperation.
2610.36791.why: Action-conditioned video world models across embodiments, relevant to WM-for-policy interests.

2610.37381.tldr: PDRVLA adds a lightweight physical-dynamics module predicting future RGB, depth, and flow features to condition VLA actions without video generation.
2610.37381.summary: Video world models are too slow for control. PDRVLA's module extracts physical tokens supervised by future feature prediction and a frozen video world model, trained on public data with human-to-robot synthesis and ECoT; reaches 99.3% on LIBERO among four sim benchmarks.

2610.37378.tldr: VLA-Stem is an RL safety layer that converts VLA action chunks into motion references and adjusts them to avoid dynamic obstacles.
2610.37378.summary: Without fine-tuning the VLA, an RL policy uses chunk-derived references, proprioception and obstacle info to preserve spatial intent while adapting motion and timing.
2610.37378.why: RL residual on top of VLA chunks; modest relevance.

2610.37799.tldr: DexSuite is a Genesis-based framework with 30 tasks, 100+ arm-hand combinations, teleoperation, simulated tactile sensing, and a 4,700-episode dataset.
2610.37799.summary: Few sim frameworks cover the full dexterous workflow. DexSuite assembles 10 arms and 12 end-effectors, standard APIs, a 16-pair benchmark across contact complexities, and demonstrations from teleop, scripts and policies.
2610.37799.why: Potentially useful infrastructure for dexterous policy research.

2610.36823.tldr: TAPESTRY repurposes a pretrained video diffusion transformer as a policy by tokenizing actions as single video patches in the shared backbone.
2610.36823.summary: Using video models for control usually requires test-time video generation or from-scratch action heads. TAPESTRY linearly projects each action timestep into the VAE patch space so the same patchify layers and transformer process actions, trained with three diffusion objectives and no video generation at inference.
2610.36823.why: Elegant unified video-action model design, a stated interest.

2610.37983.tldr: Combines autoregressive generation with hierarchical long-context denoising and warp-and-inpaint camera control for long camera-controlled video.
2610.37983.summary: AR video drifts and camera control is ambiguous. WanAR+FixAR reformulates generation as warping and inpainting for geometry consistency and adds hierarchical denoising to reduce drift.
2610.37983.why: AR video diffusion technique; moderate relevance.

2610.37666.tldr: ThinkWorld grounds VLA reasoning in discrete chain-of-dynamics motion tokens and refines it with RL in world-model imagination.
2610.37666.summary: Human videos lack action grounding. ThinkWorld represents action thoughts as motion-token sequences shared across embodiments, initialized from labeled demos, extended to human video, and reinforced via RL with world imagination.
2610.37666.why: Combines human video, world models and RL for VLAs; moderately relevant.

2610.37215.tldr: R2A retrieves future motion primitives from a graph of training demos via a GNN to make VLAs robust to visual OOD shifts.
2610.37215.summary: Structures successful demos into a spatiotemporal primitive graph and uses retrieved geometric priors at test time to bypass corrupted visual features.
2610.37215.why: Test-time retrieval for VLA robustness; tangential.

2610.37865.tldr: Echo scales visual off-policy RL by having a state-based auxiliary policy imitate the visual policy and collect cheap unrendered experience for a shared critic.
2610.37865.summary: Visual RL in GPU sim is rendering-bound and teacher-student distillation has an imitation gap. Echo uses inverse distillation to gather unrendered experience for off-policy value learning with FastTD3, tested on visual control and two dexterous tasks in Genesis.
2610.37865.why: Practical trick for scaling visual RL including dexterous tasks; preliminary.

2610.37582.tldr: EgoThumb is an open-source tendon-driven supernumerary robotic thumb controlled by a visual imitation policy from a palm camera.
2610.37582.summary: Maps egocentric palm-camera images to continuous joint positions to infer intent for hold-and-manipulate assistance, with forearm-relocated actuation.
2610.37582.why: Wearable assistive hardware; tangential to dexterous policy learning.

2610.37509.tldr: Ego-CEVR learns hierarchical visual representations: global context from future video prediction on egocentric data and interaction features from robot action supervision.
2610.37509.summary: Global and wrist interaction modules get distinct objectives, enabling pretraining on large-scale human and robot egocentric video and alignment with real-robot demos.
2610.37509.why: Learning from egocentric human video for manipulation representations.

2610.37330.tldr: AFIL uses online failure rollouts from a pretrained VLA as negative guidance via dual success/failure action generators for diffusion and flow policies.
2610.37330.summary: Success-only BC leaves VLAs brittle to compounding errors. AFIL generates failures online, jointly trains success and failure action generators on a shared backbone, and uses the failure generator as negative guidance during sampling (title in metadata refers to motion tokens; abstract describes AFIL).
2610.37330.why: Guidance-based use of failure data for diffusion/flow policies ties to CFG and policy improvement interests.

2610.36859.tldr: ActiveAlign uses active hand waving for hand-eye calibration via differentiable rendering and tactile touching for millimeter object alignment in Real2Sim2Real.
2610.36859.summary: Passive perception leaves real2sim gaps. ActiveAlign-Waving calibrates cameras from hand motion, and ActiveAlign-Touching refines object poses via touch to reach millimeter precision.
2610.36859.why: Useful for building accurate sim for dexterous manipulation.

2610.37897.tldr: PPO-based joint trajectory and resource allocation for secure energy-harvesting UAV networks.
2610.37897.summary: Optimizes secrecy rate, energy and interference with switching roles.

2610.37219.tldr: JAM decouples backbone initialization, foresight objective, and inference machinery to unify VLAs and world-action models, with a discarded latent foresight head.
2610.37219.summary: The VLA vs WAM debate bundles three choices. JAM uses a pretrained visual backbone plus action expert, trained with an action loss and a foresight loss predicting frozen encodings of future frames via a head removed after training, enabling controlled comparisons.
2610.37219.why: Clarifying analysis of what actually matters in VLA vs video-model policies.

2610.37170.tldr: Real-robot comparison of ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA and pi0.5 across 12-200 demonstrations on a low-cost SO-101 arm with 1,340 episodes.
2610.37170.summary: pi0.5 led with scarce data (16/40 at 12 demos) and plateaued near 70%; ACT rose to 37/40 at 100 demos; Diffusion Policy and SmolVLA peaked near 50%, partly due to failure-to-start.
2610.37170.why: Careful small-scale data-scaling study of common IL policies.

2610.36662.tldr: SWIM learns state-feature weights via an inverse-dynamics model to supervise JEPA world models with task-relevant state for planning.
2610.36662.summary: Uniform state supervision overcounts redundant features. SWIM learns weights by predicting recorded actions, improving JEPA latent planning.
2610.36662.why: V-JEPA-style world models for planning; moderately relevant.

2610.37091.tldr: GAWM is a sub-100M world-action model predicting future frozen DINOv3 tokens and decoding action chunks for multi-task manipulation.
2610.37091.summary: Compresses camera views into tokens, forecasts them at two horizons supervised by dense future patch features, and regresses action chunks from current and predicted tokens.

2610.36789.tldr: Torch-Hand is a 21-DoF linkage-driven humanoid hand replicating human joint structure with a 5-DoF thumb.
2610.36789.summary: Avoids tendon-driven actuation trade-offs using linkages for robustness, load and control simplicity while retaining anthropomorphic kinematics.

2610.37391.tldr: JEPA-inspired latent field world model for sparse-pilot MIMO-OFDM channel reconstruction.
2610.37391.summary: Predicts in a latent propagation-field domain for robust CSI reconstruction.

2610.38034.tldr: Extends PPO with an action-conditioned critic that compares executed actions to sampled alternatives to escape local minima in contact-rich tasks.
2610.38034.summary: State-value critics give no action discrimination once outcomes converge, stalling PPO. Adding an action-conditioned value critic combined with GAE provides relative action credit, helping long-horizon contact-rich manipulation from scratch.
2610.38034.why: Clear diagnosis of a PPO failure mode for manipulation RL.

2610.38000.tldr: Self-Labeled Preference Transfer jointly trains preference-conditioned action prediction and recognition to transfer steerability to unannotated tasks.
2610.38000.summary: Fine-tuning on unannotated target demos weakens preference control; SPT self-labels preferences to keep steerability while improving success.

2610.37175.tldr: MLE-World predicts ML experiment outputs from code to enable test-time scaling for research agents.
2610.37175.summary: A finetuned Qwen3.5-4B predicts logs and scores with confidence, guiding five TTS policies.

2610.36925.tldr: Dwell reframes a VLM as a recurrent latent transition operator serving as both world model and policy for model-based RL.
2610.36925.summary: The VLM predicts and acts in latent space, continually improving from experience efficiently.

2610.37801.tldr: Empirical study of wrist-target construction effects on joint-limit hits in humanoid arm retargeting.
2610.37801.summary: Reach-normalized targets avoid joint bounds more often than reconstructed ones on a Unitree H1-2.

2610.37566.tldr: ReferStream injects new subjects into streaming video generation via in-context reference latents and transient cache injection.
2610.37566.summary: Training-free joint latent construction and cache restoration integrate references without disrupting context.

2610.37917.tldr: Paired evaluation of inference and data strategies for a fine-tuned pi0.5 across all 100 BEHAVIOR-1K tasks.
2610.37917.summary: Using the 2025 BEHAVIOR Challenge winner (Q-score 0.39), finds previously proposed strategies do not transfer uniformly.
2610.37917.why: Practical evidence on VLA inference tricks.

2610.36535.tldr: MyoAcross builds individualized musculoskeletal models and a morphology-conditioned generalist RL policy for full-body muscle control.
2610.36535.summary: Achieves 99.24% completion on 31 held-out individuals vs 8.32% for a template-trained baseline.

2610.38508.tldr: SaiVLA-JEPA tests whether V-JEPA features and auxiliary future-latent prediction improve a flow-matching VLA on LIBERO-Plus.
2610.38508.summary: Compares no JEPA features, current JEPA conditioning, and added future supervision over 10,030 paired LIBERO-Plus episodes. Current V-JEPA conditioning raises success from 71.6% to about 82.5%, while the abstract suggests future supervision adds less.
2610.38508.why: Controlled evidence on V-JEPA features for flow policies, a stated interest.

2610.39054.tldr: Data Inoculation perturbs human teleoperation with a learned residual policy during collection to gather higher-coverage, recovery-rich demonstrations.
2610.39054.summary: Demo coverage determines robustness, but collection relies on heuristics, DAgger needs chance failures, and RL is unsafe. In Data Inoculation, a residual policy perturbs the operator's commands in shared control so humans demonstrate recoveries from useful off-nominal states.
2610.39054.why: Principled data-collection method from the Levine group, directly useful for imitation learning practice.

2610.38199.tldr: Trains 14 VLA variants on 1,616 underwater manipulation episodes and evaluates 1,260 pool rollouts, reaching 93.3% success.
2610.38199.summary: Studies proprioception configurations for generalist VLAs under marine domain shift, plus ACT comparisons.

2610.38731.tldr: Uses an RL controller's value function as the implicit cost in an MPPI planner for off-road navigation.
2610.38731.summary: Bidirectional hierarchy lets the low-level RL value guide high-level MPPI trajectory selection instead of explicit cost maps.
2610.38731.why: MPPI+RL value combination is generally interesting but applied to off-road driving.

2610.39044.tldr: Catch It All trains sim-to-real humanoid dexterous-hand catching of unseen objects from one egocentric camera, deployed zero-shot on a Unitree G1.
2610.39044.summary: Catching needs generalization to novel projectiles and real-time contact adaptation. Careful grasp rewards and safety-aware curricula enable high-frequency actions near hardware limits (wrist torque as low as 5 Nm); policies handle varied geometry, deformability and elasticity for under- and overhand catches.
2610.39044.why: Dynamic dexterous-hand sim-to-real with strong real results.

2611.09964.tldr: Measures demo- and step-efficiency of fine-tuning six VLAs (pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1-N1.7) on LIBERO suites.
2611.09964.summary: Models within two points at full data differ up to 3x with 50 demos; pi0.5 needs 2-5x fewer demos than pi0 and is most sample-efficient at every budget, especially on long-horizon tasks.
2611.09964.why: Practical guidance on choosing VLAs for low-data fine-tuning.

2610.38238.tldr: StBR regularizes offline RL by matching induced state-consequence distributions via a closed-form latent divergence instead of action distributions.
2610.38238.summary: Small action deviations can cause large transition changes; StBR constrains consequences through a structured latent space, avoiding the need for a true dynamics model.
2610.38238.why: Offline RL regularization idea; secondary interest.

2610.38661.tldr: QbD-VLA allocates mixed-precision bit widths across VLA components using short closed-loop task-success evaluations.
2610.38661.summary: Accounts for component interactions to quantize four VLAs on LIBERO at low average precision with strong performance.

2610.38657.tldr: TERRA adapts a simulation-trained world model for rovers using reward-weighted loss and loss-predictor-guided exploration in MPC.
2610.38657.summary: Reaches about 90% slope-climbing success within five trials under severe sim-to-real gaps.

2610.38253.tldr: Causally adjusted transportability framework for offline RL across domains with unmeasured confounding.
2610.38253.summary: Combines transportability with IVs, negative controls and proxies for identification and minimax estimation.
2610.38253.why: Causal offline RL theory; not relevant.

2610.38234.tldr: SimRetract achieves zero-shot sim-to-real retractor take-over from a surgeon using only simulated demonstrations.
2610.38234.summary: Uses masked instrument images, recovery demos and margin for drift; grasps the retractor in 90% of 50 trials and preserves retraction in 78%.
2610.38234.why: Medical robotics; low relevance despite nice sim-to-real IL.

2610.38496.tldr: SRLBC uses timescale-separated embeddings to behavior-clone nonlinear MPC for nuclear reactor load-following.
2610.38496.summary: Separated slow/fast/exogenous embeddings beat shared embeddings across 500 rollouts and 20 seeds.

2610.38391.tldr: SCOPE distills hindsight skills only at selected error steps for LLM agent RL.
2610.38391.summary: Improves ALFWorld and WebShop across backbones.

2610.38221.tldr: CuraEval shows popular demonstration-curation scores often reduce to trivial statistics like episode length on mixed-skill robomimic data.
2610.38221.summary: Compares curation methods against size-matched random subsets and full data with Diffusion Policy and BC-RNN; the PSD score ranks nearly identically to episode length (rho=0.999), and simply selecting the shortest 50% helps.
2610.38221.why: Rigorous sanity check on data curation for diffusion policies.

2610.38273.tldr: NAGO designs the source measure for flow matching in function space to control spectral stiffness when sampling SPDE invariant measures.
2610.38273.summary: Gives admissibility conditions for infinite-dimensional flows and shows source-target covariance ratio controls velocity stiffness, yielding a spectral-matching source rule that improves few-step accuracy.
2610.38273.why: Source-distribution design for flows is a neat theory point, though applied to SPDEs.

2610.38289.tldr: PulmoWorld is an asynchronous multimodal medical world model for longitudinal pneumonia forecasting and constrained planning.
2610.38289.summary: Combines history-aware filtering, recursive forecasting and risk-budgeted MBRL.

2610.38513.tldr: Constraint-aware object-centric RL with a particle-filter belief infers hook extraction directions from contact forces, transferring zero-shot.
2610.38513.summary: Trained in simplified peg-in-hole sim and deployed on real hooks with unseen multi-stage constraints.
2610.38513.why: Force-based contact-rich RL with sim-to-real; moderate relevance.

2610.39049.tldr: Fast Rust simulator and two-policy multi-agent PPO for the deckbuilder Balatro.
2610.39049.summary: Decomposes play into blind and shop policies with action masking and credit routing.

2610.38823.tldr: Coupled predictive model improves FCS-MPC for LC-filtered three-level inverters.
2610.38823.summary: Retains LC coupling without enlarging the candidate search.

2610.38153.tldr: StepControl generates long-horizon human motion with an autoregressive diffusion model conditioned only on foot-contact schedules.
2610.38153.summary: Injects contact events via cross-attention with CFG and uses a stochastic mixture noise schedule for stable AR generation.
2610.38153.why: AR diffusion with contact conditioning; tangential.

2610.38569.tldr: Multi-layer navigation system for smart wheelchairs with limited input interfaces.
2610.38569.summary: Uses virtual-sensor potential fields to contextualize faulty user commands.

2610.38248.tldr: MATCH jointly learns a planner and executor with hierarchical RL for continuous vision-and-language navigation.
2610.38248.summary: Execution-aware topological graph and dense macro rewards.

2610.38388.tldr: ELEVATE uses a coding agent to formulate RL problems for missing quadrupedal manipulation controllers upon task failure.
2610.38388.summary: Autonomously acquires wall-supported elevation and related controllers across seven sim tasks.

2610.38648.tldr: LOGSI derives exact and approximate logical composition (negation, XOR, conjunction) of velocity fields for stochastic interpolants with score re-equilibration.
2610.38648.summary: Shows negation and XOR compose exactly for any interpolant but conjunction incurs drift-interaction error on non-Gaussian paths; LOGSI alternates transport with score re-equilibration steps to sample logical targets.
2610.38648.why: Guidance/composition theory for flows and interpolants, a core generative-modeling interest.

2610.38439.tldr: World Reward Models select ML agent candidates directly instead of predicting execution outcomes.
2610.38439.summary: Proves direct selectors dominate outcome-predicting selectors.

2610.38241.tldr: MEV is a multi-event video dataset with temporally grounded annotations for long-take generation.
2610.38241.summary: Provides event-segmented real videos for localized conditioning.

2610.38095.tldr: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Super (120B MoE hybrid Mamba-Transformer) and Lightning (30B) for agentic AI.
2610.38095.summary: Describes distillation, long-context training, speculative decoding and multi-teacher on-policy distillation.

2610.38104.tldr: Shows action-space labels (position vs velocity) under-specify the executed interface; scaling and filtering choices swing success dramatically on contact-rich Factory tasks.
2610.38104.summary: With ten policies per condition on PegInsert, GearMesh and NutThread, changing only physical action scale shifts median success by 0.645-1.000, and removing EMA filtering also matters.
2610.38104.why: Rigorous reminder that low-level action interface details dominate contact-rich policy results.

2610.38566.tldr: CoCA co-evolves rubrics and LLM policy for rubric-based RL.
2610.38566.summary: Adapts rubric difficulty to policy capability.

2610.38980.tldr: Builds a benchmark and agent harness for context retrieval/compaction in interactive world models.
2610.38980.summary: Treats revisit inconsistency as context retrieval and adds harness-level compaction.

2610.40349.tldr: TouchBridge co-designs wearable and robot tactile interfaces and Tac-Retarget to convert human dexterous demonstrations into robot data by aligning fingertip contact patches.
2610.40349.summary: Sensing and morphology gaps hamper human-to-robot dexterous transfer. Matched visual and fingertip-tactile interfaces on human and robot establish correspondence, and Tac-Retarget uses measured contact to align fingertip patches and their spatial relations, requiring no object mesh, pose estimate or simulation.
2610.40349.why: Tactile-conditioned retargeting of human data for dexterous hands is a core interest.

2610.39582.tldr: Three-stage retargeting aligns kinematics, contact geometry, and object-centric contact wrench space so robot fingertip forces cover the human's wrench support.
2610.39582.summary: Kinematic retargeting drops tactile information. The method aligns hand kinematics and contacts, builds a human wrench support profile from tactile forces, optimizes robot fingertip force targets to cover it, and converts them into joint corrections for directly replayable trajectories.
2610.39582.why: Physically grounded tactile retargeting for dexterous hands, closely matching core interests.

2610.40002.tldr: CoC-CFG applies per-step classifier-free guidance on a reasoning VLA's chain-of-thought and learns step weights via measured action values.
2610.40002.summary: Reasoning traces can mislead action decoding. CFG between contexts with and without reasoning modulates its influence per Euler step; choosing weights is cast as an MDP whose Q-values are measured exactly by rollouts with fixed noise, and Q-adaptive guidance fits small critics to improve conservatively.
2610.40002.why: Novel mix of CFG and RL-style steering for flow VLAs.

2610.39451.tldr: Represents action chunks with movement primitives so imitation policies output smooth trajectories within and across chunks.
2610.39451.summary: Chunked policies learn temporal structure only implicitly, yielding jerky commands, vibration and velocity saturation on hardware. Encoding each chunk as movement-primitive parameters enforces smoothness and continuity across chunks for any backbone, from diffusion policies to VLAs.
2610.39451.why: Directly addresses action chunking quality, a core interest.

2610.40210.tldr: AcrossDEX pretrains bimanual motion prediction on HOT3D Aria human data and adapts it to Inspire and Allegro hands with sim experts and robot demos.
2610.40210.summary: Combines human motion pretraining predicting one second of bimanual motion, sim expert learning, robot demo collection and visual closed-loop execution; shared wrist representations, separate finger fields and validity masks support different hand embodiments.
2610.40210.why: Cross-embodiment bimanual dexterity from human egocentric data.

2610.40828.tldr: Evaluates 281 imitation policies across seven families in ~1,700 real trials of five-fingered RJ45 insertion, finding representations dominate and validation loss does not predict success.
2610.40828.summary: Validation loss shows no consistent relationship with real success. Controlled ablations show observation and action representations matter more than optimizer or sampling choices; for point-cloud policies, ROI cropping, base-frame representation and encoder normalization each raise success, and offline proxies are assessed.
2610.40828.why: Large-scale real-robot dexterous IL study with actionable design insights.

2610.39076.tldr: Tactus is a thin 3D-knit glove with calibrated capacitive fingertip force sensing and IMU-fused pose tracking for natural dexterous data collection.
2610.39076.summary: No wearable combines calibrated contact force and occlusion-robust hand tracking without disturbing manipulation. Tactus uses a 1.5 mm fingertip stackup, sensors placed via contact studies, and IMU fusion, with a documented calibration procedure.
2610.39076.why: Tactile human-data glove directly relevant to learning from human hand data.

2610.39429.tldr: ScheduleGen generates multi-arm demonstrations from a few sources via integrated planning and scheduling respecting multi-arm constraints.
2610.39429.summary: MimicGen-style generators ignore multi-arm constraints causing unsafe behaviors; ScheduleGen schedules skills to synthesize safe bimanual/humanoid demos, evaluated on 28 tasks.
2610.39429.why: Data generation for bimanual IL from Yuke Zhu's group.

2610.41009.tldr: STAR is a training-free VLA inference trick applying EMA over late-layer residual updates, modulated by proprioception, to preserve visual grounding.
2610.41009.summary: Probing reveals a late-layer grounding gap; STAR mixes earlier object-aware update directions into action representations, with adaptive strength.

2610.39232.tldr: GenSight unifies future video generation and dense 4D perception (depth, embodiment segmentation, flow) in one video DiT.
2610.39232.summary: Jointly optimizes all modalities in a unified velocity space with task modulation, supporting multi-step generation and single-step perception.
2610.39232.why: Embodied video world model with geometry; relevant to WM interests.

2610.40646.tldr: SwapBot provides low-cost tactile adapters that turn household tools into swappable robot end-effectors.
2610.40646.summary: Fixed robot-side coupling with tool-side adapters integrating tactile sensors enables autonomous tool swapping for contact-rich tasks like cooking.

2610.39280.tldr: Learns a single policy that adapts in context to different robot controllers by encoding examples of commanded actions and resulting motions.
2610.39280.summary: Different controllers give actions different meanings. A transformer context encoder summarizes action-motion interactions across six controller types and gain/compliance variations, improving real-world cross-controller transfer (Finn, Sadigh).
2610.39280.why: Addresses a real issue in pooling cross-embodiment data for generalist policies.

2610.41028.tldr: CIMI transfers robot-free human dexterous demonstrations via contact-grounded interfaces and a hierarchical contact-surface planner policy.
2610.41028.summary: Preserving natural dexterity while producing transferable data is hard. CIMI combines shared contact geometry and fingertip RGB views with contact-first retargeting, and a policy where a planner predicts relative contact-surface trajectories and a controller coordinates wrist and fingers, improving final-stage success by at least 50 points.
2610.41028.why: Contact-centric human-to-robot dexterous transfer, squarely core.

2610.40532.tldr: BURGER is a language-conditioned robot drawing benchmark with 28,200 sim demos across 282 tasks to study VLA scaling and multimodality.
2610.40532.summary: Open-ended valid drawings allow analysis of language grounding and multimodal behavior across data scales for five VLAs.
2610.40532.why: Interesting multimodality probe for policies; moderate relevance.

2610.40109.tldr: Shows naive diffusion-style guidance breaks flow matching's coupling distribution and proposes Coupled Guidance derived geometrically for flow models.
2610.40109.summary: Theoretical analysis reveals translated diffusion guidance violates the training coupling, weakening control. Coupled Guidance respects the coupling, giving more stable steering, with applications to stochastic robotic controllers and image synthesis.
2610.40109.why: Guidance theory for flow matching with robotics use, a core interest.

2610.39543.tldr: CoRAct aligns VLA actions with embodied chain-of-thought by reward-guided optimization in action noise space using movement and waypoint consistency signals.
2610.39543.summary: ECoT guidance is implicit. A Mixture-of-Transformers jointly models reasoning, actions and action-conditioned future prediction; candidate actions from sampled noise are scored against reasoning-derived verifiable signals to align actions.
2610.39543.why: Noise-space steering of generative policies, a stated interest.

2610.40373.tldr: HiFOR predicts hierarchical foresight (short-term states, milestones, goals) and retrieves action-relevant future features for VLAs.
2610.40373.summary: Uses a hierarchical dependency mask and action-guided world retrieval to fuse relevant predicted futures into actions.

2610.40026.tldr: RoboSeed scores VLAs and world-action models across capability, training/deployment affordability, research value and reproducibility.
2610.40026.summary: Maps measurements to 0-100 profiles with preference settings for different budgets.

2610.39264.tldr: Online RL with LLM-judge dense rewards trains planner and grounding agents on live iOS apps.
2610.39264.summary: Decoupled planning and UI grounding with step-level rewards.

2610.40356.tldr: JEDI compresses demonstrations into latent slots trained to predict next-stage keyframes in frozen video-JEPA space for many-shot in-context imitation.
2610.40356.summary: Counterfactuals preserve execution details; supports human-hand conditioning via keypoints and improves LIBERO and real-robot demo following.
2610.40356.why: In-context IL with JEPA objectives; moderately relevant.

2610.40257.tldr: Uses a pretrained RL model as terminal cost for short-horizon MPC of autonomous trucks.
2610.40257.summary: Hybrid MPC-RL balances constraints and long-horizon decisions in highway traffic.

2610.39385.tldr: UMI-Live is an open-source bimanual UMI with onboard LiDAR-inertial SLAM and compute for calibration-free in-the-wild data collection.
2610.39385.summary: Integrates sensing, compute and power, with an asynchronous pipeline producing training-ready datasets, validated by fine-tuning pi0.5 and others.

2610.39528.tldr: PRIME W0 is a hierarchical flow-matching VLA with per-layer VLM KV injection, world-model subgoal images, and kinematics-structured noise.
2610.39528.summary: Four-stage training with an MoE action expert and Action Dynamic Manifold flow matching using covariance-structured noise.
2610.39528.why: Structured noise for flow policies is mildly interesting; otherwise complex engineering.

2610.41041.tldr: Studies zero-shot generalization of world models as the bottleneck for continual model-based RL using contextual MDPs.
2610.41041.summary: Evaluates Dyna-Q and TD-MPC reuse in controlled FourRooms settings.

2610.40799.tldr: CaPtain post-trains small open VLMs with SFT and multi-turn RL into code-as-policy robot agents.
2610.40799.summary: Trains inside a harness exposing low-level perception and control APIs, needing no VLA or frontier model.

2610.39267.tldr: Combines conditional flow matching initialization with MPPI over a learned dynamics model for a legged robot towing a wagon.
2610.39267.summary: CFM warm-starts MPPI to speed convergence in confined spaces.
2610.39267.why: Flow-matching + MPPI combination is mildly interesting.

2610.39119.tldr: CAPTURER is an aerial manipulator achieving centimeter-level dynamic grasping via onboard perception and cooperative planning.
2610.39119.summary: Drift correction and coordinated platform-arm planning.

2610.40116.tldr: Dual-agent PPO/TD3 for vehicle scheduling and energy dispatch in electric-hydrogen transport systems.

2610.39825.tldr: AegisFlow casts path-safe guided flow matching as a non-myopic safety-critical optimal control problem, training-free.
2610.39825.summary: Min-norm controllers are myopic; AegisFlow uses global-horizon control to satisfy constraints while optimizing toward targets, applicable to obstacle avoidance.
2610.39825.why: Constrained guidance of flow models; relevant to steering policies.

2610.40726.tldr: Analyzes GRPO vs single-rollout async RL for LLMs and proposes group-relative actor-critic bootstrapping.
2610.40726.summary: Finds GRPO better on reasoning, single-rollout better on agentic tasks.

2610.40754.tldr: DyCraft breaks 4D scene animation into storyboard steps for coding agents.
2610.40754.summary: Plans, builds static scene, keyframes and verifies physics.

2610.41330.tldr: Hourglass factorizes cross-embodiment motion planning into a body-agnostic world model coupled to each robot's differentiable ego-dynamics via camera ego-motion.
2610.41330.summary: On flat ground embodiment affects observations only through ego-motion, so a shared world model plus per-robot differentiable ego-dynamics enables pooling cross-embodiment data for planning in clutter.
2610.41330.why: Clean factorization idea, but for mobile navigation.

2610.42031.tldr: Any Forcing enables any-step and stable one-step autoregressive video generation via a unified adversarial discriminator and adaptive memory selection.
2610.42031.summary: Fixed-step AR video limits flexibility and one-step generation drifts. A discriminator jointly aligns real distribution, inter-step consistency and first-frame quality, while training-free memory selection mitigates long-horizon drift.
2610.42031.why: AR video diffusion with flexible steps; moderately relevant.

2610.42146.tldr: ID-WM is a hierarchical world model where a high-level model samples reachable state transitions and a low-level world model acts as an inverse dynamics solver.
2610.42146.summary: Long-horizon planning suffers from compounding errors and rigid macro-actions. ID-WM decouples state-space reachability from local control, letting the planner choose feasible subgoals while the low level grounds them into precise actions (authors include Zichen Jeff Cui and Nicolas Ballas).
2610.42146.why: World-model planning from the JEPA/Pinto-adjacent line; relevant.

2610.41336.tldr: HandMimicX learns dexterous skills from egocentric RGB-D human videos with an object-centric RL objective plus hand-object interaction constraints for human-like grasps.
2610.41336.summary: Hand-motion imitation transfers poorly across spatial configurations. Formulating RL rewards on object motion decouples the skill from the hand trajectory, while interaction-state constraints keep hand poses natural; single demos generalize spatially in sim and on real robots.
2610.41336.why: Learning dexterous manipulation from human video via RL, a core interest.

2611.00455.tldr: TacMind is a 128-task simulated tactile manipulation benchmark with precise, recognition, and dynamic regimes and 12 perturbations, plus temporal tactile models.
2611.00455.summary: Tactile studies are task-specific and hard to compare. TacMind organizes tasks into three regimes with static/dynamic variants and robustness perturbations, motivating tactile signals as temporally evolving interaction representations.
2611.00455.why: Systematic tactile benchmark directly relevant to visuotactile dexterity.

2611.00394.tldr: CalVLA shapes OpenVLA's native action-token confidence with a margin-ranking loss on success/failure rollouts for failure prediction.
2611.00394.summary: On LIBERO-10, adapted confidence reaches failure-discrimination AUROC 0.739 vs 0.449 before adaptation, though superiority over linear probes is inconclusive.
2611.00394.why: Failure prediction for autoregressive VLAs; modest relevance.

2610.41949.tldr: Geo-FSRL picks the stochastic policy for GRPO on few-step flow models by minimizing conditional KL per velocity update within coefficient-preserving families.
2610.41949.summary: Few-step flow RL needs injected stochasticity, and coefficient-preserving constructions admit many policies with no selection criterion. Geo-FSRL selects the admissible Gaussian transition minimizing induced conditional KL for any velocity update, yielding a principled noise geometry for few-step flow RL.
2610.41949.why: Principled RL fine-tuning of few-step flow models, directly in RL x generative interests.

2610.41609.tldr: Shows VLAs start moving and often complete unspecified tasks even with empty, nonsense, or infeasible instructions on LIBERO-Goal.
2610.41609.summary: With six checkpoints and paired instruction perturbations, robots moved in every empty-instruction episode, and five checkpoints often completed unrequested tasks; studies start-suppression remedies.
2610.41609.why: Exposes language-ignoring behavior in VLAs; useful diagnostic.

2610.41540.tldr: FOCUS combines local optimal-transport alignment with short-horizon differentiable actor-critic learning for imitation from state-only observations.
2610.41540.summary: Matches rollout windows to sampled expert segments with a soft best-of-K OT objective as differentiable reward, plus a critic beyond the horizon, stable on contact-rich DFlex locomotion including a musculoskeletal humanoid.
2610.41540.why: Neat IfO method with differentiable sim; moderate relevance.

2610.41643.tldr: DMAT directly predicts clean bimanual action chunks from stochastic interpolants for single-step inference, anchored by local 3D geometry.
2610.41643.summary: Diffusion/flow policies need iterative inference causing latency. Arguing demonstrated action chunks lie on a structured observation-dependent manifold, DMAT models clean chunks directly (x-prediction-style) enabling one-step inference without trajectory straightening.
2610.41643.why: One-step generative policy via direct clean-action modeling, connected to fast policies and interpolant theory.

2610.41978.tldr: Language-conditioned BC learns six surgeon-requested endoscope guidance behaviors from 235 demos.
2610.41978.summary: Achieves 100% on focus/overview/stop and lower on search, follow and horizon leveling in phantom tests.

2610.41408.tldr: SACQ performs structure- and action-aware ultra-low-bit codebook quantization of VLA weights.
2610.41408.summary: Combines role-specific codebook fitting with action-error-based mixed-bit allocation.

2610.41892.tldr: Learns heterogeneous closed-loop dynamics under a frozen locomotion policy with a contaminated Gaussian model for precise loco-manipulation.
2610.41892.summary: Two Gaussian components separate predictable and unpredictable responses, improving floating-base prediction and end-effector tracking.

2611.00243.tldr: OmniPiano is a piano-playing benchmark with one to five Shadow Hands supporting standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent RL.
2611.00243.summary: Extends prior two-hand piano benchmarks with configurable perturbations, safety constraints and decentralized cooperation in a modular design.

2610.42021.tldr: Nexus-VLA jointly trains on human egocentric and robot data via hierarchical semantic alignment from task intent to fine-grained interaction.
2610.42021.summary: End-to-end human-robot co-training lets human manipulation experience directly shape robot action learning through a shared hierarchical latent space.

2610.41877.tldr: Movens-5M curates 5M physically executable humanoid motions from internet video, and Movens-Zero trains a multimodal flow-matching motion foundation model.
2610.41877.summary: Data pipeline covers clip generation, motion recovery, retargeting and execution verification (10,000+ hours); the model jointly learns across text, video, speech and music with real-time closed-loop execution.
2610.41877.why: Humanoid motion generation; tangential to manipulation.

2610.41275.tldr: TRACE adds an execution-time risk gate to a PPO-tuned VLA person tracker to reduce collisions.
2610.41275.summary: PPO improved tracking but raised collisions; a risk head on 84 cues intervenes selectively.

2610.42135.tldr: Shows DMD's critic must scale with the teacher to avoid collapse and proposes a step-aware critic conditioned on student generation step.
2610.42135.summary: Across seven SiT sizes on ImageNet, growing the teacher with a fixed small critic degrades or collapses students; joint scaling fixes this, and STAC estimates step-specific student scores for better signals.
2610.42135.why: Rigorous analysis of one/few-step distillation, a core generative-modeling interest.

2610.41337.tldr: Bayesian PET reconstruction using a flow-matching prior and latent Langevin posterior sampling.
2610.41337.summary: Improves low-dose reconstruction with uncertainty quantification.

2610.41190.tldr: FlowMoDE uses coarse-to-fine flow matching for efficient detail-aware monocular depth estimation with sim-to-real generalization.
2610.41190.summary: Coarse decoding from semantic features followed by flow-based refinement.

2610.41654.tldr: ∇Mimic makes first-order policy learning with exact differentiable-simulator gradients work for humanoid motion tracking via per-sample gradient clipping and cheap adjoints.
2610.41654.summary: Exact contact gradients have rare unbounded samples and costly adjoints. Median-relative per-sample clipping and efficient adjoint computation enable ultra-efficient humanoid control, outperforming learned-model surrogate gradients.
2610.41654.why: Differentiable-sim policy learning on contact-rich tasks could transfer to manipulation.

2610.41127.tldr: MotorSense is a 100-hour paired egocentric video and bimanual EMG dataset of unscripted manipulation for sensorimotor alignment.
2610.41127.summary: EMG captures finger movement, configuration and forces free of occlusion; cross-modal pretraining learns shared visual-motor action representations.
2610.41127.why: New human hand signal source (EMG) for learning from human manipulation.

2610.41903.tldr: Monograph surveying non-asymptotic statistical foundations of RL.
2610.41903.summary: Reviews finite-sample theory for data-efficient RL drawing on high-dimensional statistics and optimization.

2610.41322.tldr: PIFT transfers peptide-target interaction patterns to small molecules via joint guidance of discrete diffusion and flow matching.
2610.41322.summary: Avoids over-constraining by guiding at sampling time.

2610.41477.tldr: AC-SMPC embeds convexified collision constraints in a differentiable MPC layer tuned by an actor-critic for navigation.
2610.41477.summary: Enables explicit state constraints in learning-based MPC for confined dynamic environments.

2610.41349.tldr: Models interaction-preserving humanoid retargeting KKT conditions as a manifold ODE, giving convergence results for OmniRetarget and a faster TaSP-KKT method.
2610.41349.summary: Connects SQP iterations to backward ODE discretization and derives a tangent-space-parametrized retargeting flow.
2610.41349.why: Retargeting math may inform hand retargeting; moderate.

2611.00293.tldr: Learns particle-graph physical dynamics and injects visible-invisible motion fields into video generation for physical consistency.
2611.00293.summary: Two-stage approach: learned dynamics simulator then motion-field conditioning of video synthesis.

2610.41762.tldr: Scaly is an optimizing compiler generating fast C code for optimal control problems.
2610.41762.summary: Preserves stage structure through differentiation; Hessian evaluation up to 26x faster than CasADi.

2611.00193.tldr: Anchor 1 is a humanoid whole-body controller for precise stable manipulation using calibrated sparse motion references and error feedback.
2611.00193.summary: Offline-curated motion data and decoupled error feedback improve precision; includes a benchmark of coordination demands.

2611.00444.tldr: CLiS accelerates video diffusion attention on TPUs via certified loop-invariant softmax stabilization.
2611.00444.summary: Reduces DiT step latency up to 19.6% on Wan 2.2 and LTX-2.

2611.00405.tldr: Behavior graphs compress robot policy rollouts into interpretable directed graphs of behavior modes linked to outcomes to guide data collection.
2611.00405.summary: Learns similar behavior modes, connects them temporally and links to outcomes; 16 of 18 users preferred graphs over videos for choosing data strategies.
2611.00405.why: Useful tool for data flywheel analysis of deployed policies.

2610.41168.tldr: ROSTrans benchmarks LLMs on ROS1-to-ROS2 code migration.
2610.41168.summary: 108 tasks from 70+ repos assessing interface, behavior and system levels.

2611.00957.tldr: Systematic evaluation of pretrained tactile foundation models as encoders inside Diffusion Policy for contact-rich manipulation, with 5,000+ real rollouts.
2611.00957.summary: Asks how pretrained tactile representations should be used in end-to-end imitation learning. Integrates several tactile foundation models into Diffusion Policy and compares frozen, fine-tuned, and task-specific mid-trained encoders. Evaluated across sim and real tasks with over 5,000 real-world rollouts, yielding empirical guidance on TFM usage.
2611.00957.why: Directly informs whether to plug pretrained tactile encoders into your diffusion policies for contact-rich tasks.

2611.00522.tldr: Steers a frozen OpenVLA-OFT with TinyLoRA adapters of 8-384 parameters via GRPO or CMA-ES to change execution style.
2611.00522.summary: Studies behavioral steering (e.g., carrying objects higher) of a pretrained VLA with minimal trainable capacity. With 256 parameters, carry height rises 120 mm at 92% success on trained tasks and 74 mm on a held-out task; rescaling the update trades style for retention. CMA-ES competes at tiny capacity while GRPO wins as capacity grows.
2611.00522.why: Interesting data point for RL fine-tuning of VLAs with extremely low-dimensional updates.

2611.09973.tldr: KV-cache compression and tree-structured cache management for multi-round autoregressive video diffusion.
2611.09973.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion accumulates large KV caches. ReelCache uses per-layer low-rank decomposition plus video coding of coefficients and shares bases across chunks in a tree supporting rewind/fork. Reduces KV storage 14-21x and speeds next-chunk generation 1.25-3.4x with <1% VBench drop.
2611.09973.why: Systems work for AR video generation; tangential unless deploying video world models.

2611.00937.tldr: Shows sink/old context helps denoising but hurts KV committing in AR video; proposes training-free Commit Forcing chaining.
2611.00937.summary: Analyzes how historical context is read in autoregressive long video generation, separating denoising from KV committing. Finds older context helps denoising but degrades later blocks when used during committing. Commit Forcing, where committing reads only the previous block's KV, improves 60s VBench on all 6 generators and wins 82.9% human preference on 120s videos.
2611.00937.why: Useful insight for long-horizon AR video/world models, related to diffusion forcing interests.

2611.00612.tldr: Roz: a cheap latent-distance benchmark testing whether world model latents encode physical properties like mass and friction.
2611.00612.summary: Argues latent world models succeed on image-similarity tasks but fail to encode physical properties. Roz defines 10 contrastive and 3 continuous tasks (1734 scenarios) requiring only latents and a distance function. Finds physics encoding improves with training but does not track reconstruction MSE.
2611.00612.why: Relevant if you evaluate V-JEPA-style world models for manipulation; benchmark rather than method.

2611.01011.tldr: Decouples a low-rate cached VLM from a high-rate flow-matching action expert conditioned on cache age, plus autograd-free real-time chunking.
2611.01011.summary: VLAs re-encode observations at every step despite semantics changing slowly. Leap-VLA runs the VLM at ~1 Hz with cached context and a fast flow-matching expert with a compact visual encoder, conditioned on cache age via AdaLN and trained with age-ramped corruption. On LIBERO, holds 95.2% at 1 s refresh vs 96.3% matched; a forward-only soft-nudge RTC variant reaches 97.1%.
2611.01011.why: Touches fast VLA inference and real-time chunking, both on your list; LIBERO-only though.

2611.00810.tldr: Joint camera and object motion control for image-to-video diffusion via 3D-grounded structured input noise and LoRA.
2611.00810.summary: UniCaMo constructs motion-consistent input noise from reference image, sparse 3D object trajectories, and camera paths, using spherical Gaussian noise for disoccluded regions. Requires no architectural changes, only lightweight LoRA. Reports SOTA motion controllability on standard benchmarks.

2611.01215.tldr: JADE lets the VLM read noisy action latents and jointly denoise with the action expert in pi0.5-style VLAs.
2611.01215.summary: Diffusion VLAs use the VLM only for static conditioning. JADE feeds structured noisy action latents into the VLM at every denoising step, guiding the expert via gated cross-attention and supervising the VLM to recover clean actions, allowing fewer sampling steps. Gets 12.67% on RoboDojo (best among pi0.5-based), gains on RoboTwin 2.0, and +20.8 pts on four real bimanual tasks.
2611.01215.why: Relevant design idea for coupling VLM and flow action experts in VLAs.

2611.00896.tldr: Evaluation-integrity framework showing vectorized resets can break test-state identity in paired VLA simulation comparisons.
2611.00896.summary: Shows that in vectorized LIBERO harnesses, termination timing can change initial-state assignment so the same episode index need not mean the same state. Proposes invariants, provenance logging, and a checker, tested with emulated controllers only. No real-VLA experiments.
2611.00896.why: Minor evaluation hygiene note; low priority.

2611.01046.tldr: Entropy-regularized continuous-time RL for regime-switching consumption-investment with closed-form exploratory policies.
2611.01046.summary: Derives optimal exploratory strategies (Gaussian investment, Gibbs consumption) and shows classical decisions are their modes. Develops continuous-time q-learning with policy improvement and martingale characterizations. Numerical experiments support theory.

2611.01190.tldr: ClothDojo: sim platform using an NOCS-textured VLA policy to generate ~8,000 garment flattening/folding trajectories for training RGB policies.
2611.01190.summary: Fine-tunes a VLA with NOCS canonical-surface textures on human demos and corrections to act as a data generator in simulation. Retains ~8,000 successful trajectories over hundreds of garments, re-rendered with random appearances. RGB policies trained on them beat those trained on the original human data; unseen-garment generalization remains hard.
2611.01190.why: Deformable bimanual data generation; adjacent to your manipulation interests.

2611.00615.tldr: Second-place MetaFine solution showing that making a scripted teacher 'imitable' matters more than large VLAs for precise insertion.
2611.00615.summary: Trains a small 19M policy per task on data from a privileged scripted teacher including corrections. Finds teacher pauses become student stalls and habits become shortcuts; fixing these raised letter insertion from 0.44 to 0.82 (then 0.88), overall score 0.947, over 2x pi0.
2611.00615.why: Practical lessons on demonstration quality for precise imitation learning.

2611.00668.tldr: DDPG controller with Smith predictor for input-delay systems, with robustness conditions and delay identification analysis.
2611.00668.summary: Trains DDPG on a delay-free plant and deploys with a Smith predictor. Derives closed-loop maps, small-gain and nu-gap robustness conditions, and delay-identification convergence. Experiments on first-order plants with valve stiction.

2611.00843.tldr: Deployment report of a 20B video DiT (MiniMax H3) running quantized on an Apple M5 Pro Mac mini.
2611.00843.summary: Documents deploying a Q8 20B video diffusion transformer on 64GB Apple Silicon, with build, memory, and latency measurements. A 15s 576x1024 clip took ~81 minutes; 17 production clips rendered without failure. No model innovation.

2611.01071.tldr: High-confidence lower-bound policy optimization for safe RL in flex-route transit control.
2611.01071.summary: Combines importance sampling, concentration inequalities and a differentiable surrogate to optimize a high-confidence performance lower bound. Beats offline and safe RL baselines in average and tail risk on a Chicago-route SUMO case study.

2611.00800.tldr: Discrete-time variational framework for deterministic-step ('degenerate') diffusion, shown formally equivalent to flow matching.
2611.00800.summary: Considers diffusion models whose per-step generator is deterministic and builds a modified variational objective. Proves equivalence with discrete-time flow matching and recovery of the data distribution as the number of steps grows. Removes the need for continuous-time machinery to justify flow matching.
2611.00800.why: Squarely on diffusion/flow equivalence theory you follow; from Barber's group.

2611.00636.tldr: Replaces bang-bang Lagrange multiplier response with a continuous regularized response for primal-dual safe RL.
2611.00636.summary: SDLA uses cost centering, trajectory weighting and quadratic regularization to get a unique continuous multiplier, computed by ternary search. Proves bounds and convergence; PPO/SAC on OmniSafe and HASARD show better constraint tracking, beating human baselines on some HASARD settings.
