2611.00859.tldr: Wave Forcing: staggered multi-step streaming video generation with pipeline parallelism reaching ~135 FPS on 8 H200s.
2611.00859.summary: Chunk-wise AR video needs two forward passes per chunk. WF attends to earlier partially-denoised chunks, staggers denoising across model replicas for one chunk per round, and uses a three-stage training recipe. On Wan2.1-1.3B, matches Rolling Forcing quality with higher dynamics and 7x single-GPU throughput.
2611.00859.why: Streaming AR video diffusion; relevant only for real-time video world models.

2611.01250.tldr: SPECTRA scores manipulation execution quality from object-centric relative-pose constraints learned from sim demos.
2611.01250.summary: Learns which relative-pose directions are constrained from 30 oracle demos per task and scores deviations as a quality index. Correlates with human judgment (Spearman 0.81 overall, 0.61 among successes) and recovers constraints with 94% accuracy. Selecting top-scored demos for diffusion policy on hardware improves success in exploratory tests.
2611.01250.why: Demo-quality filtering for diffusion policy training is relevant to low-quality data concerns.

2611.01322.tldr: Localized suppression patches in latent space to correct learned reward models for interactionless IRL without retraining.
2611.01322.summary: Proposes an Alignment Flywheel that finds overgeneralized reward regions and compiles them into latent-space suppression patches for MoE-GUIDE. Tested on MuJoCo and with operator norms absent from demos. Shows localized corrections can modify learned rewards.

2611.00848.tldr: Benchmark and counterfactual decision-level RL for when VLMs should re-examine in high-resolution visual search.
2611.00848.summary: Introduces ReSee with 8,827 commit-or-re-examine decisions and counterfactual labels. CARE assigns paired-continuation advantages to verdict tokens. Improves accuracy and selectivity over GRPO on two backbones and six OOD benchmarks.

2611.00951.tldr: Negative result: Koopman-structured differentiable world models do not help humanoid tracking policy learning vs MLPs.
2611.00951.summary: Replaces the MLP world model in a G1 whole-body tracking pipeline with Koopman variants. Return is at best equal (0.823 vs 0.830) with 1.3-1.6x higher one-step error; the issue is that action-affine models only fit as a tangent at the policy's operating point. MLP world models remain better.
2611.00951.why: Careful analysis of world-model structure; tangential to manipulation.

2611.00898.tldr: Friction-cone-constrained bilateral teleoperation that provably keeps unsecured furniture static while opening doors.
2611.00898.summary: Projects commanded wrenches onto a robust admissible set from support friction cones and tipping margins, with bounded transparency loss near the boundary. Includes a pre-task certificate. 100 trials with five operators quantify the stability-transparency trade-off.

2611.00513.tldr: A VLM agent builds a minimal kinematic world model via perception tools, then a geometric planner optimizes contact and motion.
2611.00513.summary: Instead of producing actions, the VLM constructs and validates a task-relevant kinematic model, refined with execution feedback. Achieves zero-shot 91% on RoboCasa, 97% on LIBERO-PRO, 76% on R2R-CE, beating baselines by large margins with fewer tokens.
2611.00513.why: Zero-shot agentic manipulation; different paradigm from learned policies.

2611.01001.tldr: Neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for verification-aware automation of CFD, space awareness, and nuclear engineering workflows.
2611.01001.summary: Learned models propose while a symbolic rules engine and validated physics decide. Raises converged CFD rate on unseen aircraft from <1% to 74% and performs well on conjunction risk. Scaled training to 8,000 Aurora nodes.

2611.00926.tldr: 4B MLLM for mobile UI understanding and generation trained with fine-grained supervision and online render-aware GRPO.
2611.00926.summary: Builds an 80-category UI taxonomy corpus and 5,000 requirement-screenshot-DSL tuples, using decomposed rewards and rendered-output GRPO. Achieves strong grounding and generation scores at 4B and shows understanding-to-generation transfer.

2611.00586.tldr: Learning-to-reweight source prompts in GRPO using aggregated target-side feedback under dataset mismatch.
2611.00586.summary: Proposes L2RR, a bi-level objective learning a prompt sampling distribution maximizing held-out target accuracy while penalizing uninformative rollouts. Improves target performance and rollout efficiency on six math benchmarks.

2611.00634.tldr: PREM regulates recurrent visual memory updates in a pi0.5 VLA using action-conditioned future-prediction discrepancy.
2611.00634.summary: Uses future visual-feature prediction both as training signal for memory and to gate spatial memory updates at execution. On pi0.5, improves DOMINO dynamic tasks from 9.6% to 20.7% and RMBench memory tasks from 14.4% to 83.8%, with 7.7 ms overhead.
2611.00634.why: History-conditioned policies are on your list; a practical memory mechanism for VLAs.

2611.00539.tldr: Shows sped-up imitation fails because merged commands exceed controller per-step limits; greedy realisable merging fixes it.
2611.00539.summary: Explains collapse of re-timed demonstrations at 2-3x speed via commands exceeding the controller's per-period displacement bound (the 'exceed share'). A single-parameter greedy merge rule keeps commands realisable, beating baselines on robomimic (e.g., +14 pts on Square) and enabling 2.3x humanoid motion tracking at 71% success.
2611.00539.why: Clear mechanistic insight relevant to fast policy execution and action chunk timing.

2611.01307.tldr: Stability analysis of exploration strength in test-time RL with majority rewards, deriving collapse regimes in closed form.
2611.01307.summary: Models single-problem TTRL as softmax logit flow and derives boundaries between collapse and spread regimes, analyzing effects of learning rate and GRPO normalization. A rare-answer bonus needs coefficient above 1/log(G-1). Verified on MATH-500.

2611.01729.tldr: ODE policy learns a neural-ODE vector field over actions, integrating each action from the previous one for continuous trajectories.
2611.01729.summary: Instead of predicting action values, a neural ODE learns the action's dynamics by matching integrated actions to targets over short chunks (IL) or single steps (RL), with a diversity head for multimodality. Versus flow matching after one epoch: 5.9x success, 5.4x generalization, 10.8x faster generation; best on 14 real tasks spanning single-arm, bimanual, dexterous and humanoid robots. Also speeds up humanoid motion-tracking RL.
2611.01729.why: A direct challenger to flow-matching policies and action chunking with broad real-robot evidence, including dexterous hands.

2611.02171.tldr: End-to-end RGB visuomotor in-hand reorientation with image-specified goals, distilled from state teachers and transferred sim-to-real.
2611.02171.summary: Avoids explicit object pose estimation under occlusion by jointly learning visual features and control via distillation from privileged teachers with auxiliary reconstruction. Goals are specified as images rather than canonical poses. Beats pose-based and pretrained-encoder policies in sim and transfers a single policy to five real objects.
2611.02171.why: Core in-hand dexterity with sim-to-real and pose-free goal specification.

2611.01565.tldr: Shows closed-loop pass@k reveals a coverage-reliability tradeoff in generative policy pretraining that predicts post-training success.
2611.01565.summary: Argues validation loss and mean success miss what matters for post-training. Large-k pass@k distinguishes checkpoints with equal pass@1 but different RL/SFT post-training outcomes, and peaks at different points in pretraining. Proposes an offline checkpoint-selection criterion and generative data augmentation that preserves coverage while raising pass@1.
2611.01565.why: Rigorous understanding paper (Simchowitz, Song) directly on BC pretraining for RL fine-tuning of generative policies.

2611.01600.tldr: Occlusion-aware manipulation planning combining object-centric scene reconstruction, LLM-proposed actions, and MCTS over a learned world model.
2611.01600.summary: Reconstructs hidden geometry and relational states (blocker hierarchies, access corridors) in clutter. An LLM proposes structured candidates evaluated by MCTS with an action-conditioned world model. Beats VLAs and embodied agents on Reveal/Placement tasks; validated on a real shelf.
2611.01600.why: Planning in clutter; peripheral to policy learning.

2611.01390.tldr: Training-free execution layer that time-reparameterizes VLA action chunks to remove inference stalls and speed up motion while preserving path.
2611.01390.summary: Treats motion as time reparameterization of a reference path updated only by new observations: a path layer enters each replan at consumed progress, a time layer speeds execution within actuator and latency limits. Analyzes bias/variance of continuation error and a break-even success rate. On LIBERO raises throughput 33% (pi0.5) and 104% (SmolVLA) with equal or better success.
2611.01390.why: Practical real-time chunking/fast execution for chunked policies; sim-only.

2611.02160.tldr: Value Forcing learns return distributions with flow matching, enforcing Bellman consistency at every noise level for data-efficient value learning.
2611.02160.summary: Value learning suffers from indirect bootstrapped supervision with limited data. Value Forcing uses flow matching over returns and imposes Bellman consistency at all noise levels, preventing collapse of the return distribution. Actor-critic (VF) and implicit (IVF) variants outperform prior value learners on 26 long-horizon offline RL tasks, especially with little data.
2611.02160.why: RL x flow matching from Eysenbach's group; a new way to use generative models for critics.

2611.01713.tldr: Post-hoc CBF-QP safety filter for VLAs that uses predicted action chunks to generate rejoin routes around obstacles.
2611.01713.summary: Detects blocked nominal trajectories from VLA chunks and adds entry-exit-rejoin guidance as a soft term while keeping the CBF constraint hard. Improves collision avoidance and success over AEGIS on SafeLIBERO.
2611.01713.why: Safety filtering for VLAs; modest relevance.

2611.01858.tldr: Learned importance-based KV memory retention and eviction for long-horizon autoregressive video generation.
2611.01858.summary: Replaces sliding windows and fixed sinks with a router predicting frame importance, degradation-aware training, and EMA-based memory evolution under a fixed KV budget, trained by distillation. Improves long-horizon quality and consistency over baselines.
2611.01858.why: AR video memory management; related to world models only indirectly.

2611.01677.tldr: Industrial streaming multi-view causal world model for driving and embodied AI with 3D Gaussian scene context and linear attention.
2611.01677.summary: Combines view-temporal attention, multi-view RoPE, single-pass 3D Gaussian reconstruction as context, and gated linear attention for streaming. Trained in pretrain/mid-train/post-train stages and used for closed-loop simulation, training and world action models.
2611.01677.why: Large world model mostly for driving; less relevant to manipulation.

2611.01404.tldr: Characterizes serving workloads of agentic robot fleets (VLM brain plus VLA) and proposes admission control for KV-cache thrashing.
2611.01404.summary: Profiles 80 LIBERO-PRO episodes with brain contexts up to 215k tokens and VLA chunk deadlines. Shows throughput collapse from repetitive prefill beyond 20 robots; a static active-episode cap raises episode throughput from 1.30 to ~5.3/min.

2611.02236.tldr: Iterative Gumbel Planning uses factorized categorical policies with Gumbel top-K and MPPI-style search for continuous control.
2611.02236.summary: Shows distilling search winners into Gaussian policies causes projection error and variance growth. IGP aligns policy support with search candidates via per-dimension categorical policies, using Gumbel top-K sampling plus iterative MPPI-like refinement. SOTA aggregate on DMControl and HumanoidBench with smoother actions.
2611.02236.why: Search-based policy improvement for continuous control; adjacent to your RL/MPPI interests.

2611.01483.tldr: Residual steering of a flow-matching action expert's velocity field using tactile forecasts and real-time tactile feedback.
2611.01483.summary: Directly adding tactile signals to vision-dominant policies can hurt. TF2-Steering uses a tactile mixture-of-experts to learn residual velocity-field corrections for a vision-based foundation policy, trained in three stages. Gains of 10.7 pts in sim and 9.1 pts in real progress success over the strongest baselines across 12 tasks.
2611.01483.why: Combines tactile sensing with flow-policy steering, squarely in your interests.

2611.01844.tldr: Navigation world model pretrained with latent actions on 17.5M action-free navigation frames, then action-aligned.
2611.01844.summary: Curates NavAnywhere from 15 sources (robots, humans, drones) and learns latent actions via visual prediction, then aligns to physical motions. Improves visual prediction in and out of domain and navigation performance.
2611.01844.why: Navigation-focused; latent-action pretraining idea transfers somewhat.

2611.01560.tldr: Open harness enabling open-weight LLMs to act as zero-shot robot-use agents, surpassing proprietary results on RoboDojo.
2611.01560.summary: uni-robot-agent lets an open Qwen model score 31.39 on RoboDojo vs 28.97 for a GPT-based agent, and perform on 19 real tasks. Analysis links robot use to four general model capabilities.

2611.02177.tldr: ANCHOR anchors the actor to the offline policy with annealed KL plus a small conservative critic term for replay-free offline-to-online RL.
2611.02177.summary: Shows dropping offline replay causes early collapse while strong conservatism hurts final performance. ANCHOR uses an annealed KL anchor and residual conservative regularizer, with a two-phase regret interpretation. Reduces catastrophic failure on FrankaKitchen, AntMaze and Adroit while keeping strong asymptotic returns.
2611.02177.why: Relevant to stable RL fine-tuning of pretrained policies, including Adroit dexterous tasks.

2611.01372.tldr: Physics-state-driven image-to-video generation with sparse trajectory and dense motion guidance for plausible collisions.
2611.01372.summary: Predicts free-flight and collision dynamics with a calibrated physics state generator and converts rollouts into sparse and dense guidance for diffusion. Improves physical plausibility on 100 sphere-plane collision scenes.

2611.01663.tldr: Driving VLA with masked flow-matching action expert plus rule-based emergency braking for the AlpaSim challenge.
2611.01663.summary: Pairs a 4B driving VLM with a layer-wise flow-matching expert and a soft visual mask. Mask yields modest closed-loop gains; adding AEB raises score from 0.479 to 0.599 and cuts at-fault collisions from 34 to 11.

2611.01942.tldr: Fitted Q-iteration with L1-linked source coefficients for transfer in offline RL with statistical guarantees.
2611.01942.summary: DFQI jointly estimates target Q-functions while borrowing from weighted source coefficients per Bellman update. Provides sieve-based guarantees and empirical gains with limited target data in marketing/healthcare-style settings.

2611.01659.tldr: Humanoid whole-body affordance-aware grasping with active perception, trained in sim with controller-in-the-loop filtering.
2611.01659.summary: Perceive-Align-Grasp pipeline with belief-driven viewpoint selection, point-cloud affordance policy, and body repositioning. Rejects 73% of kinematically valid but dynamically infeasible grasps during data curation. Achieves 87.5% real success on a multi-level shelf with zero real demos.
2611.01659.why: Humanoid grasping; useful insight on kinodynamic data filtering.

2611.01986.tldr: World-model-guided search over rubric edits for LLM graders.
2611.01986.summary: Learns to predict correction and degradation rates of rubric edits from paired grading results to choose candidates. Wins 20 of 27 comparisons and lifts gpt-5-mini accuracy on ASAP2.0 from 18.2% to 46.7%.

2611.02101.tldr: Shows inference delay and camera shift interact superadditively to raise pi0.5 safety violations on LIBERO.
2611.02101.summary: Formalizes cross-layer variation propagation and measures interaction effects over 4,000 paired episodes. A 400 ms delay adds 3.5 pts violations normally but 37 pts under a 60-degree camera shift. Proposes a research agenda.
2611.02101.why: Interesting caution about latency plus distribution shift for VLAs.

2611.01609.tldr: Soft magnetic pillar-array tactile sensor with Hall sensing for surface texture and material recognition.
2611.01609.summary: Models pillar deformation and superposed magnetic fields. Classifies six materials at 99.34% offline accuracy and tracks periodic surface geometry.

2611.02049.tldr: Survey of reinforcement learning applications in high-energy physics.
2611.02049.summary: Reviews RL for accelerator control, tracking, jets, detector design, triggers and formal theory, with method background. Discusses when RL beats alternatives and recurring challenges.

2611.02240.tldr: Belief-space MPC coupling information gathering with clarity-adaptive CVaR barriers for interactive driving.
2611.02240.summary: Treats clarity as a planning variable to tighten or relax risk constraints. Bounds information-seeking cost; achieves top success (~94%) and lowest collisions over 5,000 merging/intersection simulations.

2611.02284.tldr: Training-free SVD/leverage-score visual token pruning for VLMs and VLAs under extreme compression.
2611.02284.summary: Frames pruning as preserving low-rank spectral structure. Cuts visual tokens by up to 99.3%; at 16 tokens reduces FLOPs 82.4% with 4.18x speedup.
2611.02284.why: Possible tool for faster VLA inference.

2611.01666.tldr: Shows action-ablation tests of world models give false positives and lose power when pooled; proposes tempered e-value mixtures.
2611.01666.summary: Under autocorrelated designs, future actions stand in for history, so standard diagnostics report spurious action effects. Proposes conditional randomization e-value tests and mixture tempering, validated on biology, diffusion models, IRIS, TD-MPC2 and iVideoGPT robot videos.
2611.01666.why: Methodological care for testing action-conditioning of world models; niche.

2611.01559.tldr: Sample-complexity bound for flow matching accounting for finite data and finite SGD optimization rather than exact ERM.
2611.01559.summary: Develops an ERM-free analysis with N samples and T SGD steps under regularity assumptions. The bound separates approximation, statistical, tail and optimization errors.
2611.01559.why: Flow-matching theory; useful background though likely technical.

2611.01645.tldr: Uncertainty-aware iterative depth restoration for transparent and reflective objects using a depth foundation prior.
2611.01645.summary: Co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty with uncertainty-gated features and robust scale normalization. Best mean rank on an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark; improves 6D pose and grasp synthesis.

2611.02304.tldr: Flow-matching-generated cost maps guide constrained A* for global routing in circuit design.
2611.02304.summary: Uses flow matching to predict routing tendencies as a cost map for A*. Comparable wirelength and vias with strong performance on hard instances.

2611.02076.tldr: Scene-adaptive layer readout and decoding depth for diffusion driving VLAs, up to 6x speedup.
2611.02076.summary: Finds late layers support trajectory readout after one sweep while early layers need more decoding. A readout MoE and adaptive decoding policy improve Waymo E2E RFS by up to 0.56 with up to 6x speedup.
2611.02076.why: Driving; adaptive diffusion decoding idea is mildly transferable.

2611.03091.tldr: Contact-rich adversarial Klask-playing IL benchmark with real human demos, synthetic PPO data, and a validated sim-to-real actuator model.
2611.03091.summary: Provides 80k real human demo timesteps, 320k symmetry-augmented steps, and up to 5M synthetic expert steps. Diagnoses BC data-scaling plateaus, weak GAIL discriminator gradients, and BC-prior x reward-density interactions. The strongest BC baseline transfers zero-shot to hardware.
2611.03091.why: Niche contact-rich IL benchmark with real-hardware bridge.

2611.02546.tldr: Energy-based orchestrator selects and refines policy-goal pairs among modular goal-conditioned policies for humanoid loco-manipulation.
2611.02546.summary: Learns per-policy composite energies over low-level goals reflecting feasibility and tracking accuracy; at runtime refines goals and runs the lowest-energy pair. New policies are added without retraining others. Improves precision-robustness in sim and transfers frozen to real humanoid tasks.
2611.02546.why: Energy-based composition of skills; tangential but conceptually neat.

2611.02822.tldr: Shows frame sinks in AR video diffusion act via a sparse subset of heads and proposes head-disentangled context routing during distillation.
2611.02822.summary: Finds long-range consistency is anchored by few attention heads while most capture local motion, so universal sinks over-condition and collapse motion. Disen-Forcing routes context per head and adds motion regularization, improving both consistency and dynamics on long-horizon benchmarks.

2611.03815.tldr: Bimanual VLA trained on 16,151 hours of handheld-gripper demos with no robot data, reaching 78% on ten long-horizon real tasks.
2611.03815.summary: Collects data with YUBI, an open-source handheld gripper, and trains a wrist-camera-only model that learns task-relevant view regions, predicts task stage, and streams actions. Averages 78% vs 27% for the best of four VLAs post-trained on the same demos at an unseen site, across multiple embodiments. Releases dataset, weights and a recipe post-trainable in under four hours on 8 H200s.
2611.03815.why: Major open data/model release showing robot-free human data can scale precise manipulation.

2611.03647.tldr: Pixel-UMI learns whole-body mobile manipulation from sensorized human demos via environment-aware retargeting, error-aware masking, and DAgger.
2611.03647.summary: Retargets human head/gripper trajectories using reconstructed scene geometry into collision-aware robot targets, masks views with retargeting error during training, and adds on-policy human corrections. Reaches 87% average task progress on five tasks including deformable and contact-rich bimanual ones.
2611.03647.why: Pathak group; learning from human data with careful handling of embodiment gap.

2611.03103.tldr: Benchmark quantifying how VLA inference latency hurts success across tasks, object speeds and sync/async execution, with a predictive model.
2611.03103.summary: Finds 100 ms latency can nearly halve success on moving targets, with sensitivity varying by task and policy; async execution partially recovers. An empirical model predicts success from limited calibration with 5.7-7.8% RMSE to guide configuration choice.
2611.03103.why: Useful empirical grounding for real-time chunking and fast inference decisions.

2611.02677.tldr: Visuotactile diffusion policy with recurrent history and an auxiliary tactile-change prediction loss for assembly.
2611.02677.summary: Conditions action generation on four-step histories of two cameras and two fingertip tactile images. An auxiliary loss predicts fingertip image changes two steps ahead given actions, training-only. Raises MuJoCo assembly success from 42.7% to 59.0%.
2611.02677.why: Simple recipe for tactile diffusion policies; sim-only evidence.

2611.03294.tldr: ForceLDM distills future force/torque and optical-flow dynamics features from a privileged teacher into a student policy for contact-rich tasks.
2611.03294.summary: A teacher with future F/T and flow extracts dynamics features, distilled into a student using current observations, with curriculum noise injection to avoid over-reliance. Outperforms baselines on five real contact-rich tasks and generalizes to novel objects.
2611.03294.why: Force-aware latent dynamics for contact-rich manipulation is close to your area.

2611.03520.tldr: Low-cost (<$50) dense three-axis tactile fingertip with shear sensing, improving visuotactile policies by 46.7 pts over vision-only.
2611.03520.summary: PanoTac provides 12x32x3 normal and shear readings at 60 Hz with characterized repeatability. Visuotactile policies on test-tube prep, grain scooping, and salt pouring beat vision-only by 46.7 pts; ablations show both spatial and shear info matter.
2611.03520.why: Affordable shear-capable tactile sensor useful for dexterous policy learning.

2611.04028.tldr: Compression Forcing tokenizes history by dynamics saliency for diffusion world models and enables hierarchical history guidance.
2611.04028.summary: Argues video-style tokenization optimizes realism, not predictive utility. Dynamics-Aware Tokenization orders compressed history by dynamics saliency, enabling guidance that amplifies salient history at inference. Improves prediction fidelity, physical realism and downstream decision-making.
2611.04028.why: History compression plus guidance for diffusion world models; relevant to world-model and long-context interests.

2611.03501.tldr: Controlled study showing heavy robot arms relative to objects make behavior cloning less data-efficient, while RL is robust.
2611.03501.summary: Varies robot and object masses in simulation. RL succeeds broadly, but BC is more reliable when a light robot handles heavier objects and heavy robots need more demos. Choosing lower-inertia workspaces or steering demonstrators toward low-inertia configurations improves imitation.
2611.03501.why: Understanding paper (Agrawal group) with actionable advice for collecting demos for contact-rich tasks.

2611.02777.tldr: REPAIR distills RL specialists into a single flow-matching VLA via critic-weighted flow matching with offline then on-policy data.
2611.02777.summary: VLAs fail in short precision-critical phases where RL specialists help but require switching. REPAIR queries specialists for multiple action candidates, weights them by critic value, and trains with weighted flow matching first on assisted rollouts then on the VLA's own states. Achieves 100% on six real tasks (30 trials each) with lower jerk than specialist-assisted execution.
2611.02777.why: Strong real-robot RL+flow-VLA fine-tuning recipe directly on your list.

2611.02497.tldr: Distributed in-the-wild evaluation of VLAs and frontier agents across 124 sites and four embodiments.
2611.02497.summary: Runs 5,699 blinded pairwise Open Track comparisons and a Fine-tune Track with 100 demos per task over 20 tasks. Frontier agents rival VLAs; GR00T N1.7 and pi0.5 lead different embodiments; rankings agree weakly across embodiments and zero-shot rankings poorly predict post-fine-tuning performance.

2611.02629.tldr: DexArena: simulation benchmark with 10 long-horizon and 30 stage-level bimanual dexterous tasks with teleoperated demos.
2611.02629.summary: Provides staged tasks with physically grounded success conditions, unified interface, scene randomization and verified human demos. Baselines expose difficulty in precision, scene generalization and skill composition.
2611.02629.why: Directly useful benchmark for dexterous bimanual policy learning.

2611.02782.tldr: History Forcing adds teacher residuals from informative history to distillation targets for few-step AR video world models.
2611.02782.summary: Uses the difference between teacher predictions with and without informative context (less-drifted chunks or fixed-view rollouts) to correct distillation targets. SOTA among 1.3B models (VBench 85.07 at 15s, 79.82 VBench-Long at 60s) and better out-of-sight consistency.
2611.02782.why: Memory and consistency for video world models; relevant to your WM interests.

2611.03648.tldr: Pixel: co-designed low-cost wheeled humanoid, data-collection interfaces, whole-body controller and policy stack for mobile manipulation.
2611.03648.summary: Integrates human-aligned hardware with compliant grippers, teleop and robot-free collection, unified whole-body control, and hierarchical language-conditioned policies. Demonstrates dexterous, active-perception and navigation behaviors.
2611.03648.why: Full-stack system from Pathak group; companion to Pixel-UMI.

2611.04083.tldr: Open-source $8.1k 56-DOF mobile bimanual robot with 17-DOF hands and Vision Pro whole-body teleoperation.
2611.04083.summary: MABEL combines two 7-DOF arms, 17-DOF hands, torso, lift, neck and holonomic base, with back-drivable compliance and floor-to-2.23m reach. Vision Pro teleop achieves 137 ms latency; demonstrates an end-to-end IL pipeline.
2611.04083.why: Affordable dexterous-hand platform for data collection.

2611.03622.tldr: Prompting VLMs to first describe scene dynamics then assess with explicit rubrics yields calibrated zero-shot robot progress rewards.
2611.03622.summary: Decouples description and assessment to avoid confirmation bias where VLMs hallucinate progress in failures. Matches or beats post-trained reward models across tasks and embodiments and supports downstream RL.
2611.03622.why: Cheap reward model for real-world RL fine-tuning.

2611.02699.tldr: Reproduction of the Robotic World Model dynamics model showing its ensemble uncertainty ranks errors well but badly understates scale.
2611.02699.summary: Reimplements RWM; ensemble disagreement correlates with error (rho 0.90) but one-sigma coverage is only 4.6% at 100 steps. Self-rollout raises coverage to 33%; horizon rescaling partially fixes it. Identifies evaluation pipeline defects.

2611.02803.tldr: Modality-wise on-policy distillation for joint audio-video generation addressing sparse audio supervision.
2611.02803.summary: Uses asymmetric noise for privileged visual context, grouped multi-noise audio sampling, and timestep importance weighting. Improves video generation while preserving audio quality.

2611.04031.tldr: LLM-based decision transformer with language-guided trajectory augmentation for multi-task offline RL.
2611.04031.summary: Uses one LLM to generate and filter task-aligned trajectories and then as a language-conditioned DT. Outperforms baselines on Meta-World and MuJoCo, especially with little data.

2611.02964.tldr: Test-time personalization of pose-driven human video diffusion using self-generated static key-pose clips.
2611.02964.summary: Generates pseudo-ground-truth frames at key poses, filters by identity, and trains a per-subject LoRA on static clips. Beats base and matches five-real-frame adaptation on TikTok and UBC Fashion.

2611.03584.tldr: LVLM agent with belief-space TAMP tools for partially observable mobile manipulation.
2611.03584.summary: Agent writes partial plans of observation and execution actions completed by classical search, then binds geometric parameters via tools. Outperforms direct tool-calling agents on household tasks with Rainbow Y1 and G1.

2611.03163.tldr: Fourth-place MetaFine solution routing tasks to adapted DINOv2-DiT or pi0.5 policies.
2611.03163.summary: Uses a task-routed mixture of policies with local visual features and expert continuations. Overall score 0.878, beating the reference on all five tasks.

2611.04073.tldr: Ablation showing computer-use agents gain little from world-model rollouts when given tutorials.
2611.04073.summary: Builds tutorial datasets and a policy-judge framework; even oracle visual futures add little. Bottleneck is judge reasoning over futures.

2611.04010.tldr: Contrastive task-aware decision transformer using an LLM backbone for offline meta-RL.
2611.04010.summary: Learns task representations from contrastive, language, world-model and Q supervision to condition a DT. Outperforms prior offline meta-RL methods, especially zero-shot.

2611.02690.tldr: Conceptual framework for human-oriented world models of a person's state and evolution.
2611.02690.summary: Proposes estimation, personalized prediction and support loops, illustrated with hypothetical scenarios. No experiments.

2611.02341.tldr: Agentic video world model that plans exploration and maintains spatial memory to build persistent worlds from one image.
2611.02341.summary: An agent designs the world and journey while the video model generates chunks stored with geometry; occlusion-aware history selection and reliability-based memory maintenance handle drift. SOTA on revisiting and exploration benchmarks.
2611.02341.why: Video world models for content; tangential.

2611.02922.tldr: Ablation ladder showing satellite inspection fuel efficiency depends on allowing drift, state memory, and horizon, not algorithm choice.
2611.02922.summary: Removing drift, drift state, or horizon doubles fuel; model-based agents ignoring fuel waste it; a CBF filter eliminates keep-out violations.

2611.02660.tldr: Hierarchical VLA keeping explicit language memory via event detection for non-Markovian manipulation.
2611.02660.summary: Maintains task history as language updated on detected events. On 10 real non-Markovian tasks (56 variants), +12.8 pts intra-episode over best baseline, 78% compositional subtask success, 4.5x less memory and 2.5x faster than keyframes.
2611.02660.why: Memory for VLAs; moderately relevant to history-conditioned policies.

2611.05754.tldr: Sampling-plus-recovered-gradient trajectory optimization for physics-based retargeting of human demos to dexterous hands and humanoids.
2611.05754.summary: GRASP extends tempered SMC by fitting local quadratic models to archived rollouts and using their gradients for MCMC rejuvenation, without a differentiable simulator; GRASP-MPC scales to long demos. Achieves 92.8% success on 1,352 bimanual OakInk2 demos with a shared tracking objective and improves PPO tracking for pen spinning. Real-hardware dexterous and humanoid demos.
2611.05754.why: Directly addresses retargeting human hand data under contact, a core interest.

2611.05163.tldr: RoboTryOn converts egocentric human videos into robot videos via 'virtual try-on' and labels actions with a depth-aware IDM.
2611.05163.summary: Keeps the demonstrated motion and swaps the human for a target robot specified by a reference image, translating keyframes autoregressively and conditioning on hand skeletons. An inverse dynamics model infers actions from synthesized videos. Raises novel-task success including bimanual from 2% to 60% with no robot demos of those tasks and matches teleop-only training at about a third of the cost.
2611.05163.why: Synthetic dexterous data from human video, in line with DreamGen-style ideas you track.

2611.05295.tldr: GSBR regularizes online RL by distance to a diffusion/flow base policy's support rather than its full distribution.
2611.05295.summary: BC regularizers penalize dropping suboptimal modes while hard support constraints block nearby improvements. GSBR applies zero penalty inside the base policy's support and a smoothly growing penalty outside, estimated from base-policy samples only. Across 19 tasks on four benchmarks, raises success from 33% to 95% with ~23% higher normalized throughput than the next-best RL method.
2611.05295.why: Levine-group method for RL fine-tuning of generative BC policies, squarely in your core interests.

2611.04392.tldr: Few-step flow-matching control over JEPA latents for quadrotor forest flight on edge hardware, with a runtime shield.
2611.04392.summary: BC fails via copycat causal confusion; DAgger plateaus at 11-21%; a map-free runtime shield raises success from 21.1% to 52.2% over 180 missions. Uses two-step Euler flow matching for action chunks.
2611.04392.why: Drone navigation; low relevance though the BC failure analysis is instructive.

2611.04870.tldr: PrimeSim: action-conditioned multiview world-model simulator midtrained on 30k hours of cross-embodiment robot data, made autoregressive at 10 FPS.
2611.04870.summary: Uses a unified cross-embodiment action representation, dual-path frame-aligned conditioning, view-aware interleaved attention, and fast-video/slow-memory posttraining with self-rollout. Runs at 10.1 FPS, stable over long rollouts, adapts to new platforms in 100-200 steps, leads four of five WorldSimProbe suites and supports GRPO policy optimization. Weights and code released.
2611.04870.why: Open video world-model simulator for policy evaluation and RL; directly on your WM list.

2611.05093.tldr: Closed-loop benchmark showing generic PTQ (RTN/AWQ/GPTQ) matches VLA-specific quantization and rarely speeds up inference.
2611.05093.summary: Evaluates five PTQ methods on four VLAs over 180k LIBERO/LIBERO-plus episodes and three GPUs. 4-bit generic methods match VLA-specific ones; LIBERO hides 1.5-4.3 pt losses seen under perturbations; quantization is often slower at batch 1 because pi0.5's memory-bound action expert stays 16-bit.
2611.05093.why: Useful reality check on fast VLA inference via quantization.

2611.05119.tldr: DexHOT frames dexterous manipulation as transfer between hand-object configurations, learning a reusable primitive from synthetic pairs.
2611.05119.summary: Learns a relation-conditioned transfer primitive between feasible hand articulation plus object pose configurations without human reference motions, composing long-horizon behavior via subgoal tracking. A single policy reaches 80.5%/69.4% on seen/unseen objects across 120, 61.5% over 200 real transfers, and 90% on six demo-guided real tasks.
2611.05119.why: Core dexterous manipulation with a new goal interface and real-hand results.

2611.05080.tldr: CRONOS benchmarks RL fine-tuning of VLAs under non-episodic, reset-free shared-scene multi-task settings.
2611.05080.summary: Shows naive fine-tuning fails without resets due to shifted object configurations and end-effector poses, mitigated by targeted reset allocation and correcting pretrained biases. Non-episodic training improves long-horizon manipulation and generalization.
2611.05080.why: Practical insight for real-world RL fine-tuning of VLAs.

2611.05585.tldr: Contact-implicit whole-body trajectory optimization for humanoid locomotion on smooth parameterized uneven terrain.
2611.05585.summary: Models ground as a smooth surface with new contact constraints, planning without predefined contact sequences via NLP. Demonstrated on steps and ramps in sim with preliminary real ErgoCub tests.

2611.05372.tldr: PolicyIK: PPO-trained goal-conditioned policy for millimeter-precision inverse kinematics, also trained on a real arm.
2611.05372.summary: Updates joint references from pose feedback with two-scale errors, error-dependent gains, and progress/dwell rewards. Keeps errors within 1 mm/0.2 deg on 93.5% of held-out tasks (98.9% with protocol), beats classical IK on hardware, and executes pi0.5 commands at 95.7% success.
2611.05372.why: Useful low-level component for VLA deployment; modest relevance.

2611.04873.tldr: Audits world-model imagined rewards with execution feedback to select safer supervision for VLA post-training.
2611.04873.summary: A multidimensional reward model ranks candidates and an auditor flags overestimation patterns learned from paired imagined and real executions. Improves LIBERO mean success to 76.25% (+3.0 pts) and raises clean completion on real recordings from 58% to 70%.
2611.04873.why: Relevant to world-model-based VLA post-training; modest gains.

2611.04493.tldr: Diffusion policy conditioned on material properties estimated via 3D Gaussian splatting plus differentiable MPM.
2611.04493.summary: Recovers physical parameters from demo videos with GS-MPM, conditions a material-aware MoE diffusion policy, and uses a physics memory bank for fast retrieval. Improves success and generalization on diverse simulated and real objects.
2611.04493.why: Physics-aware diffusion policy for heterogeneous materials; moderately relevant.

2611.04368.tldr: RAFT first trains LoRA on reasoning annotations then freezes it while fine-tuning VLAs on actions, preserving robustness.
2611.04368.summary: Two-stage post-training mitigates robustness loss from few-demo fine-tuning. On real DROID, OOD success rises from 27.9% to 75.0%; on a bimanual YAM task, 70% vs 36%. Policies attend more to task regions and probe object identity better.
2611.04368.why: Simple VLA fine-tuning recipe with strong real OOD gains.

2611.05377.tldr: DreamX extracts compact (4-token-per-frame) latent actions from a pretrained video diffusion model's features for cross-embodiment transfer.
2611.05377.summary: Compresses latent video frames 300x into action tokens disentangled from appearance using the video model's generative prior. SOTA on LARY-Bench, supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer, and enables cheaper latent-action policies.
2611.05377.why: Latent actions from video models for learning from human video; relevant to WM interests.

2611.04527.tldr: DreamFree distills a video diffusion model's future-predictive features into a current-observation encoder, enabling WAM control without generating video.
2611.04527.summary: Trains a visual encoder to predict a frozen 14B video diffusion model's representations from the current frame, then an action module reads it. Beats SOTA VLAs and WAMs in real and sim at 11 Hz, scales with stronger video priors, and learns new tasks from action-free cross-embodiment videos.
2611.04527.why: Practical route to fast world-action models; squarely in unified video-action interests.

2611.04916.tldr: Kling team report on how multimodal understanding (captioning, prompt enhancement, reward models) drives video generation quality.
2611.04916.summary: Describes Kling-MLLM specialized for captioning, reference-grounded captions, RL-tuned prompt enhancement, perceptually trained text encoders, and dual reward models. Shares evaluation lessons.

2611.04164.tldr: Training-free test-time selection of which past frames to show an AR video decoder using internal representations.
2611.04164.summary: ReCR picks context units matching global rollout state, avoiding redundancy and covering temporal boundaries and spatial layouts, then maps them onto a compact causal axis. Improves multiple AR backbones under matched token budgets.

2611.04477.tldr: Multi-task diffusion policy with VGGT visual tokens and SVD-decomposed rank-one experts routed spectrally to reduce interference.
2611.04477.summary: Uses frozen VGGT features and decomposes denoiser layers into orthogonal rank-one experts adapted via routing and Householder rotations. Averages 68.4% on six RoboTwin tasks (+21.8 over multi-task VO-DP) and improves real bimanual success by 19 pts.
2611.04477.why: Addresses multi-task diffusion policy interference; incremental.

2611.04391.tldr: H2RB co-trains pretrained VLAs on unpaired human and robot demos with geometry-anchored alignment and decoupled-decoder action tokens.
2611.04391.summary: Bridges the embodiment gap at representation and action interfaces so human demos supervise behavior without overwriting robot priors. Real-world object transfer improves from 8.0 to 51.8, skill transfer reaches 62.7 where baselines fail, OOD from 6.0 to 45.3.
2611.04391.why: Learning from human demonstrations for VLA adaptation is close to your interests.

2611.05667.tldr: Operators preview predicted motion in XR and intervene proactively; rejected predictions paired with corrections drive preference post-training.
2611.05667.summary: PHIL displays policy-predicted trajectories, collects corrections before failures, and pairs rejected chunks with executed corrections for preference learning. With five correction episodes, raises diffusion policy success from 44.0% to 70.3% and X-VLA from 57.8% to 76.9% vs HG-DAgger.
2611.05667.why: Preference-based post-training of diffusion/VLA policies with real results.

2611.04424.tldr: 10 ms whole-body tactile withdrawal reflexes integrated with learned humanoid control on Unitree G1.
2611.04424.summary: A reflex pathway detects hazardous contacts and sends withdrawal poses within 10 ms; reflex-in-the-loop training and alignment maintain balance and recovery. Reduces first force peak by 34% and contact impulse 2.15x vs 20 ms delayed reflex.

2611.04204.tldr: Online iLQR-MPC jointly optimizing footsteps and contact forces with whole-body control for humanoid push recovery.
2611.04204.summary: Single-rigid-body iLQR with augmented-Lagrangian constraints replans at 100 Hz; WBC maps to torques at 500 Hz. G1 in MuJoCo recovers from 245 N pushes.

2611.05666.tldr: Systematic study of SAC critic variants finds replayed lambda-return critics help most while soft advantages and soft GAE do not.
2611.05666.summary: Compares six critic variants across full random hyperparameter searches on 14 tasks. Training lambda-return critics on replayed trajectory segments without importance correction improves continuous control; advantage critics and soft GAE add nothing.
2611.05666.why: Rigorous RL fundamentals result directly usable in SAC-based pipelines.

2611.05062.tldr: FloMo fine-tunes a 5B video model to predict 3D scene flow and actions, showing motion beats video as the intermediate.
2611.05062.summary: Renders scene flow as RGB into the video latent space, co-training on action-free human video and robot teleop. Generalizes to unseen objects, primitives, tasks; replacing or adding video prediction hurts, and action tokens attend mostly to motion.
2611.05062.why: Clear evidence on how video pretraining should transfer to actions; relevant to world-action models.

2611.04764.tldr: U-JiT: UNet-like transformer enabling pixel-space video diffusion that beats latent models on Kinetics-600.
2611.04764.summary: Diagnoses shortcomings of pixel-space image transformers for video and proposes a UNet-like transformer plus recipe and sampling changes. Improves FVD 27% over prior SOTA at 128px and gains grow with compression at 256px.
2611.04764.why: Generative modeling architecture insight; moderately relevant.

2611.04566.tldr: Research world model of power engineering from 1.1M papers forecasting concept dynamics and interventions.
2611.04566.summary: Extracts concepts with an LM, learns graph-temporal dynamics and intervention operators, and answers natural-language what-ifs. Outperforms baselines on held-out forecasts.

2611.04543.tldr: CANDO combines conservative noise-space directional residuals with action-space residuals to RL-tune frozen generative policies.
2611.04543.summary: CNDO learns state- and noise-conditioned directions around Gaussian latents with conservative value estimation and gated execution, removing fixed latent feasible regions. CANDO adds an action-space residual, achieving 76.1 NAUC and 91.4% success, +6.6 NAUC and +4.1% over the best single-space method.
2611.04543.why: Noise-space steering of diffusion policies with RL is exactly on your list.

2611.04357.tldr: Moving horizon estimation plus offset-free constrained MPC for wheel-legged robot balance under unknown disturbances.
2611.04357.summary: Virtual-leg MHE with impact-aware noise and constrained MPC outperform LQR baselines in MuJoCo under payloads and wind. Simulation only.

2611.05368.tldr: GUILD guides teleoperated data collection with VLM task proposals and data-attribution feedback on policy performance.
2611.05368.summary: Alternates VLM-proposed environments/goals and collection with predictive data attribution estimating each trajectory's effect on target performance. Improves sample efficiency and deployment performance over passive collection and experienced roboticists in sim and real.
2611.05368.why: Practical for efficient IL data collection.

2611.05448.tldr: Driving agent pairing a typed probabilistic decision model with a language world model forecasting neighbor motion.
2611.05448.summary: Foreseen consequences lower merging collisions from 26.0% to 2.4% and replayed NGSIM collisions from 48.2% to 2.8%.

2611.06724.tldr: Full-stack survey of dexterous hands in the foundation-model era covering hardware, data, cross-embodiment transfer, learning and evaluation.
2611.06724.summary: Reviews work from 2024 to Nov 2026 in five layers with tactile and human hand-object perspectives, plus comparative tables and case analyses. Concludes human data value depends on kinematic/visual/contact alignment, shared action spaces do not remove embodiment constraints, and task completion does not establish physical correctness. Lists eleven open problems.
2611.06724.why: A timely map of your core field; useful reference rather than new results.

2611.05979.tldr: Learns object-centric future hand-object state predictors from HOI datasets and uses predicted object states as RL rewards for dexterous hands.
2611.05979.summary: Rather than imitating human demos directly, predicts future hand-object states and uses object predictions as a general reward term. Outperforms SOTA on three tasks in sim and real with better novel-object generalization, deployed on multiple hands.
2611.05979.why: Human-data-driven rewards for dexterous RL; relevant but details thin.

2611.07245.tldr: MAC-v2 makes long-horizon model-based value expansion work from pixels using a reconstruction-free latent world model with action chunking.
2611.07245.summary: Pixel-based value expansion suffers compounding representation and dynamics errors. MAC-v2 learns latents from prediction and control objectives and uses action chunks to cut recursive predictions. Strong results vs model-free and model-based offline RL on visual OGBench, MMBench2, Robomimic and LIBERO-10; analyses show long horizons, chunking and latent objectives are each essential.
2611.07245.why: Levine-group work tying action chunking to world-model RL from pixels.

2611.06673.tldr: Controlled 720-trial real-robot study isolating which tactile cues (RGB, depth/normal, marker flow) help contact-rich imitation learning.
2611.06673.summary: Derives tactile RGB, normal/depth maps and marker-flow from one vision-based tactile stream and compares them with identical demos and backbone. Tactile raises success from 57.8% to 78.9%; marker flow alone reaches 74.4%; cue-factorized encoders help and cross-attention fusion matches pretrained tactile encoders.
2611.06673.why: Actionable guidance on tactile representations for your contact-rich policies.

2611.06710.tldr: Measurement study of seven VLA inference optimizations across seven VLAs and four GPUs, with stacking guidelines.
2611.06710.summary: Analyzes how CPU launch overhead, memory bandwidth and kernel efficiency shape gains from CUDA graphs, compilation, pruning and quantization, and how methods interact. Derives VLA-Triage guidelines for latency budgets.
2611.06710.why: Practical reference for fast VLA deployment.

2611.06796.tldr: Velocity Adversarial Distillation unifies score distillation, Fisher and moment matching via a critic comparing student and teacher velocity fields.
2611.06796.summary: Argues student-score estimation at intermediate steps is unreliable and uses flow-matching velocities built from the student's sampling process. VA-TDM adds trajectory distribution matching with online velocity learning, giving SOTA four-step text-to-image and text-to-video results and scaling to 33B.
2611.06796.why: Few-step distillation theory/method relevant to fast generative policies.

2611.06184.tldr: Three-tier system (GPT-6 Astra planner, pi0.5 executor, small VLM completion monitor) solving memory-dependent RoboMME cheaply.
2611.06184.summary: The monitor checks subtask completion after each chunk so the expensive planner is called only ~3.6 times per episode. Achieves 79.13% success, 34.6 pts over the best non-oracle baseline.
2611.06184.why: Karen Liu group; practical hierarchical memory design but system-engineering focused.

2611.06622.tldr: Importance-weighted imitation of MPC via kernel density estimates of operating data for power-converter control.
2611.06622.summary: Combines uniform sampling with KDE-based importance weights to focus small networks on expected operating regions. Validated experimentally on a dual active bridge converter.

2611.06905.tldr: Shows generalist robot policies can be improved online across many tasks simultaneously with value-based RL, generalizing to untrained tasks.
2611.06905.summary: Builds structured evaluations for multi-task online improvement and studies value estimation, policy extraction and resource allocation. The right recipe improves many tasks at once and boosts unseen tasks; training task distribution and value-based RL are critical.
2611.06905.why: Directly on RL fine-tuning of foundation policies, with systematic design analysis.

2611.06447.tldr: Auto-derived target/robot regions supervise VLA attention allocation and contrastive alignment to reduce visual shortcuts.
2611.06447.summary: Generates candidate regions from interaction-induced visual changes refined by segmentation, then adds attention-allocation and contrastive losses. Gains of 6.5-25.2% across backbones in sim and real.

2611.07055.tldr: Competitive flow matching adds a latent code with winner-take-all loss over K velocity candidates to cover modes, plus a new guidance.
2611.07055.summary: Standard FM collapses multiple valid targets into a mean velocity. Sampling K candidates via a low-dim code and training only the best enables mode specialization and 'auxiliary conditioning scaling' guidance. On ImageNet-256 at 67% recall, FD drops from 19.22 to 5.91 on SiT with <3% of pretraining compute.
2611.07055.why: New angle on flow-matching mode coverage and guidance, directly in your generative-modeling interests and relevant to multimodal policies.

2611.05847.tldr: Learns a time-to-goal metric on frozen JEPA latents via margin ranking to replace Euclidean planning costs.
2611.05847.summary: Shows Euclidean goal costs in LeWorldModel lose temporal contrast at long offsets. T2G trains on latent triples without rewards and lifts average planning success from 32.7% to 63.0%, rivaling hierarchical H-JEPA.
2611.05847.why: Simple fix for JEPA world-model planning; moderately relevant.

2611.06270.tldr: NextGAN trains a critic by regressing its input gradient onto feature displacements, enabling simple one/few-step adaptation up to 14B.
2611.06270.summary: Equivalent to adversarial training with gradient-energy penalty. One-step ImageNet FID 2.87 (pixel JiT-B), 1.54 (DiT-XL/1), 1.36 adversarial; Wan2.1-1.3B tops VBench among 1.3B methods at one and two steps.
2611.06270.why: One-step generation method; relevant to fast generative policies.

2611.06918.tldr: Encoder-free NEO-VLA lets a flow-matching action expert read visual tokens across backbone depths, beating encoder-based VLAs.
2611.06918.summary: Tokenizes images with light patch convs that evolve jointly with language, letting the action expert tap multiple depths. Native architectures outperform encoder-based ones under controlled comparisons, and action-critical signals peak before the final layer.

2611.06523.tldr: Hierarchical heterogeneous MARL with joint-level descriptors and planner-executor co-optimization for humanoid control.
2611.06523.summary: Factorizes policy per joint conditioned on physical descriptors and co-adapts pose planner and joint executor. Improves locomotion stability in MuJoCo and Isaac Gym.

2611.06442.tldr: TwinBridge uses Gaussian-splat digital twins to pretrain policies and distill dense visual rewards for real-world lab RL.
2611.06442.summary: Simulator states provide event-based progress rewards, distilled into a visual reward model for human-in-the-loop real RL. Reaches 98% success on five lab tasks within 25 minutes of real interaction each.
2611.06442.why: Practical real-world RL fine-tuning recipe; moderately relevant.

2611.06422.tldr: Cross-modal conditional flow matching for denoising with unaligned guidance images in one or two steps.
2611.06422.summary: Progressive FM couples restoration and alignment with stage-focused training and sparse guidance propagation. SOTA few-step results.

2611.05917.tldr: Training-free decoupled sparse attention with cluster compensation and fixed exact blocks for video diffusion acceleration.
2611.05917.summary: Semantic clusters compensate all keys while fixed exact blocks correct errors, allocated by a rate-distortion budget, with cached reassignment. Speeds up few-step video DiTs.

2611.06625.tldr: Learned adiabatic spectral submanifold model plus MPC for full-body dynamic shape control of a helicoid soft trunk robot.
2611.06625.summary: Outperforms linear baselines 10x in shape regulation and balances a tennis ball for 25+ seconds; a 12-hour hardware RL policy fails.

2611.06196.tldr: New safe-set classes beyond control invariance with MPC constraining intermediate horizon nodes and safe-abort.
2611.06196.summary: Guarantees recursive feasibility with broader sets and safety via safe-abort. Fewer constraint violations on a 6-joint arm in sim and on hardware.
2611.06196.why: Safe MPC for manipulators; modest relevance.

2611.06120.tldr: Embodied video world model predicting interaction response fields to guide object feature updates and temporal attention.
2611.06120.summary: Anticipates participant roles, motion intensity and local changes, feeding back into object features and attention biases. Scores 77.51 on RBench (+3.29 over PhysisForcing) and strong EZS-Bench results.
2611.06120.why: Embodied video generation; moderately relevant to video world models.

2611.05936.tldr: $7, 2 g camera-free optical six-axis tactile sensor running at ~300 Hz.
2611.05936.summary: Uses spectrally encoded illumination through silicone and an MLP to reconstruct forces and moments with R^2 0.97-0.99. Demonstrated in tactile-guided manipulation and HRI.

2611.05793.tldr: One-step drifting generator produces multimodal short-horizon MPC cost corrections ranked by a critic.
2611.05793.summary: Models bimodal corrections in overtaking scenarios, trained from cost evaluations without differentiating through the optimizer. With eight candidates crashes 0.74% vs 3.4% for a regressor; single samples beat an MDN.
2611.05793.why: Generative models for MPC; small-scale but conceptually interesting.

2611.06544.tldr: Typed spatial Markdown world model for web agents.
2611.06544.summary: Represents UI state as typed spatial Markdown and trains a two-stage predictor. Raises a web agent's success from 22.9% to 37.6% on Online-Mind2Web.

2611.05893.tldr: Identity-preserving sequential video generation via prompt/frame anchoring and candidate routing; challenge winner.
2611.05893.summary: Combines semantic prompt anchoring, keyframe anchors and metric-based routing over generators. First place in both ACM MM 2026 tracks.

2611.05890.tldr: Agentic cellular world model for single-cell expression prediction, explanation and updating.
2611.05890.summary: Improves differential-expression AUPRC by 63% on SciPlex3 with large token savings.

2611.05825.tldr: Dual-image conditioned DiT for e-commerce videos preserving product and presenter.
2611.05825.summary: Separates product and human latents at sequence boundaries with region-weighted loss and condition dropout. Trained on 10K curated videos.

2611.06817.tldr: Open recipe scaling egocentric human-video pretraining of world-action models to 50k hours, finding log-linear scaling to robot success.
2611.06817.summary: Curates Open-HumanWAM-50K with hand motion and language annotations; HumanWAM-Vanilla pretrained on human video alone reaches 92.1% on RoboTwin Clean2Clean after post-training. Joint human-robot goal-conditioned pretraining reaches 84.6% on Clean2Random and shows in-context adaptation on real robots. Data, pipelines and checkpoints released.
2611.06817.why: Large open resource on learning from egocentric human data via world-action models.

2611.06296.tldr: Formulates smart-home multi-resident data association as an MDP solved with behavior cloning (Transformer or LLM).
2611.06296.summary: Outperforms baselines on three datasets, especially with concurrent events.

2611.06881.tldr: Simulation benchmark of six industrial-style variational automation tasks for agentic robotics with 33 reference skills.
2611.06881.summary: Built on Newton physics with standardized variations and difficulty tiers; baselines with Graph-as-Policy and Isaac Lab Arena.

2611.07881.tldr: TactileLab adds rigid-body 'tactile flow' shear simulation to IsaacLab for scalable RL, plus real-to-sim tactile translation for sim-to-real dexterous manipulation.
2611.07881.summary: Simulating tactile shear with soft-body physics is too slow for large-scale RL. TactileLab estimates dense tangential contact motion from rigid-body sim as a 'tactile flow' field alongside contact depth, pairs it with a long-horizon proprio+tactile policy architecture, and maps real tactile images to simulated flow/depth. Policies show emergent contact-aware behavior and deploy on real dual-arm and in-hand dexterous tasks across several sensor designs.
2611.07881.why: Directly on target: scalable shear-aware tactile sim and sim-to-real for in-hand dexterity.

2611.07551.tldr: PreSTP prunes redundant tokens across frames and denoising steps in few-step autoregressive video diffusion, training-free, for 1.5-3.2x speedups.
2611.07551.summary: Few-step AR video diffusion leaves little cross-step redundancy for caching. PreSTP uses early clean estimates to detect cross-frame and cross-step redundant tokens and skips their computation with mask reuse. It gets 1.52-3.20x speedup on 5s videos and up to 1.96x on 30s videos while improving VBench-Long, even in one-step regimes.
2611.07551.why: Engineering speedup for AR video diffusion; tangential unless you deploy video world models.

2611.07566.tldr: AGAVE shows MeanFlow's interval-integral target can absorb an arbitrary CFG guidance field, compiling time/space/frame-varying guidance into one-step video generation.
2611.07566.summary: One-step MeanFlow generators can only use a fixed CFG scale, yet optimal guidance varies with noise level and content. The interval-integrated CFG identity folds any guidance field into the MeanFlow training target with no discretization error; AGAVE adds a learnable temporal schedule, motion-saliency spatial modulation and frame asymmetry with fewer than ten scalars. It beats one-step baselines on VBench, UCF-101 and MSR-VTT and matches multi-step guided sampling.
2611.07566.why: Neat MeanFlow + guidance theory result, relevant to one-step generation interests.

2611.07712.tldr: AffectiveVLA gates VLA social-touch behaviors on a Unitree G1 with an RGB intent classifier, compliance profiles and voice-triggered safe stop.
2611.07712.summary: Social touch interactions (handshakes, hugs) need intent inference and safe contact. The authors collect ~1,300 VR-teleop episodes, fine-tune four VLAs (GR00T best) and add an intent model converting perceptions into prompts with low-confidence suppression. Intent gating raises macro-F1 from 0.75 to 0.90 with 6.27 ms p95 latency.
2611.07712.why: Systems integration for humanoid HRI; little methodological transfer to dexterous policy learning.

2611.08338.tldr: GPWM is a generative 3D particle world model combining flow matching and diffusion forcing across rigid, deformable, cloth and granular materials, enabling noise-space planning.
2611.08338.summary: Video world models model appearance, not 3D physics. GPWM is an object-aware multi-resolution transformer trained with flow matching plus diffusion forcing on a 25.5M-frame ParticleWorlds corpus, reducing prediction error 31% on average over the best per-domain baselines across six domains, with one unified model. Planning by searching the model's latent noise over joint actuator-object motion beats action-space search on contact-rich pushing and picking.
2611.08338.why: Generative world model for contact-rich manipulation with noise-space planning, close to your WM/GenModel interests.

2611.08577.tldr: Meituan's MR0 VLA trains on 15k robot hours with a discrete-to-flow-matching recipe, CFG-DAgger with 'Rollback' correction data, and async chunk merging.
2611.08577.summary: MR0 combines 147M vision-language samples and 15,060 robot hours over 12 embodiments with a three-stage recipe: discrete action-token pretraining, flow-matching mid-training, real-world post-training. Rollback pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections for positive/negative supervision in CFG-DAgger without value learning, and asynchronous chunk merging handles latency. It reaches 93.6% on RoboTwin 2.0, beats pi0.5 under matched HG-DAgger, and gets 70% on Ethernet insertion.
2611.08577.why: Industrial VLA recipe with useful details on CFG-based correction learning and async chunking.

2611.08458.tldr: Distills sim RL rollouts into a frozen flow-matching action decoder with latent task context, then learns only a visual-to-latent interface from few demos.
2611.08458.summary: Visual dexterous policies need many demos while sim RL with privileged info learns rich control. Latent RL Prior distills RL rollouts into a proprio- and latent-conditioned flow-matching decoder, then freezes it and trains a visual interface to its latent with action supervision only, also shareable across arms for bimanual tasks. It beats full fine-tuning of pi0.5 and GR00T N1.7 in low-data regimes and matches full-data baselines with 5-10x fewer demos in sim.
2611.08458.why: Combines RL-trained control priors with flow policies for data-efficient dexterity, a method you could use.

2611.08156.tldr: La-JEPA trains a compact policy from scratch in V-JEPA 2.1 feature space with auxiliary future-feature prediction, matching larger world-action models.
2611.08156.summary: World-action models inherit costly video-generation backbones. La-JEPA trains a policy transformer natively in frozen V-JEPA 2.1 features, predicting future features with actions during training and only actions at inference. It achieves SOTA on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO-Plus among non-embodied-pretrained policies, runs 2-5x faster than Fast-WAM, scales to 2.1B, and matches pi0.5 on four real tasks; JEPA features beat video VAE latents especially OOD.
2611.08156.why: Useful evidence that JEPA latents beat video VAE latents for control, relevant to V-JEPA world-model interest.

2611.08698.tldr: VICTR uses a demo-conditioned progress estimator to retrieve stage-matched demo chunks for in-context learning in a post-trained pi0.5.
2611.08698.summary: Retrieval-based ICL for VLAs relies on visual similarity, which misses execution stage. VICTR's In-Context Value Function Estimator predicts task progress conditioned on a reference demo video, and uses it to retrieve matching chunks for an ICL-trained pi0.5. On unseen OOD real tasks success rises from 6.2% to 23.8% and progress from 28.9% to 55.5%.
2611.08698.why: Interesting ICL angle for VLAs, though absolute success remains low.

2611.08413.tldr: T3R prunes VLA visual tokens via segmentation and biases attention toward salient regions, training-free, for speed and OOD robustness.
2611.08413.summary: VLAs process hundreds of visual tokens, wasting compute and inviting distraction. T3R does segmentation-guided token pruning followed by saliency-guided attention biasing. On LIBERO-Spatial it removes 85% of scene tokens with matched success, +7pp under OOD placement, and up to 3.3x LLM-forward speedup at higher resolution.

2611.07301.tldr: ArtiVidRM is a video reward model that first lists visible generation artifacts, then scores quality using them as rubrics, trained with multi-reward RL.
2611.07301.summary: Video RL needs interpretable, reliable rewards. ArtiVidRM follows observe-then-score: predict a structured artifact list, then use it as rubric for quality assessment, jointly optimized with coverage/efficiency and pairwise preference rewards. It reaches SOTA on video preference benchmarks and provides useful signals for video diffusion optimization.

2611.08664.tldr: ForPC trains a two-stage RL force-aware whole-body controller letting a Unitree G1 push carts with up to 30 kg payload.
2611.08664.summary: Cart pushing couples bimanual contact wrenches with balance. ForPC first trains a locomotion prior under varied hand loads, then a residual policy using inferred force and state latents without force sensors, with rewards penalizing internal opposition and slip. It cuts velocity RMSE up to 68.2% in sim and transfers zero-shot to a G1 pushing 30 kg at 0.5 m/s.
2611.08664.why: Humanoid loco-manipulation; tangential to dexterous hands.

2611.08209.tldr: RoboARCade benchmarks frontier multimodal agents directly acting as robot controllers on long-horizon MuJoCo manipulation tasks.
2611.08209.summary: Agentic robot control uses LLM agents as policies. RoboARCade provides harder long-horizon tasks across three embodiments with pluggable interfaces; GPT-6 Astra scores 49.8% vs 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1. Failures come mainly from strategy choice and imprecise execution, agents falsely claim success on 24-39% of subtasks, and one in-context demo raises Astra from 53.5% to 73.0%.
2611.08209.why: Informative snapshot of LLM agents as policies, but not your core direction.

2611.08128.tldr: FreeOcc factors out SE(2) ego-motion in a flow-matching 4D occupancy forecaster for efficient driving world modeling.
2611.08128.summary: Occupancy world models spend capacity disentangling ego-motion. FreeOcc explicitly factors ego-motion, runs attention-free temporal fusion and uses ODE solving only on uncertain voxels. With 28.3M params at 27 FPS it achieves SOTA on nuScenes (0.47 m NFCD, 32.1% mIoU) and transfers zero-shot to SemanticKITTI.

2611.08462.tldr: OopsieRecover infers the intent of a few corrective demos via abduction and encodes it as spatial costs that steer a VLA away from failures.
2611.08462.summary: DAgger-style recovery needs many corrections and generalizes poorly. OopsieRecover uses abductive reasoning over a handful of corrective demos to produce dense spatial representations and conditional costs that steer the VLA's action sampling. Across 6 tasks, a few corrections let the VLA recover in novel object, pose and scene variations.
2611.08462.why: Inference-time steering of VLAs with semantic costs; moderately relevant to policy steering.

2611.08576.tldr: Q-OIL models real human interventions as progress-triggered and adds optimistic bonuses on intervention transitions with decoupled critics for RL from interventions.
2611.08576.summary: Human-in-the-loop algorithms are developed with unrealistic simulated humans. From participant data, humans intervene when progress stalls and give suboptimal corrections; a progress-based human model better ranks algorithms. Q-OIL adds optimistic bonuses to intervention transitions with decoupled critics to prevent backup to pre-intervention states, gaining 10-50% success in sim and real and improving pretrained VLAs on two bimanual tasks.
2611.08576.why: Practical RL fine-tuning from interventions, including for VLAs.

2611.07532.tldr: S2C uses a VLM to localize task regions, then real-world human-in-the-loop residual RL with force feedback to learn robust contact-rich behaviors.
2611.07532.summary: Real-world RL overfits to scene appearance. S2C decomposes into VLM-based semantic focusing for coarse spatial guidance and residual HIL RL with force feedback for contact refinement, plus object-centric background augmentation. Across six real contact-rich tasks it outperforms baselines and remains robust to visual and positional variations.
2611.07532.why: Contact-rich real-world RL recipe; solid but incremental.

2611.07294.tldr: HME encodes motion into video diffusion noise via Householder reflections on channel vectors, preserving Gaussianity without costly noise-warp correction.
2611.07294.summary: Noise-warping for motion control breaks i.i.d. Gaussian noise and requires expensive correction. HME applies per-location orthogonal Householder transformations driven by motion, exactly preserving per-frame Gaussian structure while correlating frames. It matches or beats SOTA motion control with 2.7x speedup over noise warping.
2611.07294.why: Elegant noise-structure trick; mild relevance to noise conditioning ideas.

2611.08425.tldr: VLA-Tug probes VLA latent layers for early, calibrated failure detection with bounded error rates and failure-mode classification.
2611.08425.summary: VLAs need cheap, calibrated runtime monitors. VLA-Tug supervises a lightweight probe on pre-failure segments, improving early detection by up to 30% at matched FPR, keeping error bounds valid in up to 86% of runs on unseen tasks (vs 21%), and predicting failure modes (+44% top-3). A 3,180-episode annotated dataset is released.
2611.08425.why: Deployment monitoring for VLAs; moderately tangential.

2611.07513.tldr: Concertina generates continuous action tokens blockwise inside a shared diffusion VLM backbone with no separate action expert.
2611.07513.summary: Decoupled VLAs either discretize actions or bolt on an action expert. Concertina encodes each control step as a continuous latent token denoised by the diffusion VLM's own corrupt-and-reconstruct operator, using 0.21% action parameters in a 4.46B model. It reaches 98.15% on LIBERO, 85.9% on LIBERO-Plus and 4.142 on CALVIN ABC-D.
2611.07513.why: Interesting architectural take on unified diffusion VLAs; sim-only benchmarks.

2611.07275.tldr: LARBRID fine-tunes pretrained diffusion/flow policies via RL over initial noise using a linear-MDP representation bridging noise and action values.
2611.07275.summary: Noise-space RL fine-tuning of diffusion policies suffers 'noise aliasing' between noise and action values. The authors define a Latent Noise Linear MDP and derive a Bridge Equation aligning values via a shared noise-action representation, with near-optimal guarantees. LARBRID gives up to 2-3x performance gains on locomotion and manipulation tasks.
2611.07275.why: Directly in your noise-space steering of diffusion policies interest, with theory.

2611.08762.tldr: Robust adaptive Lyapunov-based MPC with RBF-network uncertainty modeling, validated on quadcopter attitude control.
2611.08762.summary: The paper derives adaptive laws with barrier Lyapunov functions and embeds them as contractive constraints in MPC for constrained nonlinear systems. It guarantees uniform boundedness and validates on HIL simulations and a custom quadcopter.
2611.08762.why: Classical control on drones; low relevance.

2611.07939.tldr: WAM-Sim anchors an autoregressive driving world model with hierarchical persistent memory and post-trains it with online flow-matching RL.
2611.07939.summary: Driving world models drift over long rollouts. WAM-Sim uses structural, scene and instance memory tokens and online flow-matching RL with visual rewards and a VLM physics judge. It achieves FID 3.47 / FVD 25.72 on nuScenes and reduces drift on minute-scale rollouts.
2611.07939.why: Driving-focused; memory and flow-RL ideas only loosely transferable.

2611.08654.tldr: CS-Pi enforces unseen inference-time constraints on flow policies via draw-project-renoise sampling that stays plausible under the policy.
2611.08654.summary: Gradient guidance fails on multimodal policies (averaging can pass through obstacles), rejection is slow and projection is implausible. CS-Pi projects each draw to the nearest safe action, renoises proportionally to the projection distance, and reruns the unmodified flow policy until safe. It reaches 81% safe success on a shelf pick-and-place and 55% on a Franka vs 55% and 40% for projection.
2611.08654.why: Clean, usable idea for constrained sampling from flow-matching policies.

2611.08407.tldr: Social Humanoid generates partner-reactive whole-body humanoid motion via token sequence modeling plus a tracking controller, with a 260-hour retargeted interaction dataset.
2611.08407.summary: Humanoids are trained as solitary agents. A high-level tokenized sequence model generates reactive robot motion and predicts occluded partner motion, executed by a low-level tracker on a G1. A two-phase adaptive retargeting procedure builds a 260-hour HHI benchmark from five mocap datasets.
2611.08407.why: Human motion retargeting for interaction; tangential to dexterity.

2611.07261.tldr: Empirical study of PPO stacks, observations and robustness for planar deformable linear object keypoint positioning with zero-shot sim-to-real.
2611.07261.summary: The study compares three PPO training stacks for one-end-grasped DLO manipulation, finding GPU MuJoCo Playground fastest, and relative keypoints plus asymmetric actor-critic helpful. With randomization, sim success is 88.8-98.0% and real trials 8-10/10.
2611.07261.why: Practical sim-to-real RL notes; narrow task.

2611.08669.tldr: ChainFlow is a few-step latent flow-matching drafter for LLM speculative decoding conditioned on target hidden states.
2611.08669.summary: AR drafters scale with draft length and diffusion drafters ignore token dependencies. ChainFlow transports compressed hidden states in one or two flow steps with feedback heads and tree drafting. On Qwen3.5 it beats EAGLE-3 by 39% and DFlash by 11% in vLLM.
2611.08669.why: Flow matching applied to LLM inference; tangential.

2611.08373.tldr: SLA continually pretrains pi0.5 with alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and a frozen 3D perception model's features across heterogeneous robot data.
2611.08373.summary: VLAs inherit 2D visual representations. SLA adds gated multi-layer visual-to-3D feature alignment during continual pretraining and post-training, using partial depth/calibration and state dropout, with no inference-time cost. The abstract reports the recipe but no headline numbers.
2611.08373.why: Relevant VLA training recipe for spatial grounding; results unclear from abstract.

2611.07403.tldr: Detects replay attacks on vision-based controllers with RL-adapted dynamic watermarking and an action-conditioned latent dynamics model.
2611.07403.summary: A private Gaussian watermark is added to controls, and a latent dynamics network predicts the resulting observation latents; discrepancies flag replay attacks. An RL policy tunes watermark covariance under safety penalties, evaluated on a UR5 reaching task.

2611.08240.tldr: FewStepRL systematically adapts diffusion RL objectives (FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, ReFL) to few-step average-velocity models via an x-space gradient decomposition.
2611.08240.summary: RL post-training of diffusion is dominated by many-step rollouts; few-step models predict average velocities incompatible with existing objectives. The authors express objectives in x-space, decompose gradients into self-regression toward an anchor plus reward augmentation, and compute anchors from few-step flow maps. Reward-gradient methods work best when gradients are affordable; otherwise DiffusionNFT-style methods reach high reward quickly.
2611.08240.why: Unifying view of RL for few-step/flow-map models, transferable to fast generative policies.

2611.07417.tldr: MessyNav uses VLM affordance reasoning to decide whether to swipe, pick or avoid obstacles for zero-shot interactive navigation.
2611.07417.summary: Interactive navigation in clutter needs context-aware decisions about which objects to manipulate. MessyNav runs VLM affordance reasoning before planning on a mobile manipulator, improving real-robot success by 27pp over the strongest baseline.
2611.07417.why: Navigation with VLM planning; low relevance.

2611.08939.tldr: RevoSim simulates 285 piezoresistive taxels and five visuotactile fingertips on the BrainCo Revo3 hand at up to 4,096 parallel envs.
