2611.08939.summary: Dexterous tactile RL needs fast multimodal tactile simulation. RevoSim jointly generates pressure, depth, RGB and marker-displacement signals for the Revo3 hand, scaling to 4,096 environments on one RTX 5090. In-hand manipulation and grasping policies are trained in sim; real transfer is left for future work.
2611.08939.why: Useful tactile-hand simulation infrastructure, but no sim-to-real yet.

2611.09096.tldr: Trajectory Forcing conditions autoregressive video diffusion on previous chunks' full denoising trajectories rather than only final predictions.
2611.09096.summary: AR video diffusion discards the intermediate predictions of previous chunks. TraF uses denoising trajectories as context, trained first on pseudo-trajectories from Gaussian interpolation of ground truth, then on the student's own rollouts with a teacher. It scores 85.15 on VBench (+0.84 over Self Forcing) and has the best quality on 30-second (6x horizon) generation.
2611.09096.why: Fresh idea in the diffusion forcing / AR video line you follow.

2611.10148.tldr: BATCH aligns human and robot behaviors via cycle-consistent temporal representations, then co-trains an autoregressive video-action diffusion model with alignment and style transfer.
2611.10148.summary: Human demos differ from robot data in embodiment, viewpoint and timing. BATCH learns self-supervised cycle-consistent temporal correspondences between human and robot videos and uses them for behavior-aligned co-training and human-to-robot style transfer in a video-action diffusion model. On real tasks it generalizes better to unseen configurations than unaligned co-training and prior cross-embodiment baselines.
2611.10148.why: Learning from human demos with video-action diffusion, from Shuran Song's group.

2611.09672.tldr: ODEAction replaces action-chunk prediction with an ODE over action evolution time, generating actions recursively from the current action.
2611.09672.summary: Chunked VLA outputs create discontinuities at chunk boundaries. ODEAction learns an Action Transition Field and integrates it from the current action to produce subsequent actions with explicit dependencies, as a modular action head. On LIBERO, EBench, RoboTwin and real robots it improves success and trajectory smoothness over chunk-based baselines, especially for fine manipulation.
2611.09672.why: Directly challenges action chunking, reminiscent of streaming flow policies.

2611.09124.tldr: A2-MEAS couples a history- and world-model-augmented VLA with learned 'correction codes' from a MetaBrain agent for failure recovery, topping BEHAVIOR 2026.
2611.09124.summary: Sustained autonomy needs efficient control and recovery. A2-WLA adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a VLA; correction codes combining language, spatial evidence and history are distilled into weights or applied at test time. It gets 0.6411 Q-score on all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 tasks, 95.05% on RoboTwin 2.0, 57.92% vs 26.67% for pi0.5 on 12 real tasks, and 4x training throughput.
2611.09124.why: Big systems result with strong numbers; history-conditioning and recovery are relevant pieces.

2611.08872.tldr: Lodos is a parallel rigid-body simulator built for fast detailed mesh-mesh contact, about 10x throughput over existing simulators.
2611.08872.summary: Parallel simulators rely on primitive collision approximations; mesh-mesh collisions slow throughput. Lodos redesigns broadphase, narrowphase and contact dynamics, matching established simulators in faithfulness with roughly an order of magnitude higher throughput in the detailed mesh setting.
2611.08872.why: Could matter for contact-rich dexterous sim with complex geometry.

2611.08827.tldr: ActPrune prunes VLA visual tokens before the encoder using the previous action chunk's projected end-effector and camera motion.
2611.08827.summary: Prior token pruning runs after encoding. ActPrune uses the previous action chunk as a geometric prior: keeping patches along the projected end-effector path in third-person views and dropping motion-compensated unchanged patches in wrist views. It gets up to 1.61x speedup and 59.5% FLOP reduction with negligible success loss on LIBERO, VLABench and four real tasks.
2611.08827.why: Clever but incremental VLA efficiency trick.

2611.09625.tldr: TT-MBRL encodes episodic memory into world model weights via test-time gradient descent, setting SOTA on Memory Maze.
2611.09625.summary: MBRL struggles with long-term memory. TT-MBRL fine-tunes the world model per episode at test time to store observations in parameters rather than context. It improves across architectures on Memory Maze 2D, sets SOTA on 3D Memory Maze, and keeps performance on DMC and Atari 100k.
2611.09625.why: Interesting test-time-training angle on world-model memory.

2611.09371.tldr: DrilDICE uses distributionally robust BC with DICE stationary-distribution correction to handle covariate shift from arbitrary data distributions.
2611.09371.summary: BC fails when expert data come from biased or incomplete state distributions. DrilDICE derives a feasible distributionally robust BC objective using stationary distribution correction ratio estimation. It outperforms offline IL baselines across diverse covariate-shift scenarios.
2611.09371.why: Principled BC robustness idea; benchmarks likely low-dimensional.

2611.08987.tldr: VLA Handover runs a small on-robot VLA and switches to a large server VLA only when failure is predicted, to save network requests.
2611.08987.summary: Querying a server VLA every chunk limits robots per server. A heuristic switching framework uses SmolVLA locally and pi0.5 remotely, improving success 11-22pp over SmolVLA alone with 49-77% fewer requests than server-only at 2-4pp lower success on LIBERO.

2611.10137.tldr: A unified inertial encoder trained on human and retargeted humanoid IMU synthesis transfers zero-shot to Unitree G1 velocity estimation and motion-text retrieval.
2611.10137.summary: Humanoid state estimation data is limited by robot repertoire. The encoder synthesizes IMU signals at corresponding body sites for humans and retargeted humanoids, jointly training velocity estimation and motion-text alignment with randomization. It achieves 0.099 m/s velocity error on a real G1 without real robot data.

2611.09684.tldr: SURE trains VLAs with a probabilistic transposed-conv action decoder over bins and Soft-DTW chunk alignment to model spatial and temporal demo variability.
2611.09684.summary: Pointwise action supervision ignores that nearby actions and different speeds are equally valid. SURE models spatial uncertainty via local correlations among action bins and temporal variations with Soft-DTW alignment. With 10% of demos or 20% of steps it matches or beats baseline VLAs on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0 and real tasks.
2611.09684.why: Data-efficiency idea related to action representation; moderately relevant.

2611.08920.tldr: HOC2R extracts hand-object contact trajectories from human videos with frozen DINOv3/SAM 2.1 features for robot motion transfer.
2611.08920.summary: Human videos lack robot-usable motion cues. HOC2R adds learned heads for hand-object association and contact localization, supporting contact counting in untrimmed videos and two-finger contact localization. It improves contact-count accuracy from 58.1% to 71.4% and halves localization error vs adapted VRB2, succeeding on 3 of 6 robot sequences.
2611.08920.why: Human-video-to-robot contact extraction; relevant to learning from human data but gripper-focused and modest results.

2611.09795.tldr: AR-Edit enables training-free, inversion-free streaming video editing by caching and injecting source attention values in DMD-distilled AR video diffusion.
2611.09795.summary: Training-free video editing assumes offline access. The authors find queries/keys stay stable across denoising while values carry content in distilled AR models, so caching source values from one pass reconstructs input without inversion. AR-Edit enables real-time streaming editing with better preservation across AR backbones.

2611.08904.tldr: MotionCore drives a controllable video diffusion model with a learned latent rigid-body dynamics simulator to improve physical consistency.
2611.08904.summary: Video models produce physically inconsistent motion. MotionCore learns a latent neural PDE-like simulator of object states whose predictions become spatial controls for video diffusion, with a decodability constraint preserving trajectories. It improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience at comparable visual quality on rigid-body benchmarks.
2611.08904.why: Physics-grounded video generation; loosely related to world models.

2611.12940.tldr: Thesis applying Q-learning and model-based offline RL (CQL, MOPO) to cancer chemotherapy scheduling on colon cancer clinical data.
2611.12940.summary: The work surveys RL for dynamic treatment regimens, simulates chemotherapy with Q-learning, and builds a model-based offline RL scheduler using CQL and MOPO on real colon cancer data. The model is presented as decision support for oncologists.

2611.09892.tldr: Apple's AMP1 harness lets a generalist AI model directly command manipulators, outperforming VLAs and WAMs zero-shot in sim and on 104/108 real trials.
2611.09892.summary: The paper argues generalist agents can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies. AMP1 provides no motor skills yet reaches 85.6% zero-shot on RoboLab-120 vs 49.2% for the best VLA, succeeds on 104 of 108 real trials (15-20x fewer failures), and with cross-episode memory cuts RoboDojo bimanual failures 4.6x.
2611.09892.why: Provocative challenge to the VLA paradigm; worth knowing even if far from dexterous control.

2611.18702.tldr: SN-TRV transfers adversarial robustness updates from source tasks to target VLA visual encoders without target adversarial training.
2611.18702.summary: VLA adversarial defenses usually need task-specific training. Averaged source defense updates with norm calibration are applied to the target encoder, improving robustness across three backbones and raising physical-patch success on PiPER from 20.3% to 45.8%.

2611.09041.tldr: DobotTrack is a 0.8B target-grounded VLA for language-guided embodied person tracking with auxiliary grounding and identity-preserving history compression.
2611.09041.summary: Embodied person tracking needs target identification and consistent following. DobotTrack adds mask/box grounding supervision and a Q-identity history compression module, reaching 77.9% on EVT-Bench (+16.9pp), and releases a quadruped tracking dataset.

2611.08895.tldr: Mechanistic study finds OpenVLA ignores negated instructions and localizes where its goal representation can be edited.
2611.08895.summary: Using LIBERO-Goal, OpenVLA executed the forbidden task in 79% of negated rollouts. Activation patching shows goals depend on instruction tokens before layer 12 and on the last prompt token after layer 16; steering at layer 8 redirected 12/18 rollouts while later fixed vectors redirected none of 158. Goal probes detect non-compliance better than failure detectors.
2611.08895.why: Nice interpretability analysis of VLAs, but OpenVLA-specific.

2611.08977.tldr: Energy-Based Reasoners frame looped latent reasoning as gradient descent on a learned energy, with exploration-based training, hitting 99.9% on Sudoku-Extreme.
2611.08977.summary: Looped models lack a measure of progress. EBRs learn an energy over latent states, iterate gradient descent on it with an energy-based stopping signal, and use exploration-based training to shape the landscape. They match or beat recurrent reasoners with 345x less inference compute on Sudoku-Extreme and achieve SOTA solution coverage on multi-solution tasks.
2611.08977.why: Relevant to energy-based / equilibrium-style generative modeling interests.

2611.08917.tldr: PRISM stores skills as frozen LoRA action-expert primitives and composes them via a per-chunk VLM router for retentive VLA adaptation.
2611.08917.summary: Shared fine-tuning gives no locus for reusable skills. The authors find per-skill LoRA updates occupy a distinguishable low-dimensional subspace, then build a primitive bank with skill residuals and a router supervised by an action-derived oracle. On RoboCasa365 it gets 56.43% atomic and 20.00% composite success vs 17.86%/17.50% for pi0.5-LoRA.
2611.08917.why: Modest gains on continual VLA adaptation.

2611.10316.tldr: Derives energy lower bounds for latent world-model rollouts and proposes a near-memory accelerator chip for embedded world-model planning.
2611.10316.summary: Profiling a DreamerV3 RSSM shows rollouts are memory-bandwidth bound and GPUs use ~5.9e10 times the CMOS energy floor, with thermal issues. WMPA combines near-memory compute, entropy estimation, variable precision and copy-on-write scratchpads, targeting 40x lower power.

2611.09679.tldr: Trains an RL camera-placement policy on a 6-DoF arm in CFD-based simulation for autonomous particle image velocimetry, transferring zero-shot to a water tunnel.
2611.09679.summary: PIV quality depends on camera placement. An RL agent observing only estimated velocity fields controls the arm to locate and frame hydrofoil wakes, trained in photorealistic CFD simulation. Real deployment resolves wakes at higher resolution in about half a full scan's time.
2611.09679.why: Novel application of sim-to-real RL; off-topic.

2611.09293.tldr: MDF++ is a visuo-tactile world-action model learning multisensory latents end-to-end with a diffusion backbone, beating frozen-encoder WAMs on contact-rich tasks.
2611.09293.summary: WAMs use frozen reconstruction encoders poorly suited for control. MDF++ learns visuo-tactile representations end-to-end with a multi-task strategy exploiting cross-modal correlations to avoid collapse. On real bolt screwing and nut mating it outperforms frozen-representation WAMs by up to 50%.
2611.09293.why: Tactile + world-action modeling for contact-rich manipulation.

2611.09894.tldr: Video-Coder trains a coding agent with SFT and agentic RL to build 3D draft scenes that guide downstream video generators.
2611.09894.summary: Video generators lack precise structure and motion control. Video-Coder writes code to render dynamic 3D draft videos, trained with execution and video rewards with annealing. It improves Minimax-H3 by ~7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 on VBench-2.0.

2611.09417.tldr: Future-informed actor-critic conditions the critic on action-dependent future features and derives a corresponding policy gradient.
2611.09417.summary: Prior hindsight critics only use exogenous future features. The authors define a future-informed value function that can condition on endogenous features and derive an unbiased future-informed policy gradient. It outperforms standard actor-critic under noisy and sparse rewards.

2611.09355.tldr: HiMEM consolidates, prunes and composes episodic/semantic memories for VLAs, lifting pi0 on LIBERO from 91.88% to 98.20%.
2611.09355.summary: VLA episodic memories are noisy with scene details. HiMEM synthesizes semantic memories, prunes redundant episodes and composes memories across scenarios. Gains are shown on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus across backbones.
2611.09355.why: Memory for VLAs on saturated benchmarks; low priority.

2611.09290.tldr: Two-timescale Q-learning reformulates safe RL as risk-sensitive control plus average cost, with convergence guarantees.
2611.09290.summary: The paper transforms safety-constrained RL into a risk-sensitive problem combined with average reward and solves it with two-timescale Q-learning. Convergence is proven and validated on GridWorld and Safety Gymnasium CarGoal.

2611.10169.tldr: Capturability-aware sequential MPC with rectangular safe corridors gives recursively feasible LIP footstep planning for humanoids in clutter.
2611.10169.summary: The method combines obstacle avoidance via intersecting rectangle corridors with capturability constraints, guaranteeing recursive feasibility and switching to in-place walking when blocked. Validated in Digit simulations with horizon-insensitive performance.

2611.09036.tldr: ToolDex is an ego-exo multi-camera human demonstration dataset of creative tool use with hand, tool and object annotations and benchmarks.
2611.09036.summary: Real-world creative tool-use data is scarce. ToolDex records humans selecting and repurposing objects as tools with egocentric plus eight exocentric cameras, annotating hands, tools, targets and deformable interactions. Benchmarks cover tool-use reasoning, sparse-view 3D/4D reconstruction and robot policy learning.
2611.09036.why: Human hand-object data source for dexterous tool use.

2611.10410.tldr: SimDuoReal shows bimanual dexterous behaviors (regrasp, in-hand adjustment, handover) emerge from one object-centric RL reward, distilled into one real-world policy.
2611.10410.summary: Hand-designing bimanual arm-hand coordination is task-specific. RL policies trained with a shared object-pose reward across varied environments discover pre-grasp, regrasp, in-hand adjustment and handover; experts are refined on transitions and distilled with DAgger and RL into a single policy. On hardware it succeeds in 61/80 (76.3%) trials across four tasks with unseen objects, and 85.0% vs 60.4% on sim barcode scanning.
2611.10410.why: Squarely in core interests: emergent bimanual dexterity with sim-to-real.

2611.10343.tldr: GUARD steers diffusion/flow policies with gradients of a Q-function trained on sparse rewards plus dense anomaly scores from the policy's training distribution.
2611.10343.summary: Generative policies drift into unsupported states under covariate shift. GUARD learns anomaly scores from training data, propagates them with sparse task rewards through a Q-function, and uses its gradients to steer denoising without modifying the base policy. It reaches 96.0%/80.0% on Adroit under nominal/perturbed dynamics (+21/+20pp) and gains 40 and 25pp on real in-hand screwdriver rotation and reorientation.
2611.10343.why: Q-steering of generative policies for dexterous in-hand tasks with sim-to-real, core RLGen + Dex.

2611.10894.tldr: RAGu retrieves geometrically warped in-the-wild DROID trajectories and uses them to guide a VLA's flow-matching inference in new domains.
2611.10894.summary: VLAs break under small domain shifts. RAGu calibrates source demos into the target setup, does coarse-to-fine retrieval of the trajectory most compatible with the base VLA, and guides flow-matching sampling instead of retraining. It lifts real-world VLA success from 20% to 80% and beats related baselines in sim and cross-embodiment humanoid settings.
2611.10894.why: Training-free guidance of flow-based VLAs via retrieval; usable idea.

2611.10872.tldr: DreamVLA turns generated human motions into RL-tracked humanoid trajectories and distills them into VLAs with reference-conditioned DAgger.
2611.10872.summary: Humanoid whole-body teleop data is costly. DreamVLA uses generated motions as references for sim RL, then distills to a VLA with a DAgger variant that restarts the RL expert from failed learner states with the same reference suffix. Evaluated on humanoid picking, drawer opening, button pressing and walk-and-pick, with ablations.
2611.10872.why: Synthetic-motion-to-policy pipeline; humanoid focus, sim only.

2611.10993.tldr: DPDP replaces a diffusion planner's behavior prior at execution with a value-optimized diffusion policy, composing scores to execute plans with valuable actions.
2611.10993.summary: Diffusion policies are value-aware but myopic; diffusion planners are far-sighted but execute with behavior-only inverse dynamics. Treating the executor as a posterior, DPDP swaps in a value-optimized diffusion policy prior, sampled training-free by composing scores with Langevin correction or amortized via a preference objective. On D4RL it improves its base planner, matches reactive diffusion policies on locomotion and leads on long-horizon navigation.
2611.10993.why: Principled score composition for diffusion RL, from Mingyuan Zhou's group.

2611.10490.tldr: Controlled real-world study shows two cheap fingertip tactile arrays in a visuotactile ACT policy outperform adding wrist cameras on contact-rich tasks.
2611.10490.summary: Contacts are often hidden even from wrist cameras. Holding demos and architecture fixed across three contact-rich tasks, wrist cameras add 18.3-28.3pp over scene vision while tactile instead adds 31.7-60.0pp and beats vision-with-wrist on all three tasks. Six task families including insertion, occluded retrieval and tool use are evaluated.
2611.10490.why: Careful sensing ablation directly informing tactile policy design.

2611.10677.tldr: FOCAL uses feasibility-partitioned behavior-regularized policy gradients with a CVAE actor and feasibility-scaled latent prior for safe offline RL.
2611.10677.summary: AWR in safe offline RL amplifies value errors exponentially. FOCAL trains a CVAE actor with first-order objectives that increase return on feasible transitions and reduce violations on infeasible ones, adjusting latent prior scale by feasibility at inference. Theory shows linear vs exponential error dependence, and it satisfies constraints on all DSRL tasks with competitive returns.

2611.10967.tldr: BAT-WAM bridges vision, hand joint states and whole-hand touch in a world-action model with separate codebooks linked by an RGB-conditioned latent bridge.
2611.10967.summary: Dexterous WAMs need hand state and contact, which may be missing. BAT-WAM learns tactile and action codebooks connected via a continuous RGB-conditioned bridge, reducing tactile reconstruction RMSE by 34.7-38.8% vs HandTouch and future tactile RMSE by 85.6% vs OpenWAM. Real-robot dexterous experiments show gains including on unseen objects and scenes.

2611.10647.tldr: Controlled study finds a small contact-statistics-selected taxel set matches dense uniform tactile coverage for dexterous RL policies across three hands.
2611.10647.summary: Uniform taxel placement is an untested default. With teacher, training and candidates fixed, few taxels chosen from contact statistics match many uniform ones, rarely contacted taxels equal no tactile input, and tensor layout doesn't matter even for CNNs, on in-palm rotation and grasping with three hands. The authors distill reporting guidelines for tactile policy studies.
2611.10647.why: Rigorous 'understanding' paper on tactile design for dexterous hands.

2611.10949.tldr: Vine sampling (querying the demonstrator k times from the same state) makes distilled diffusion policies truly multimodal rather than memorizing one action per observation.
2611.10949.summary: Sliding-window BC data can be fit by a high-Lipschitz unimodal policy, so diffusion policies memorize. Querying the demonstrator multiple times from identical observations resolves this; larger k better matches the conditional distribution on a synthetic task. On 2D truck unloading it yields a closer policy and substantially improves best-of-N and expert iteration.
2611.10949.why: Sharp insight on diffusion policy multimodality vs memorization, relevant to RL fine-tuning and search.

2611.10451.tldr: Grip, Trace, Write learns freely-held-pen handwriting with a two-branch actor, BC initialization and force-aware RL in simulation.
2611.10451.summary: Robot handwriting usually mounts the pen rigidly. This work couples grasp retention, tip motion and contact force: a grasp controller, BC from IK demos and RL with ink/force/time/retention rewards. The policy improves completion, precision and force regulation and generalizes to unseen English and Chinese text.

2611.10877.tldr: Unifies predictive sampling, MPPI, CEM and variants as one Sequential Monte Carlo algorithm with proposal, update and resampling axes.
2611.10877.summary: Sampling-based MPC is treated as distinct algorithms. Framing them as SMC with three design axes, resampling cuts collisions 30% at long horizons, and programmable proposals raise push-T success from 1% to 100% in sim and 10% to 90% on a Franka FR3.
2611.10877.why: Clean unifying view of MPPI-style control with real contact-rich results.

2611.10660.tldr: DIAL trains latent world models with rollout alignment and inverse dynamics, then uses inverse+forward rollouts to initialize CEM planning.
2611.10660.summary: Teacher-forced latent dynamics mismatch planning, and CEM starts from goal-agnostic proposals. DIAL aligns autoregressive rollouts, adds multi-step inverse supervision, and initializes CEM with a dynamics-informed action sequence. It beats latent world model and planning baselines on four visual control benchmarks.

2611.10635.tldr: Model-based IL learns a monocular collision-risk model and scene-dependent cost weights from demos for trajectory-optimization navigation.
2611.10635.summary: End-to-end navigation encodes safety implicitly. The method learns a worst-case clearance distribution from images and candidate controls, used as a risk cost, with imitation learning tuning cost balance and warm starts. It substantially lowers collision rates across embodiments.

2611.10443.tldr: SPARK-VLA distills 3D-expert attention into a LoRA visual branch and routes action-relevant tokens, with only 53M trainable params.
2611.10443.summary: VLAs need 3D understanding without external 3D inputs at inference. SPARK-VLA preserves the original visual pathway, adds a distilled spatial LoRA branch, and routes tokens using action-loss-gradient supervision. It performs strongly on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, CALVIN and real tasks with a 0.5B backbone.

2611.10553.tldr: MetaBFM combines behavior foundation models with meta-RL to adapt to new rewards and environments via exploration and zero-shot reward inference.
2611.10553.summary: BFMs support zero-shot RL in fixed environments, while meta-RL handles novel environments with supervised tasks. The authors identify four challenges to extend BFMs and propose MetaBFM, mixing supervised reward-following with unsupervised learning and interpolating exploration and reward inference at test time. It recovers in-distribution meta-RL performance while generalizing to new rewards.
2611.10553.why: Conceptual RL bridge; limited manipulation relevance.

2611.10965.tldr: Multi-task Gaussian process framework for target-aware source selection in offline Q-learning with contraction and performance bounds.
2611.10965.summary: Indiscriminate transfer causes negative transfer in offline RL. The method uses predictive evidence and MMD to select sources and posterior uncertainty for conservative updates, proving minimax rates under conditions. Simulations and human decision data show reduced negative transfer.

2611.10750.tldr: AERO routes RLHF preference queries to the oracle only where an ensemble reward model disagrees, using synthetic labels elsewhere.
2611.10750.summary: Preference labels dominate RLHF cost. AERO uses ensemble vote entropy with adaptive thresholds in a Dyna-style online RLHF loop, reducing oracle queries while matching online DPO and active-exploration baselines.

2611.10712.tldr: GPU-parallel orbital propagator plus curriculum DRL learns low-thrust multi-revolution spacecraft rendezvous guidance.
2611.10712.summary: A tensorized J2-perturbed propagator gives 67x throughput, and curriculum training in equinoctial elements learns robust rendezvous, robust to eclipses, also warm-starting trajectory optimizers.

2611.11023.tldr: Review and edge-centric framework for partitioning LLM/VLA inference across robot, edge and cloud over WiFi/5G.
2611.11023.summary: The article reviews collaborative inference and measures latency-optimal partition points for ResNet-101, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and OpenVLA-7B between Jetson devices and an AGX Thor edge server.

2611.10870.tldr: Proves an online-vs-offline imitation separation for stabilizing Vlasov-Poisson plasma and proposes a DAgger-style partially observed controller.
2611.10870.summary: BC errors compound exponentially in this unstable system, while online IL loss polynomially controls stability. A DAgger-style method under macroscopic measurements stabilizes a 1D plasma longer than BC.
2611.10870.why: Neat compounding-error theory, but plasma application.

2611.10806.tldr: WARP-JEPA replaces test-time gradient planning in frozen hierarchical JEPA world models with learned multi-candidate trajectory proposers.
2611.10806.summary: H-JEPA planning spends up to 97.7% of runtime on gradient optimization. WARP-JEPA trains a world-model-in-the-loop transformer and residual MLP proposers with rollout costs and best-of-K BC, giving 9.6-18.8x faster inference and up to +33.3pp success across 30 frozen models on four benchmarks.
2611.10806.why: Amortized planning for JEPA world models; relevant to V-JEPA interest.

2611.10392.tldr: LCWM-Bench unifies 15 datasets for language-conditioned world modeling; Tiresias plans with a diffusion policy proposer, ranker and video world model verification.
2611.10392.summary: Language-conditioned world modeling is fragmented. The benchmark pairs 142,987 episodes with 428,961 instructions across navigation, robotics, games and driving; Tiresias generates diffusion-policy candidates, ranks them, imagines with a video world model and visually verifies. It is competitive, with ablations showing complementary ranking and verification.
2611.10392.why: Benchmark-level contribution to video world models for planning.

2611.10682.tldr: Muscle-aware retargeting plus null-space exploration lets a value-guided flow policy control a 700-muscle whole-body model from monocular video.
2611.10682.summary: Kinematic references are hard for muscle dynamics and the action space is huge. MAR adapts references under constraints and NSE injects structured perturbations along the muscle-to-force null space. On 24 clips both solve every reference with half the samples and 44% lower joint error.
2611.10682.why: Musculoskeletal control with flow policy; tangential.

2611.10956.tldr: Distributional TD3 options-hedging agent trained on real S&P 500 data reduces CVaR tail loss vs delta hedging and simulated-market training.
2611.10956.summary: Using an empirical replay environment 1996-2017 and testing on 2018-2023, the agent cuts CVaR by 3.1% (8.9% in falling markets) but costs 7-10% in rising markets.

2611.10844.tldr: Practical book on RLVR post-training for language models: GRPO, failure modes, reward design and debugging lessons.
2611.10844.summary: It explains GRPO step by step and walks through five training programs (math, search agents, stability, MoE, SWE) with lessons, plus references on reward design, evaluation and infrastructure.
2611.10844.why: LLM RL; off-topic beyond general RL intuition.

2611.10769.tldr: Beam search over perturbed action chunks with simulator rollouts improves a frozen ACT policy on PushT, gated by a one-step-ahead check.
2611.10769.summary: Test-time search for chunking policies: beam search raises PushT success from 0% to 18%, and the OSA gate cuts runtime ~3x. Larger budgets don't consistently help; no VLA or real-robot evaluation.
2611.10769.why: Relevant idea but weak, sim-cloned evaluation.

2611.10638.tldr: Benchmarks class-weighted deep RL for IoT edge-cloud offloading against exact DP optima.
2611.10638.summary: Class-blind penalties stay 65-118% above optimum; corrected per-class rewards get within 0.13%. PPO is within 9-11% in small systems but 41-76% above optimum in larger ones.

2611.10448.tldr: ESTRA enables training-free 1-5% density sparse attention for video diffusion transformers via clustering and variance correction.
2611.10448.summary: Training-free sparse attention degrades at high sparsity. ESTRA computes exact attention on important keys found via query clustering and approximates the rest with corrected cluster representatives, achieving 3.26-4.71x speedups on Wan2.1-14B and HunyuanVideo-13B at 5% density.

2611.10938.tldr: BRACE infers a disturbance belief from prediction errors to condition a residual RL policy for reach-avoid quadcopter navigation.
2611.10938.summary: Spatially varying disturbances can exceed control authority. BRACE adapts the reference trajectory via nominal plus belief-guided residual terms, trained with likelihood-ratio reweighting, beating MPC and RL baselines in sim and Crazyflie hardware.

2611.11098.tldr: Zora accelerates autoregressive VLA inference with retrieval-based speculative drafting, kinematics-guided acceptance and a dedicated hardware core.
2611.11098.summary: AR VLA decoding is slow on edge platforms and neural draft models are costly. Zora drafts via retrieval exploiting robot dynamics, verifies with kinematics-guided acceptance and KV-cache sharing, and adds custom hardware for irregular retrieval. It gets up to 3.4x software and 7.6x hardware speedups on LIBERO with comparable accuracy.
2611.11098.why: Hardware/AR-VLA efficiency; tangential to diffusion/flow policies.

2611.11136.tldr: Auto-generates game environments and programmatic expert demos to train a 4B VLA (Script2Play) on Minecraft/Roblox gameplay via BC.
2611.11136.summary: An LLM agent builds executable game tasks targeting skills, and privileged-state experts produce aligned instructions, observations and keyboard/mouse actions. BC on 150.3 hours of synthetic gameplay yields a policy that follows instructions and generalizes across engines.

2611.11166.tldr: DexForesight distills an action-conditioned 3D hand-point and scene world model into dexterous policy latents, dropping depth and future prediction at deployment.
2611.11166.summary: Dexterous policies need spatial foresight including occluded fingers. DexForesight trains a world model predicting 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes from depth, hand kinematics and demos, then aligns policy queries to its frozen predictive queries. It lifts DexJoCo success from 49.4% to 60.5% over 11 tasks and reaches 58.3% vs 50.0% on three real dexterous tasks.
2611.11166.why: Dexterous policy with implicit world-model foresight, core interest.

2611.11220.tldr: EbbFlow schedules MeanFlow's diagonal vs interval temporal sampling as a PINN-style curriculum, improving one-step ImageNet FID from 44.82 to 39.65.
2611.11220.summary: MeanFlow's fixed temporal sampler mixes boundary (diagonal) and differential-consistency (interval) supervision. Viewing them as PINN collocation points, EbbFlow starts with diagonal supervision and progressively expands left-anchored intervals, leaving loss, target and inference unchanged. On ImageNet 256 DiT-B/2 without CFG it reaches FID 39.65 (1-NFE) and 36.02 (2-NFE) vs 44.82 and 39.86, though a fixed full-horizon variant does better at 1-NFE.
2611.11220.why: Practical MeanFlow training insight, relevant to one-step generation interest.

2611.11452.tldr: SemanticKV compresses KV caches in agentic AR video generation by retaining entries most attended by planner-extracted semantic constraints.
2611.11452.summary: Growing KV caches burden agentic AR video generation. SemanticKV groups queries by constraint-related positions via text cross-attention and keeps top-k entries by max-over-groups attention, bounding worst-group discarded attention. On Causal Forcing at 0.7 compression it matches full KV quality with 1.22x speedup and 3.35x memory reduction.

2611.11089.tldr: Formulates asynchronous chunked policy execution as tracking control to generate smooth targets, plus variance-based adaptive action skipping for faster execution.
2611.11089.summary: Vision-based policy execution is limited by inference latency. The authors generate continuous targets from discontinuous asynchronous predictions via a tracking-control formulation and skip actions when predicted-position variance is low. With ACT and OpenVLA-OFT on a bimanual robot, execution speeds up substantially while keeping high success.
2611.11089.why: Practical take on real-time chunk execution, related to real-time chunking.

2611.12978.tldr: TRD combines distribution matching and teacher-trajectory supervision via a momentum-mixture policy in one student pass for one-step flow distillation.
2611.12978.summary: Trajectory alignment degrades at tiny budgets while distribution matching needs an extra score network. TRD's single-pass momentum-mixture policy acts as one-step generator, student marginal velocity estimator and trajectory-supervised velocity field. On SANA-1.6B and SD3.5 it beats consistency and DMD baselines in quality and efficiency, with some diversity loss.
2611.12978.why: One-step distillation method; relevant to fast generative policies.

2611.11521.tldr: K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with EKF inference and closed-form GECM training for data-efficient partially observed world modeling and MPPI.
2611.11521.summary: Learning world models from partial vector observations is hard. K-PWM uses bilinear latent dynamics enabling exact Gaussian belief propagation, EKF/smoothing inference without an encoder network, and closed-form EM updates. It achieves lower long-horizon error on partially observed MuJoCo tasks with less training time and competitive real-time tracking on Menagerie robots.
2611.11521.why: Structured world model for MPPI control; moderately relevant.

2611.11688.tldr: Streaming Failure Forecasting refits only the last linear layer of a VLA failure monitor after each episode using success labels.
2611.11688.summary: Frozen failure monitors decay after task or policy changes. SFF updates its readout per episode (2.18 ms on a Jetson CPU) and moves its alarm threshold only after successes, beating frozen and reset monitors on simulated drift and on 434 real SO-101 runs across four VLAs.

2611.11605.tldr: ScanDreamer conditions a Dreamer-style world model on an online 2D scan map for quadrotor navigation, reaching 96.3% success in Isaac Sim.
2611.11605.summary: Depth-camera quadrotors lack geometric memory. ScanDreamer builds a scan-memory map that conditions world model, actor and critic, defines a geodesic reward and adds a forward-cone penalty. It gets 96.3% success / 3.6% collision vs 59.6% / 28.8% for AirDreamer.

2611.11127.tldr: Engineering report transferring a 43-second Japanese festival dance from monocular video to a Unitree G1 via retargeting and RL tracking.
2611.11127.summary: The pipeline combines human mesh recovery, retargeting, sim RL tracking and ONNX deployment, with an eleven-version hardware ladder fixing artifact corruption, estimator drift and reference edits. It achieves rope-free 43-second routines and a 9.7-minute continuous performance.
2611.11127.why: Humanoid motion tracking case study; low relevance.

2611.11421.tldr: GenRM-Flow shows a preference-tuned flow model's velocity-error differences are an implicit process reward in noisy latent space.
2611.11421.summary: Video reward models ignore the generator's own generative capacity. From the KL-constrained optimal policy of offline preference objectives, the implicit reward is the relative velocity-prediction error difference, unifying DPO, IPO and RWR as paths to the same optimum. This generator-derived reward replaces VLM scorers in FlowAWR and improves video generation.
2611.11421.why: Theory linking flow matching and implicit rewards, transferable to RL with flow policies.

2611.11179.tldr: Shows CFG at the first (pure-noise) step causes speaker-similarity loss in few-step flow TTS; skipping guidance on step one recovers most of it.
2611.11179.summary: At pure noise the network returns the conditional mean, so guidance shifts all trajectories by a near-constant vector whose size grows with first-step length. First-step unguided sampling recovers 84-91% of the 2-step SIM loss on CosyVoice, and a midpoint variant matches the 10-step teacher on some decoders, with fewer NFEs.
2611.11179.why: Clean analysis of guidance in few-step flow sampling, applicable beyond speech.

2611.11500.tldr: ForeAct uses a pretrained video world model as a single-pass representation backbone with next-frame depth tokens for low-latency geometry-aware control.
2611.11500.summary: WAMs are costly due to iterative denoising and lack explicit geometry. ForeAct encodes only the clean current latent in one pass, with learnable tokens supervised by next-frame relative depth during training only. It gets 96.6% on LIBERO, 63.5% on SimplerEnv-Bridge and 74.4% over 90 real rollouts.
2611.11500.why: Efficient use of video world-model priors for policies.

2611.11697.tldr: SurgTAP-3D is a 520K-frame surgical video dataset with contact-aware pseudo-3D point tracks for instruments and tissue.
2611.11697.summary: A pipeline converts monocular surgical videos into 4D annotations via contact prompting, tool segmentation and bundle adjustment, producing 1.4M trajectories across procedures, with benchmarks on tracking and reconstruction.

2611.11050.tldr: Learns Floquet-constrained Koopman linear predictors via EDMD for MPC tracking of periodic orbits.
2611.11050.summary: Monodromy-matrix constraints from Floquet theory regularize least-squares EDMD, yielding physically consistent predictors used in MPC, evaluated on a periodically forced cartpole against data-driven baselines.

2611.11517.tldr: InfCoiL jointly RL-fine-tunes a flow-matching HOI planner and physics controller in closed loop, introducing Semantic Flow Policy Optimization.
2611.11517.summary: Planner-controller HOI systems keep the planner fixed. InfCoiL alternates RL fine-tuning of a morphology-aware flow planner and multi-morphology controller from shared rollouts; SFPO stochasticizes selected denoising steps with semantic covariance and uses group-relative sequence rewards. It beats open-loop hierarchical baselines on OMOMO.
2611.11517.why: RL fine-tuning of flow planners, though for character animation.

2611.11087.tldr: SoftPAT3D generates simulation-ready text-to-3D scenes with deformables in intersection-free equilibrium via rest-shape recovery and differentiable contact simulation.
2611.11087.summary: Generated deformable meshes lack rest shapes and materials. SoftPAT3D derives rest shapes from manufacturing, assigns materials, places objects and drives scenes to static equilibrium, correcting with grid search and adjoint optimization. All 65 prompts have no interpenetration, unlike other systems.

2611.11091.tldr: SURE selects which offline transitions to reward-label using successor features and reward-model uncertainty, with a suboptimality bound.
2611.11091.summary: In limited-feedback RL with retained labels, the bound splits into offline RL error and reward uncertainty. SURE picks uncertain rewards at states from which high-value states are reachable, reaching near full-feedback performance with few labels across domains.

2611.11554.tldr: Kimodo-Policy uses a frozen text-to-motion generator with ControlNet visual conditioning as the action backbone for humanoid loco-manipulation.
2611.11554.summary: VLA priors don't capture motion structure. Kinematic Action Models pretrain on whole-body motion; Kimodo-Policy adds ControlNet conditioning, a root-body-hand hierarchy and history-conditioned chunking. It gets 72.14% on HumanoidArena and 60% across eight real tasks with 92M trainable params.
2611.11554.why: ControlNet-style fine-tuning of motion priors; humanoid-focused.

2611.11601.tldr: Kinora is a versioned workflow system linking text-to-motion generation, retargeting and validation for robot motion authoring.
2611.11601.summary: The system connects motion generation, libraries, agent tools and G1 retargeting through versioned artifacts, evaluated with regression tests; it explicitly does not establish quality or hardware safety.

2611.11464.tldr: Challenge report: off-policy RL (AWR + RECAP) on a pi0.5 policy that is its own value function, plus Thompson-sampled inference parameters, wins RoboEval.
2611.11464.summary: The solution fine-tunes pi0.5 with advantage-weighted regression and RECAP on the official score, treating each rollout as a Thompson-sampling trial over ~20 inference parameters. Generic RL reaches 0.85 RDS in two days; with generated full-reward demos and recovery episodes it reaches 0.990 on held-out seeds.
2611.11464.why: Practical recipe for RL fine-tuning of VLAs.

2611.11242.tldr: DeepSoMo estimates soft-robot deformable motion from proprioception using latent dynamics with a self-supervised predictive constraint.
2611.11242.summary: Proprioceptive sensing gives only indirect access to deformable shape. DeepSoMo enforces latent states predictive of future observations, improving trajectory, orientation, shape and contact estimation over recurrent baselines in FEM simulation.

2611.11085.tldr: ObjectWorld introduces 3D full-object flow, a 1210-hour dataset, and a world model predicting dense full-object trajectories from image and task text.
2611.11085.summary: World models need an actionable intermediate representation supervisable at scale. Full-object flow assigns 3D trajectories over complete object surfaces incl. occluded parts, for rigid and deformable objects; a 1210-hour real+sim dataset with an annotation pipeline trains an image+text-conditioned flow predictor. It shows data-scalable prediction and downstream manipulation across scenes and embodiments.
2611.11085.why: Object-flow world models as an embodiment-agnostic interface, useful for learning from video.

2611.11650.tldr: FlowEval uses flow-matching loss disagreement on a few target demos to predict how much adaptation an embodied foundation model needs.
2611.11650.summary: Practitioners need to know how much target data to collect. FlowEval probes models with flow-matching objectives on successful target demos, distinguishing seen from unseen deployments across pi0.5, MolmoAct2, GR00T and DreamZero, and correlating with success gains when fine-tuning pi0.5 and GR00T on 17 RoboCasa tasks.
2611.11650.why: Useful training-free diagnostic for VLA fine-tuning.

2611.11516.tldr: Neutral world model trained on routine and accident videos corrects survivorship bias in driving world models.
2611.11516.summary: Driving datasets rarely contain collisions, so world models imagine benign futures. Mixing accident videos with box-guided training better anticipates collisions, and using it as an imagination engine selects better trajectories on NAVSIM.
2611.11516.why: Driving; off-topic, though the data-bias lesson generalizes.

2611.11438.tldr: ArmedAgent benchmarks safety risks (misuse, indirect prompt injection) of coding agents controlling robot arms zero-shot.
2611.11438.summary: Coding agents with web access can carry digital threats into the physical world. 36 tasks in 5 scenarios cover robustness, malicious use and injection in sim and on a real arm, revealing substantial risks for frontier models.

2611.11123.tldr: HARP-Bench evaluates manipulation policies in workspaces shared with active humans across cueing, contribution, interruption and co-presence.
2611.11123.summary: Benchmarks assume the robot is the only agent. HARP-Bench adds human-present task variants and a demo-generation pipeline; VLAs and IL methods struggle, and training on its demos helps in sim with partial real transfer.

2611.11330.tldr: TACA fixes tool-call credit suppression in agentic LLM RL with advantage projection, decision contrast and supervised replay.
2611.11330.summary: Agentic RLVR degrades tool use due to token imbalance and aggregation effects. TACA enforces nonnegative mean tool-token advantage and adds contrastive and replay signals, improving over MT-GRPO by 3.6-4.6pp on six benchmarks.

2611.12992.tldr: ZeroPoint is an energy-based decision model with a fixed zero-energy 'no option fits' state enabling abstention.
2611.12992.summary: Standard EBM energies are shift-invariant and lack a reference level. ZeroPoint fixes the empty answer at zero energy, letting abstention arise from ordinary likelihood training, slightly beating a learned rejection class.

2611.12806.tldr: LingBot-Touch is a tactile foundation model unifying piezoresistive, magnetic and visuotactile sensors into plug-and-play tokens for diffusion policies and VLAs.
2611.12806.summary: Heterogeneous tactile sensors have sensor-specific physics that fragment data. LingBot-Touch learns a unified, extensible tactile representation whose tokens plug into diffusion policy and VLAs such as pi0.5 and LingBot-VLA. Sim and real experiments across hardware platforms show substantial gains on complex dexterous tasks with low compute.
2611.12806.why: Cross-sensor tactile representation for dexterous policies, squarely in scope.

2611.12177.tldr: Embodied First Exam benchmarks coding agents controlling 47 robots across 1,156 tasks via direct control, code or self-trained policies.
2611.12177.summary: It is unclear whether coding agents can control diverse robots. The benchmark offers 35 suites including dexterous and whole-body tasks, with standard, realtime and privileged settings. The best agent (GPT-6 Astra in Codex) gets 34% on 456 core tasks in the standard setting.
2611.12177.why: Agentic robotics benchmark; tangential to policy learning.

2611.12383.tldr: PCTac is an open-source mechanochromic photonic-crystal fingertip whose hue field directly encodes load, boosting Diffusion Policy success on real tasks.
2611.12383.summary: Visuotactile sensors infer force indirectly from deformation. PCTac's structural-color hue changes repeatably with normal load; integrated into Diffusion Policy across 90 rollouts on three tasks, hue gets 75.6% vs 66.7% (PCTac RGB), 63.3% (Wedge RGB) and 32.2% (vision only).
2611.12383.why: New tactile hardware with policy-learning validation.

2611.11854.tldr: DASH decouples a slow VLM backbone from a fast flow-matching action head running asynchronously, holding 20 Hz control regardless of backbone size.
2611.11854.summary: In synchronous VLAs, bigger backbones mean stale observations and lower control rate. DASH runs System 2 and a System 1 flow head (with its own ResNet for fresh vision) as concurrent processes, trains with desynchronization and aggregates overlapping chunks. It keeps 20 Hz from 0.8B to 8B backbones vs 9.7 to 4.1 Hz synchronous with higher success, and improves real dexterous humanoid pick-and-place.
2611.11854.why: Relevant to real-time/async chunked execution for dexterous VLAs.

2611.12676.tldr: Case study fine-tuning pi0.5 for chess-piece moves on an SO-101, finding LR cool-down crucial, val loss unreliable, sim pretraining helpful and self-improvement methods unhelpful.
2611.12676.summary: The study varies data size, updates and sim vs real demos. A short learning-rate cool-down adds up to 31 points and is needed to compare checkpoints; validation loss and action error don't predict success; sim demos help when real data is scarce. Filtered BC, RECAP-style advantage conditioning, coaching and residual RL gave no measurable gain over BC.
2611.12676.why: Useful practical lessons and honest negative results on VLA fine-tuning.

2611.11798.tldr: PAIR contrastively aligns joint image-ray representations by robot proprioception for viewpoint-robust Diffusion Policy and VLA training.
2611.11798.summary: Viewpoint changes entangle appearance with task state. PAIR pulls together observations with similar robot states across viewpoints in an image+camera-ray representation, usable for DP training or VLA post-training. It beats BC without ray conditioning by 12.7pp in sim and 26.7pp in real under camera variation.
2611.11798.why: Practical robustness trick for diffusion policies.

2611.12017.tldr: BetaGrasp conditions a DP3 point-cloud diffusion policy on a grasp-taxonomy label to select grasp modes on a LEAP hand for climbing holds.
2611.12017.summary: The point-cloud encoder fails to distinguish holds, so unconditioned DP3 always produces a jug grasp (25% correct type) vs 94% with the label. On 80 hardware trials with a slip-force testbed, average slip force rises from 9.6 to 14.3 N and full slips drop from 44% to 10%.
2611.12017.why: Small but clear insight on mode collapse in dexterous diffusion policies.

2611.13030.tldr: APS-VLA learns a lightweight token-importance estimator with action and visual-transition supervision to prune VLA visual tokens.
2611.13030.summary: Heuristic token pruning ignores decision relevance. APS-VLA trains a Decision Influence Estimator with frozen backbone, matching full-input predictions and demos plus an auxiliary transition objective. On real dual-arm tasks latency drops from 137 to 93 ms (1.47x) at 61% vs 60% success.

2611.12824.tldr: DreamLander applies DreamerV3 to 6-DoF planetary entry-descent-landing guidance, landing within 2 m.
2611.12824.summary: Model-based RL generates guidance and control for powered descent from state observations, landing within 2 m at under 0.3 m/s.

2611.12286.tldr: VLA-MOPD consolidates flow-matching VLA specialists via on-policy distillation that supervises every intermediate ODE step at student-visited states.
2611.12286.summary: Merging task specialists is hard: RL gives sparse credit and offline/endpoint distillation misses student states and intermediate flow states. VLA-MOPD has the student roll out, queries routed frozen teachers at each visited observation and ODE state, and applies masked per-step matching with an optional reference term. It lifts LIBERO from 75.4% to 98.9%, RoboTwin 2.0 from 73.0% to 89.3%, and a real Piper from 70% to 90%.
2611.12286.why: On-policy distillation for flow policies; directly usable technique.

2611.11981.tldr: Thermo-VLA injects cold/hot thermal attributes into RGB tokens via language-conditioned residual modulation for temperature-aware manipulation.
2611.11981.summary: Thermal images treated as ordinary visual inputs limit temperature reasoning. The ThermoRes encoder decomposes thermal into attributes, achieving 0.86 success on four thermal tasks on a dual-arm G1, 18pp over pi0.5 with RGB-thermal input.

2611.12382.tldr: AutoVLA-D adds a discrete trajectory-geometric condition before continuous trajectory prediction in autonomous driving VLAs.
2611.12382.summary: Driving instructions describe actions rather than states. TrajCond learns discrete differential trajectories as an intermediate condition, improving continuous prediction on NAVSIM, nuScenes and NeuroNCAP.

2611.11887.tldr: Analyzes nearest-of-m (conditional IMLE) one-step world models on frozen DINO tokens as random-codebook distortion, with pre-registered predictions.
2611.11887.summary: One-step stochastic world models avoid flow-matching cost. With m=16, nearest-of-m covers enumerated futures better than 50-step flow matching at 1/30 latency and stays on-manifold; a random-codebook view predicts memorization, mode flattening and under-dispersion. Per-step matching cuts long-horizon error by a third on stochastic Push-T, though planning doesn't improve (reported negative).
2611.11887.why: Rigorous analysis of one-step generative world models vs flow matching.

2611.13160.tldr: Shows kNN retrieval of demo action chunks reaches 91.7% on LIBERO, and that fine-tuned VLAs mostly act as better retrieval keys.
2611.13160.summary: It's unclear how much LIBERO success needs generalization. Retrieval without training reaches 91.7% and degrades least under LIBERO-Plus; across nine VLAs, fine-tuning mainly makes the backbone a better retrieval key with actions staying close to demos. A Local Action Consistency metric tracks retrieval success and can guide key training.
2611.13160.why: Important 'understanding' paper questioning what VLAs and benchmarks measure.

2611.12111.tldr: GAP learns in simulation how to adapt dexterous piano-playing actions between executions via a gradient guidance network, transferring the prior to hardware.
2611.12111.summary: Sim-trained dexterous policies degrade on hardware and real adaptation is costly. GAP learns from paired executions how action adjustments affect performance and uses its gradients to adjust subsequent attempts. It gives ~2.4x the F1 gain of a fast-adaptation baseline in sim, generalizes to held-out pieces, and improves real F1 by 3.6-23% after ~7 minutes per piece.

2611.13013.tldr: FaST factorizes synthetic transition generation into state, action, dynamics, reward and terminal models, enabling best-of-N advantage-targeted action synthesis for offline RL.
2611.13013.summary: Diffusion generators like SynthER model transitions monolithically. FaST matches SynthER with TD3+BC/IQL while generating 90x faster, and best-of-10 action synthesis beats real data on 11/12 D4RL medium settings (+8.9 points avg).
2611.13013.why: Offline RL data augmentation; moderately relevant.

2611.12879.tldr: Grasping-the-Future is a flow-matching model of joint 3D hand-object motion trained with masked completion on 3D interactions reconstructed from internet videos.
2611.12879.summary: Anticipating hand and object motion requires 3D supervision. A unified flow-matching model with masked spatiotemporal completion handles forecasting, conditional hand/object prediction and goal-directed generation, with contact constraints. A scalable pipeline reconstructs interactions from internet videos; it outperforms released forecasters and retargets plausibly to a robot hand.
2611.12879.why: Human hand-object priors from video, relevant to learning dexterity from human data.

2611.12643.tldr: Uses simulated data only as a control variate to reduce variance in policy evaluation and actor-critic, avoiding sim-bias in the target.
2611.12643.summary: Mixing sim and real data biases solutions toward inaccurate simulators. The authors use simulation solely for variance reduction in policy evaluation, extend it to actor-critic and offline RL, and improve over mixing on MuJoCo.
2611.12643.why: Principled sim-real RL idea; small-scale evidence.

2611.11856.tldr: DeltaForge consolidates per-domain driving VLA fine-tunes into a post-hoc MoE via shared SVD basis and tiny domain deltas.
2611.11856.summary: Weight updates from the same base share structure; SVD separates a shared part and small domain parts, and routers over VLM and flow experts are trained on a proxy set. It approaches per-domain accuracy across six driving domains at near single-model cost.
2611.11856.why: Driving; idea of post-hoc MoE could transfer but off-topic.

2611.13182.tldr: Distills oracle RL policies into interpretable decision lists of linear motion primitives, then tunes them online with Augmented Random Search.
2611.13182.summary: Symbolic Imitation Learning approximates oracle performance across 20 RL tasks and exceeds it on 11 while producing parsimonious interpretable policies.

2611.12411.tldr: PhysOPSD uses executable simulation code as privileged context for on-policy self-distillation to improve physical plausibility in video generation.
2611.12411.summary: SFT has state mismatch and RL lacks physical rewards. PhysOPSD translates real scenarios into verifiable simulation programs and distills with dual-level privilege and controlled variations under shared noise, outperforming SFT and RL with only 3K samples.

2611.12069.tldr: MPEG-Diffusion generates video with mixed resolution via dual-resolution attention, a mixed decoder and self-selected HR regions, for up to 4.8x speedup.
2611.12069.summary: Mixed-resolution video generation suffered quality drops. Processing 30% of full tokens it speeds Wan2.1 14B denoising 4.8x with raters preferring it over prior methods in 90%+ of pairs.

2611.13204.tldr: GRF-MPC integrates live ground reaction force into a centroidal QP-MPC for an underactuated cable-driven rehabilitation stand trainer.
2611.13204.summary: Across ~300 trials with six participants, it reduces CoM error 19.6%, tracking error 24.1% and work 28.7% versus an 8-cable impedance baseline, solving in under 1 ms.

2611.12732.tldr: Adds backward-dynamics and inverse-dynamics latent losses to LeWorldModel, improving performance and planning efficiency.
2611.12732.summary: Decoder-free JEPA-style world models rely on forward prediction plus an entropy term. Sigma-LeWM adds backward and inverse dynamics predictors to structure latents, giving gains on world-model benchmarks and two simulated manipulation tasks.

2611.12678.tldr: Library of Hands keeps a world model frozen and corrects only the command-to-action map, identified from image pairs and cached for returning setups.
2611.12678.summary: Rotating commands by 90 degrees drops a LeWM planner from 77.5% to 7.8%. LoH infers the action best explaining observed changes through the frozen model and stores identified 'hands', raising success from 28.6% to 62.3% on three sim tasks with little cost when nothing changes.
2611.12678.why: Clever training-free adaptation for world-model planners.

2611.12251.tldr: RAIL trains privileged teachers in a contrastively learned latent shared with student observations so their behavior is reproducible by students.
2611.12251.summary: Teacher-student distillation suffers an imitation gap when teachers use unavailable information. RAIL constrains the teacher to a shared representation during training, reducing the gap without reward shaping or student RL and beating direct RL from raw observations, with zero-shot transfer to new tasks.
2611.12251.why: Relevant to privileged-teacher distillation used in dexterous sim-to-real.

2611.11821.tldr: DTO aligns text-to-image diffusion at inference by optimizing intermediate scores and noises directly, without backprop through the denoiser.
2611.11821.summary: Inference-time alignment usually needs costly backprop. DTO treats scores and noises as variables and uses Reward-Optimized Score Guidance interpolating with pretrained predictions, with a reward-improvement guarantee. It outperforms inference-time alignment baselines on three models and two benchmarks.
2611.11821.why: Inference-time steering idea possibly transferable to diffusion policies.

2611.11780.tldr: Shows planners exploit persistent round-to-nearest quantization error in low-bit world models; shared, redrawn dither fixes most damage.
2611.11780.summary: Low-bit world models can collapse planning success by up to 100 points even with small one-step error. The cause is error that persists across planner iterations and is shared across candidates; dither shared by candidates and redrawn each iteration recovers a median 95% of damage in TD-MPC2 and works in DINO-WM. A W8A4 TD-MPC2 runs rollouts 1.9-3.3x faster than FP32, with pre-registered hypotheses.
2611.11780.why: Insightful analysis of planner-model interaction, relevant to TD-MPC2 users.

2611.13113.tldr: Compares 24 intrinsic motivation objectives with three representation strategies for building reusable world models in model-based RL.
2611.13113.summary: Integrating curiosity, entropy and competency objectives into one MBRL framework, curiosity with observation reconstruction is strongest overall, and episodic plus lifelong novelty gives best zero-shot and few-shot transfer in compositional vision tasks.

2611.12739.tldr: Plant Orbiter uses video diffusion orbit cameras and 3D Gaussian Splatting to reconstruct and generate 3D plants from a single image.
2611.12739.summary: For digital phenotyping, it produces 3D plant splats from one image with the highest 3D F-score among baselines and supports text-to-3D plants.

2611.12162.tldr: State-of-the-art report on differentiable physics simulation, separating which object gradients refer to from how backward passes are realized, including contact.
2611.12162.summary: The report classifies methods by referent (executed computation, converged equation, continuous dynamics) and realization (autodiff, adjoint, custom), adds a contact taxonomy, measures four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost, and reviews when zeroth-order methods win, closing with a checklist and diagnostic tool.
2611.12162.why: Useful reference if considering differentiable sim for contact-rich control.

2611.14092.tldr: Generates diverse, physically executable dexterous robot demos by expanding human hand-object interaction sequences in simulation for VLA training.
2611.14092.summary: Teleoperated dexterous demos are costly and human HOI datasets usually only reproduce given interactions. DexSeed groups human sequences by grasp mode, retargets with InteractionMesh, augments arm trajectories across objects and placements, and realizes them under arm-tracking dynamics in physics sim to produce executable arm+finger actions with visuals for VLA training.
2611.14092.why: Directly on human-hand-data-to-dexterous-policy pipelines, a core interest.

2611.14815.tldr: Driving world model that jointly generates perspective and schematic BEV video so vehicle layout becomes part of the predicted future.
2611.14815.summary: Layout-conditioned driving video models need future trajectories of other vehicles as input. BirdDreams autoregressively generates perspective and rendered BEV video with joint attention between two video DiTs, making surrounding-vehicle motion predicted and reactive to ego actions.
2611.14815.why: Driving-specific; multi-view joint generation idea is only loosely transferable.

2611.14420.tldr: Extracts scene-free latent actions from frozen V-JEPA 2 frame-pair embeddings to train action-conditioned video world models from unlabeled video.
2611.14420.summary: Latent action models learned from scratch trade expressiveness for scene separation. OnlyAct starts from V-JEPA 2 embeddings of frame pairs, which already carry action information, and learns to extract action while discarding scene content, improving generalization to unseen domains.
2611.14420.why: Relevant to latent-action pretraining and V-JEPA-style world models for policy learning.

2611.14383.tldr: A tutorial casting most of ML (generative, discriminative, representation, RL) through the energy-based model lens.
2611.14383.summary: Bo Dai and Yilun Du present EBMs via energy, inference, and learning choices, showing learning methods share a contrastive structure. They connect GANs, flows, diffusion, autoregressive models, contrastive learning and EBM policies in RL under one framework.
2611.14383.why: Useful reference for energy-based/equilibrium-matching views of generative policies, though a tutorial rather than new results.

2611.14186.tldr: Model-based RL with a stochastic Koopman linear dynamics model plus critic for one-step-lookahead policy gradients.
2611.14186.summary: K-MBRL learns linear Koopman dynamics so the model-based policy gradient reduces to a constant matrix product, uses one-step propagation plus a critic to avoid compounding error, and proves convergence. Validated on nonlinear robotic control.
2611.14186.why: Classical control-flavored MBRL; tangential to manipulation policy learning.

2611.13610.tldr: Survey of learning robot manipulation from egocentric human video, organized into four transfer paradigms.
2611.13610.summary: Ego2Robot learning is categorized as explicit embodiment transfer, action/task supervision, egocentric representation pretraining, and latent action/dynamics modeling. The survey traces what each extracts from human video and reviews datasets and benchmarks.
2611.13610.why: Handy overview for human-video-to-robot work, relevant to dexterous learning from human data.

2611.14834.tldr: Trains a compact action-chunk verifier from a frozen VLA's own rollouts and uses it to pick the best of sampled candidates.
2611.14834.summary: Expensive verifiers add latency to VLA best-of-N selection. HDH collects autonomous rollouts, trains a lightweight success-score verifier on action chunks, and selects among frozen-VLA candidates; it reaches 82.3% on four LIBERO-10 tasks and +22.6% on three real tasks.
2611.14834.why: Cheap test-time improvement for generative policies without fine-tuning.

2611.14432.tldr: Engineering report of a single pi0.5-based VLA solving 100 BEHAVIOR household tasks, emphasizing longer training and variance reduction.
2611.14432.summary: Building on their 1st-place 2025 solution, the team mostly trained longer and reduced gradient noise, adding stage embeddings, a 21-D action space, and variance-reduced multi-sample flow matching with a noise-vs-compute model. Q rose from 0.260 to 0.371 on shared tasks, 0.392 over 100 tasks (9th place).
2611.14432.why: Practical training-recipe lessons for flow-matching VLAs.

2611.14488.tldr: Shows memory-augmented VLAs use elapsed time as a shortcut for progress, failing under pauses (phantom progress).
2611.14488.summary: On RoboMME counting tasks, brief pauses or wrist fidgets drop success from 47 to 16 and 44 to 10 of 50, because time-stamped uniformly-sampled memory lets elapsed time predict progress. Rescaling timestamps alone shifts stopping behavior; the paper diagnoses and addresses this temporal shortcut.
2611.14488.why: A sharp understanding paper on history-conditioned policies, a stated interest.

2611.14033.tldr: Few-step streaming video generation that replaces DMD's fake-score network with condition-shifted estimation inside the generator.
2611.14033.summary: APEX uses a shifted text condition so the same generator estimates the fake velocity field, removing the separate fake network. On 180-second streams it slightly beats S2-Avatar in instruction fulfillment and aesthetics.
2611.14033.why: Few-step distillation trick, marginal gains; peripheral.

2611.13499.tldr: Navigation-oriented depth representation learning combining BEV reachability supervision with depth reconstruction.
2611.13499.summary: DeRep pretrains frozen encoders and evaluates them with linear probes, flow-matching IL, and PPO for cluttered navigation, comparing representation objectives under controlled conditions.

2611.14440.tldr: Unified generative model of RGB video, depth and camera pose using per-modality/time noise levels for 4D scene understanding.
2611.14440.summary: UGG treats generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion with heterogeneous noise levels, enabling training on partially-annotated datasets and inference-time search over scene hypotheses. It beats non-unified baselines.
2611.14440.why: Diffusion-forcing-style per-modality noise is a transferable idea; application is vision.

2611.14374.tldr: Replaces the critic and AAE penalty in a process-control offline RL method with a sparse GP critic using uncertainty-adjusted returns.
2611.14374.summary: On a polymerisation-reactor benchmark, the paper analyzes the AAE penalty in HOFLON and swaps in an sGP critic maximizing mu - kappa*sigma.

2611.13810.tldr: Small study finding four IL policies on an SO-101 arm unaffected by an 11.5x illuminance drop due to camera auto-exposure.
2611.13810.summary: ACT, SmolVLA, Diffusion Policy and pi0.5 trained on 50 demos had 20/40 vs 19/40 success at 520 vs 45 lux; image brightness barely changed thanks to auto exposure.
2611.13810.why: Methodology caution for real-robot evals; minor.

2611.13732.tldr: Action codec aligning actions, visual changes and language into a shared intent space, decoded per embodiment for cross-embodiment policies.
2611.13732.summary: CIALLO pretrains on eight embodiments and adapts to a new robot from a <=10s recording by updating embodiment embeddings only. A Qwen3.5-4B policy predicts intent, needing no large-scale robot-action pretraining, with 20 demos per task.
2611.13732.why: Relevant to action representations and cheap VLA recipes.

2611.14062.tldr: VR teleoperation to semi-autonomous dual-arm control paradigm for construction tasks.
2611.14062.summary: Combines VR guidance, a skill-primitive library, and shared autonomy with explicit role allocation, tested on facade installation.

2611.14049.tldr: Humanoid motion tracker that redacts selected movements by training on edited references while observing originals.
2611.14049.summary: RedirectMimic trains PPO tracking rewards on rule-edited references; on Unitree G1 sim it cuts forbidden content to 2.7% with 94.2% core-window success.

2611.14599.tldr: Builds a replay graph from experience and uses DP-derived shortest-path actions to guide DQN/SAC in sparse-reward tasks.
2611.14599.summary: StructRL boosts DQN success on MiniGrid (e.g., DoorKey 0.10 to 0.90) and SAC on PointMaze (0.17 to 1.0).
2611.14599.why: Simple exploration aid in discrete/toy settings.

2611.13923.tldr: Online selection of clustering topology for robust tube-based distributed MPC of coupled multi-agent systems.
2611.13923.summary: A mismatch measure from cost bounds plus communication penalty selects clusters online, preserving feasibility and stability; shown on an eight-agent spring-damper system.

2611.13766.tldr: GPU-accelerated dense QP solver for real-time linear MPC using fused kernels and CUDA graphs.
2611.13766.summary: FAME-QP reduces latency versus GPU solvers on benchmarks and simulated humanoid/quadrotor control.

2611.14307.tldr: Streaming multi-reference video generation with separate LoRA adapters for scene establishment vs continuation.
2611.14307.summary: TaoMate-R1 trains role-specialized adapters with Self Gradient Forcing, reducing boundary luminance jumps from 1.96 to 0.613.

2611.13986.tldr: Distributionally robust stochastic MPC with Gelbrich ambiguity sets and closed-form offline constraint tightening.
2611.13986.summary: Moment uncertainty is propagated to give a QP with a single additive robustness term and CVaR guarantees, illustrated on a planar quadrotor.

2611.13482.tldr: Adapts long-action-chunk policies with off-policy RL by learning only how long to execute each chunk.
2611.13482.summary: RL fine-tuning of long-chunk policies is sample-hungry due to high-dimensional chunks. ExRL adds a lightweight adapter predicting execution length per chunk, trained with off-policy RL, giving sample-efficient adaptation across diverse long-chunk policies in sim and real with little tuning.
2611.13482.why: Squarely at action chunking + RL fine-tuning of generative policies; simple and usable.

2611.14262.tldr: Recurrent spiking networks with community structure for RL, comparing ways to obtain modularity.
2611.14262.summary: CoRe SNNs use local three-factor learning and a new Map-STDP rule, comparing dynamic, partial and full modularity.

2611.14015.tldr: Distributes GRPO advantage over tokens according to top-2 probability margin (hesitation) for LLM RLVR.
2611.14015.summary: MCPO improves macro avg@32 by 6.55 points over GRPO on math benchmarks with MiniCPM 2B, and +4.75 on Qwen3-4B.

2611.13995.tldr: Lipschitz-controlled flow matching architecture and regularization for robust image restoration.
2611.13995.summary: Derives stability bounds for flow-from-Y and posterior sampling, then builds LipHDiT with spectral normalization and gain regularization, reducing adversarial sensitivity in face restoration.
2611.13995.why: Flow-matching stability analysis might interest; application is image restoration.

2611.14048.tldr: World action model inserting an interaction-centric latent reasoning expert between world and action experts in a Mixture-of-Transformers.
2611.14048.summary: LaST0.5 learns a compact latent supervised by robot-object interaction cues to bridge world modeling and action generation, with adaptive world-to-action reasoning.
2611.14048.why: Unified video-action model design, an 'also interested' area.

2611.13592.tldr: Few-shot residual corrections adapt a frozen latent world model to dynamics shifts from three interaction episodes.
2611.13592.summary: Corrections learned from latent prediction errors are applied inside the predictor and on predicted latents. On a real robot, success under CoM and friction shifts recovers from near zero to 90% and 100%.
2611.13592.why: Practical world-model adaptation with real-robot results.

2611.13528.tldr: LiDAR-inertial-visual 3D Gaussian splatting SLAM with refined extrinsics and online relocalization.
2611.13528.summary: GEMOR-GS calibrates LiDAR-camera extrinsics, refines keyframes and Gaussians, and supports relocalization.

2611.14515.tldr: A frozen teacher LLM diagnoses RLVR training experience and designs adaptive strategies and hints as training scaffolds.
2611.14515.summary: AutoScaffold applies across ALFWorld, search QA, math and kernel generation, improving students evaluated without scaffolds.

2611.15981.tldr: A high-force three-finger hand with 3-axis fingertip force sensing plus a nine-scenario real-robot suite for contact-rich removal tasks.
2611.15981.summary: Removal manipulation (adhesive detachment, cleaning, occluded retrieval) depends on partially observable contact states. DexRemo expresses fingertip forces in a shared wrist frame and trains ACT policies fusing vision, proprioception, fingertip pose and force; six core tasks benchmark the value of force sensing.
2611.15981.why: Contact-rich dexterous hardware + force-aware action-chunking policies, core interests.

2611.15381.tldr: Low-cost mobile bimanual SO-101 platform benchmarking four VLAs on long-horizon toilet cleaning.
2611.15381.summary: With 250 demos, pi0 performs best (60% strict, 70% relaxed, 90% with interventions) while progress- and memory-augmented variants fail to help.
2611.15381.why: Reproducible VLA comparison on cheap hardware; limited insight.

2611.15117.tldr: Hierarchical whole-body controller executing end-effector trajectories on quadruped mobile manipulators across arm morphologies.
2611.15117.summary: A trajectory-conditioned coordinator plans base motion from previewed EE targets, arm-specific IK tracks, and a frozen locomotion policy executes, extending reach across four arm families.

2611.15491.tldr: Systematic study of what makes chunked VLAs (pi0.5) reactive in dynamic manipulation: horizons, async inference, continuity, adaptation.
2611.15491.summary: On two dynamic sim benchmarks and three real tasks, the best prediction horizon is ~1 s, short horizons help more with async execution, and trajectory-continuity methods beat pure latency reduction. Changing execution horizon matched RL adaptation gains on a conveyor task.
2611.15491.why: Rigorous empirical guidance on action chunking and real-time chunk execution.

2611.15107.tldr: Agentic prompt refinement guided by predicted brain responses to make generated videos more memorable.
2611.15107.summary: MemCrafter builds a cortical-region neuro-memorability signal and sensitivity-aware feedback to refine T2V prompts.

2611.14969.tldr: Production VLA fleet-serving system coordinating heterogeneous computation with robot timing constraints.
2611.14969.summary: XInfer exploits parallelism while protecting time-critical feedback, giving 1.26-3.75x effective robot capacity over prior serving systems on three VLAs.
2611.14969.why: Systems for VLA inference; relevant only if deploying fleets.

2611.15133.tldr: Residual TD3 policy on top of an H2 controller enables domain-randomized sim-to-real vibration control of a powertrain.
2611.15133.summary: Model-based assistance stabilizes training under wide randomization; transfer demonstrated experimentally.
2611.15133.why: Automotive control; residual-RL idea is familiar.

2611.15246.tldr: Diffusion-policy RL scheduler with dual attention representations for flexible job-shop scheduling.
2611.15246.summary: DredRL uses a diffusion model as policy over scheduling decisions and outperforms DRL baselines on FJSP benchmarks.
2611.15246.why: Diffusion policy for combinatorial scheduling; off-domain.

2611.15658.tldr: Embedded Jetson pipeline comparing sim-to-real PPO reaching vs force-guided placement on a Franka.
2611.15658.summary: Learned hybrid and analytical pipelines achieve 70% and 74% real completion; perception latency 34.6 ms.

2611.15215.tldr: World model with adaptive fast-slow timescales to respond to, stabilize, and retain sudden dynamics changes.
2611.15215.summary: AFTER-WM, inspired by predictive coding, balances responsiveness, stability and persistence when payloads change during interaction.
