2611.26744.tldr: FORTH pairs forward-only tactile encoding, zeroth-order adapters, and a slip gate to ground VLA force control.
2611.26744.summary: It argues proxy losses don't imply force grounding; a slip-triggered gate achieves 29x lower peak grip force on a deformable shell, with 97.6% on LIBERO and 7.12x less activation memory.
2611.26744.why: Tactile grip control idea, but the framing is diffuse.

2611.26617.tldr: O2LaF initializes both inverse and forward latent-action dynamics from one pretrained video DiT to learn transferable actions from unlabeled video.
2611.26617.summary: A feed-forward transition encoder with action queries and a causal action-conditioned generator are both adapted from the same video DiT and trained end-to-end through a compact bottleneck. It sets state of the art in few-shot action probing and zero-shot action transfer across embodiments, and also works with V-JEPA2 priors.
2611.26617.why: Leveraging video generation priors for latent actions, relevant to video-action models.

2611.26444.tldr: Mind2Act World benchmark separates history reasoning, precise execution, and their composition across 30 sim manipulation tasks.
2611.26444.summary: The strongest agent gets 52.7% Mind and 39.0% Act but only 12.0% Mind2Act; end-to-end policies retain little task state.
2611.26444.why: Diagnostic benchmark highlighting memory limits of policies.

2611.26239.tldr: SAFI teaches VLAs to halt and keep holding objects when prohibited tasks are taken over mid-execution.
2611.26239.summary: Fallback targets with stationary arm and consistent gripper reduce takeover success to 1.3% with no physical incidents on LIBERO while retaining other skills.

2611.25683.tldr: TipDex-VTLA gates tactile-forecast-based action refinement by estimated visual reliability for illumination-robust dexterous manipulation.
2611.25683.summary: Visual reliability is learned from a reference policy's action sensitivity to lighting, and predicted-vs-measured touch discrepancies gate bounded corrections. On four real dexterous tasks it gets 87.5% normal and 73.8% under unseen lighting.

2611.26855.tldr: CoMP propagates epistemic uncertainty through flow-matching policy ODEs correctly, fixing BayesDiff's O(1/T) variance collapse.
2611.26855.summary: The authors prove BayesDiff's variance decays as O(1/T) with Euler steps, introduce EKF/UKF-style recursions carrying state-weight cross-covariance, and widen last-layer posteriors with observation embeddings. On three manipulation benchmarks it improves failure detection and demo selection.
2611.26855.why: Rigorous uncertainty estimation for pretrained flow policies.

2611.26040.tldr: Streaming-AAA generates 1080p controllable game video at 43 FPS with 198 ms latency via diffusion forcing and distillation.
2611.26040.summary: A redesigned VAE, long-horizon diffusion-forcing pretraining, and distillation with memory compression enable stable long play.

2611.25695.tldr: Gradient-free search over diffusion-generated natural textures to attack closed-loop VLAs.
2611.25695.summary: Reaches 57.9% clean-conditioned attack success vs 44.7% for UPA-RFAS with lower detectability.

2611.25778.tldr: ECHO is an in-context humanoid behavior foundation model adapting to dynamics via context-conditioned residuals.
2611.25778.summary: A behavior prior plus history-based dynamics representation enables adaptation without parameter updates, shown on G1 acrobatics and payloads.

2611.25838.tldr: ContextRenderer is an AR video diffusion renderer for game worlds following changing conditions.
2611.25838.summary: Dynamic-context learning and recurrent history compression enable minute-long interactive rendering.

2611.26098.tldr: Training-free frequency-selective boundary coupling for multi-prompt long video generation.
2611.26098.summary: FreqSync shares low/mid frequencies across prompt boundaries while keeping high-frequency details target-specific.

2611.25553.tldr: TwoPass self-conditions action-conditioned video prediction on its own draft, achieving SOTA with 4 NFE.
2611.25553.summary: Self-generated draft training and draft-reuse refinement keep the flow matching objective while cutting calls from 50-59 to 4 on Bridge and Language Table.
2611.25553.why: Fast video world models for policy evaluation.

2611.25667.tldr: CauSyncVLA predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visuals and executed actions, warm-starting flow correction for asynchronous control.
2611.25667.summary: A causal latent world model updates memory and predictive flow warm-starting aligns the unexecuted horizon; LIBERO-10 reaches 93.8% at 5.04x throughput.
2611.25667.why: Relevant to real-time chunking with flow policies.

2611.26334.tldr: Temporal rotation quantization enables 2-bit KV caches in video diffusion transformers.
2611.26334.summary: Online per-block planar rotations flatten channel means before quantization, improving subject consistency over QVG.

2611.26164.tldr: MultiBinder binds entity phrases to identity tokens to prevent multi-subject leakage in personalized video.
2611.26164.summary: An entity-aware Q-Former and MLLM director improve multi-subject identity fidelity.

2611.25494.tldr: Koopman lifting enables homomorphically encrypted linear LQR/MPC for nonlinear plants.
2611.25494.summary: Encrypted control matches unencrypted results on a CSTR.

2611.26825.tldr: Skill-JEPA learns a state-conditioned VAE skill space with Gaussian prior so planners' samples match world-model training data.
2611.26825.summary: Gaussian planner candidates are off-distribution for JEPA models; planning over latent skills raises success on 80-step goals from 42% to 62% across three models and four planners, and AntMaze far-goal success from 0.4% to 38%.
2611.26825.why: Clear insight on action-space mismatch in world-model planning.

2611.26763.tldr: Embeds GPU-batched MPPI within MCTS expansions for kinodynamic planning in cluttered maps.
2611.26763.summary: SI-MPPI yields the smallest search trees and smoothest controls on four 2D maps.

2611.26565.tldr: PhyDEX benchmark of dynamic throwing shows VLAs (<3% success) lack physical property reasoning.
2611.26565.summary: 35K automatically generated trajectories across nine tasks; giving ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success.

2611.26242.tldr: Training-free plan buffering with motion-aligned correction for fast off-road driving VLAs.
2611.26242.summary: Reduces FDE up to 36.7% at ~5% request rates and cuts processing cost ~17-21x.

2611.25927.tldr: Fast-JEPA predicts outcomes of complete action candidates for faster latent world-model planning.
2611.25927.summary: Achieves 96.5% average success with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT and introduces DynaGoal benchmark.

2611.25400.tldr: Dune is a zeroth-order optimizer with learned historical error regression for VLA test-time adaptation.
2611.25400.summary: Reduces ZO gradient variance without backprop, improving LIBERO and real-robot success at low memory.

2611.25373.tldr: Differentiable CFD-fit hydrodynamic model enables whole-body MPC of underwater vehicle-manipulators.
2611.25373.summary: Spherical-harmonic force fields with closed-form derivatives are validated and used in Stonefish closed-loop MPC.

2611.26438.tldr: R2-VLA calibrates retrieval-augmented VLA uncertainty to meet task-level risk with minimal expert help.
2611.26438.summary: Improves average success 9.2-11.2 points across three backbones on LIBERO with fewer expert requests.

2611.26865.tldr: FlowScope pretrains an ACT trunk on unlabeled surgical stereo video by forecasting metric 3D scene flow.
2611.26865.summary: On 1.35M clinical clips, scene-flow pretraining raises real needle pickup from 54% to 90%; metric 3D flow beats kinematics, 2D tracks, and depth as pretraining signals, and gains hold with a flow-matching head.
2611.26865.why: Medical domain, but the scene-flow pretraining insight transfers to manipulation.

2611.25336.tldr: MoRE is a 3D world model with rigid, deformable, and prehensile motion experts used with MPC.
2611.25336.summary: Mixed sim and real training improves regime-wise prediction and real-world MPC performance.

2611.26527.tldr: SAC-weighted ensemble forecasting of GPU power in AI data centers.
2611.26527.summary: Reduces normalized MAE to ~1% on MIT Supercloud telemetry.

2611.25500.tldr: PRIO predicts object-specific configuration spaces from static geometry for real-time Lagrangian 4D object dynamics.
2611.25500.summary: Pretrained on 4D trajectories, it generalizes to unseen shapes and supports real-to-sim and manipulation demos.

2611.28286.tldr: Adds classifier-free guidance and a scalable training recipe to Beckmann Transport Models for teacher-free one-step generation.
2611.28286.summary: Beckmann Transport Models learn one-step generative maps without distillation but lacked CFG and scalable training. SBM observes that the BTM current is a positive multiple of an autonomous denoising field, so CFG can be applied using the map's own conditional/null predictions, with characterized bias. Guidance provably shifts basin boundaries toward condition-favored modes while keeping single-NFE sampling.
2611.28286.why: One-step generation theory with guidance is directly in the reader's generative-model interests and relevant to fast policies.

2611.27266.tldr: PP-CFG keeps positive and negative prompts separate in a distilled few-step student to retain adjustable CFG and negative prompting.
2611.27266.summary: Few-step distillation tends to lose adjustable guidance and negative prompting. PP-CFG mixes positive/negative attention with opposite signs via a scale- and timestep-aware mixer in one backbone pass. On Wan2.1 with DMD it hits 81.46 VBench in four steps and beats teachers on a new 1K-prompt negative-removal benchmark.
2611.27266.why: Guidance in distilled samplers is loosely related, but this is an image/video product-quality paper.

2611.27288.tldr: Regularizes RL fine-tuning of diffusion models to preserve the pretrained CFG correction direction, reducing reward hacking.
2611.27288.summary: RL post-training of diffusion models often improves reward at the cost of overall quality. The authors view CFG and RL as correction vectors in prediction space, use the projection of the RL correction onto the CFG direction as a diagnostic, and propose Conditional Contrast Regularization to preserve it. Analysis and rotation interventions show the CFG direction carries quality information RL updates discard.
2611.27288.why: The CFG-vs-RL geometric view could inform RL fine-tuning of diffusion policies, though experiments are on images.

2611.27967.tldr: An agentic design 'Skill' iterates dexterous hand morphology through contact, dynamics, and learning gates, producing a 16-DoF SAGE Hand.
2611.27967.summary: Designing dexterous hands requires repeated expert iteration over geometry, URDFs, grasps and policy training. Task2Hand packages this into gated checks where an agent revises bounded parameters and escalates to a human, yielding SAGE Hand with four fingers, 16 DoF and an opposable thumb. Under matched training it reaches 45.6% in-hand success on a hexagonal prism vs 37.3% for a baseline.
2611.27967.why: Hand co-design for in-hand manipulation touches core dexterity interests, though results are sim and modest.

2611.27645.tldr: LS-MBPO improves frozen VLAs with a residual policy trained in a lightweight latent world model using subchunk rollouts.
2611.27645.summary: Model-based RL for VLAs usually relies on expensive video world models. LS-MBPO uses a latent world model with Hierarchical Forcing to curb compounding errors and Latent Subchunk Rollouts that refine frozen-VLA action chunks with a residual policy, plus a progress-conditioned branch-start curriculum. It aims for efficient imagination-based VLA improvement.
2611.27645.why: RL fine-tuning of VLAs with action chunks via world models is a direct fit to the reader's RL-for-BC interests.

2611.28256.tldr: Uses optical flow to jointly prune visual tokens and cache action blocks for faster VLA inference.
2611.28256.summary: Training-free VLA acceleration usually uses static token pruning and action caching. FlowPAC uses task-aware optical flow to propagate token importance, select contiguous tokens for KV-cache compression, and adaptively refresh action blocks. It targets lower latency and memory for edge deployment.
2611.28256.why: Systems-level VLA speedup; marginal for the reader.

2611.28402.tldr: BigSmall lets a 14B AR video model plan the opening chunk and a 1.3B model render the rest, keeping most quality at ~3x speed.
2611.28402.summary: The authors find that in AR video diffusion, letting the large model generate only the first chunk retains 95% of its semantic advantage, while the reverse retains 16%. BigSmall is a training-free planner-renderer sampler with a lazy cross-model KV cache. On VBench it is 3.02x faster than the 14B model.
2611.28402.why: Interesting insight about where capacity matters in autoregressive video diffusion; tangential to robotics.

2611.27011.tldr: Force-guided stage segmentation and an RL-refined retry policy let VLAs recover from failed grasps.
2611.27011.summary: VLAs often keep transporting after a failed grasp. FoRe splits demonstrations by force into approach-grasp and transport stages, trains a retry policy refined by local RL from post-failure states, and gates stages with force plus gripper status. It improves autonomous recovery on pick-and-place.
2611.27011.why: Practical force-based recovery, but narrow pick-and-place scope.

2611.27074.tldr: Hindsight Forcing routes gradients from future chunks back to history in AR video diffusion via a latent straight-through bridge.
2611.27074.summary: Self-rollout training of AR video diffusion truncates cross-chunk gradients, causing drift. Hindsight Forcing does full multi-step forward rollouts but backpropagates future losses to one selected denoising step per historical chunk, training context writing and denoising jointly. This reduces long-horizon drift and collapse.
2611.27074.why: Relevant to the reader's interest in autoregressive video diffusion / self-forcing training.

2611.28265.tldr: DeFlowCritic trains an internal critic on noisy latents to give dense rewards for RL alignment of text-to-image flow models.
2611.28265.summary: Sparse final-image rewards slow RL alignment of flow-matching T2I models. DeFlowCritic introduces a critic using diffusion features to score intermediate latents, trained on a new continuous-score reward dataset, for dense supervision. It aims for better Pareto trade-offs between composition and aesthetics.
2611.28265.why: Dense latent critics for flow RL are conceptually relevant to RL for flow policies but image-focused.

2611.27149.tldr: Studies how conserved quantities, symmetries and structured dynamics heads affect long-horizon rollouts of predictive world models.
2611.27149.summary: Accurate short-term prediction does not ensure physical rollouts. Across token models of planetary motion and JEPA-style visual models, they test conserved-quantity supervision, symmetry, temporal consistency and energy-based dynamics heads. Gains depend on how structure enters prediction, not on auxiliary readouts alone.
2611.27149.why: Analysis-style world-model paper on toy physics; mildly relevant.

2611.28289.tldr: InteR-VLA trains VLAs on diverse task-completing demos so they stay competent when safety filters intervene.
2611.28289.summary: Safety filters can push robots into states poorly covered by training data. InteR-VLA uses diverse demonstrations under the same data budget to broaden state coverage and mitigate intervention-induced shift. Real-world experiments raise safe success rate up to 90% from 0% for nominal training.
2611.28289.why: Demonstration diversity vs. distribution shift is a useful IL data insight.

2611.26981.tldr: ViewDreamer is a multi-view robot video world model handling variable camera sets via shared slot tokens.
2611.26981.summary: Robot data uses varying camera numbers and placements. ViewDreamer keeps per-view generation from a pretrained single-view model and couples views through slot tokens grouped by visual foundation models, with a view-count curriculum. It improves cross-view consistency on RoboView-Bench and carries over to world-action and action-conditioned models.
2611.26981.why: Multi-view video world models matter for robot policy learning and evaluation.

2611.27338.tldr: Latent Jacobian Steer maps joint-space perturbations through a policy-Jacobian inverse into latents to elicit contact-rich behaviors from a frozen humanoid controller.
2611.27338.summary: Exploring raw joints breaks coordination while latent exploration is hard to steer. LJS samples task-relevant joint-action perturbations, maps them via a damped inverse of the policy Jacobian to latent commands, executes them through the frozen behavioral foundation model and evaluates in sim. This elicits out-of-distribution contact-rich behaviors.
2611.27338.why: Steering a frozen pretrained policy's latent space resembles noise-space steering of diffusion policies.

2611.27171.tldr: Trains flow-matching VLAs with interval motion supervision to learn from demonstrations with missing action labels.
2611.27171.summary: Egocentric demos often have gaps in action labels but reliable endpoint poses. They add a composition objective constraining aggregate motion of missing actions plus a shared interval branch, while keeping flow matching on reliable actions. On LIBERO with 70.5% missing actions it reaches 87.9%, and 59.6% vs 48.8% (masking) on five real tasks.
2611.27171.why: Learning from incomplete/corrupted demonstrations with flow policies matches the reader's low-quality-data interest.

2611.27124.tldr: Shows latent world model planning can produce adversarial plans and adds a cheap action read-back check to CEM/MPPI.
2611.27124.summary: On DINO-WM and LeWM, more CEM iterations lower predicted cost but lose up to half of already-solved problems. They propose an action read-back network that penalizes mismatches between planned actions and predicted states. With 0.2-3.1% more planning time it improves CEM and MPPI on three tasks.
2611.27124.why: Sharp insight on failure modes of planning with learned world models.

2611.28346.tldr: Detects transferable adversarial attacks on VLAs by checking visual robot localization against proprioception.
2611.28346.summary: Transferable VLA attacks share the effect of disrupting the model's perception of the robot itself. The defense compares proprioceptive robot position with visually inferred position to detect and mitigate attacks. It detects adversarial patches and improves closed-loop and real-robot performance.

2611.27344.tldr: MoReWorld focuses action-conditioned video world model learning on predicted motion regions to improve interaction fidelity.
2611.27344.summary: Video world models optimize global reconstruction and miss contact details. MoReWorld predicts a motion region from history and actions and uses it for local motion prediction, region-aware loss, and gated conditioning. This reduces hallucinated contacts in robot video prediction.
2611.27344.why: Incremental but relevant to video world models for policy evaluation.

2611.26944.tldr: Characterizes batching and co-execution tradeoffs for serving multiple VLA clients on shared hardware.
2611.26944.summary: VLA serving leaves hardware idle. The paper measures latency, throughput, power and utilization for multi-client batching and co-execution. Findings inform future multi-VLA serving systems.

2611.28274.tldr: Neural Fidelity Calibration uses conditional flow matching to infer simulator parameters and residual dynamics online for sim-to-real fine-tuning.
2611.28274.summary: Domain randomization needs expert knowledge and calibration covers few parameters. NFC infers physical parameters and latent residual fidelity with flow matching, samples realistic environments for real-to-sim fine-tuning, and triggers adaptation only on anomalies. It targets agile locomotion sim-to-real.
2611.28274.why: Generative sim calibration is transferable to sim-to-real for hands, though shown on agile robots.

2611.27459.tldr: Ego2Ego generates a collaborator's egocentric video from one's own egocentric video, a scene point cloud and the collaborator's trajectory.
2611.27459.summary: Prior perspective taking was reduced to estimation or QA. Ego2Ego adds geometric modules rendering shared scene-coordinate maps into a pretrained video diffusion model to handle extreme viewpoint shifts. It defines and tackles generative visual perspective taking.
2611.27459.why: Egocentric video generation; tangential to manipulation.

2611.27164.tldr: PhysForce conditions an interactive video world model on applied forces with SFT plus RL for physically consistent responses.
2611.27164.summary: Representing forces as trajectories introduces motion priors. PhysForce encodes force location/direction/magnitude into video latents, adds a physics attribution network, and refines with RL. It improves physical consistency in unseen scenarios.
2611.27164.why: Force-conditioned video models are loosely relevant to contact-rich world models.

2611.28411.tldr: ScaleEvals evaluates generalist policies through reset-free autonomous play with VLM task proposal and grading across a fleet.
2611.28411.summary: Real-world policy evaluation is bottlenecked by resets and grading. ScaleEvals uses a VLM AutoPrompter and AutoGrader (90.7% human agreement) with Bradley-Terry scoring over 3,000+ rollouts on DROID and YAM, cutting human labor by 98%. Rankings correlate with manual evaluation (r=0.94).
2611.28411.why: Scalable real-world evaluation is valuable infrastructure for anyone training generalist policies.

2611.28319.tldr: Learns a world model predicting post-pick heightmap and picked mass from 61K production food-picking events.
2611.28319.summary: Food assembly robots must pick target weights. A model trained on self-labeled production picks predicts next heightmap and mass with uncertainty, achieving 10.93 g RMSE, 24% lower than the controller's estimate. Uncertainty-based rejection improves accuracy, though prediction barely responds to commanded action.

2611.27639.tldr: SOAR adaptively compresses latent world-model rollouts per planning decision while preserving candidate rankings.
2611.27639.summary: Sampling-based planners only need candidate rankings, so rollouts can be compressed. SOAR probes token budgets per decision and keeps the smallest that preserves ranking, keeping the first step exact. Across seven tasks it matches dense planning at 2.3x speedup.
2611.27639.why: Planning efficiency trick for latent world models; modest relevance.

2611.27547.tldr: Recovers pseudo-clean targets via video inpainting to train HUD removal from real gameplay footage.
2611.27547.summary: HUDs in gameplay videos obstruct world-model learning. GameScrub-Data inpaints HUD regions with a video diffusion model using flow-guided pre-fill to avoid leakage, producing training pairs. Models trained this way remove far more real HUD elements than synthetic-pair baselines.
2611.27547.why: Data cleaning for game videos; not relevant.

2611.27648.tldr: Caps per-rollout action-gradient norms when backpropagating through a learned world model for humanoid motion tracking.
2611.27648.summary: First-order world-model policy gradients are dominated by a few unverified large-gradient rollouts. The simulator confirms 94% of predicted change for small gradients but 1% for gradients above 30x median, so they cap at 10x median and adjust start sampling and resets. Trained on 223 h of motion, the tracker generalizes to 353 unseen motions.
2611.27648.why: Rigorous analysis of model-based policy gradients; transferable insight for RL with learned models.

2611.27173.tldr: PACE-WM conditions a JEPA world model on executed-action history and predicts futures in parallel for faster visual planning.
2611.27173.summary: Similar observations can hide different motion states. PACE-WM uses a recurrent memory of executed actions to condition a causal Transformer predicting multiple futures in parallel, and a RAMP action-scoring rule. It reaches 98% average success and plans 7-9x faster than LeWM.
2611.27173.why: History conditioning in world models parallels history-conditioned policies; moderately relevant.

2611.27129.tldr: Implements RL for manipulator reaching/grasping on a Mach-Zehnder-interferometer opto-electronic hybrid network.
2611.27129.summary: RL inference on electronics is power hungry. The authors use MZI-based optical computing in a hybrid RL architecture for point-to-point reaching and grasping. They target low-power edge deployment.

2611.27042.tldr: RoboColiseum combines system identification, composable simulation and multi-track benchmarking for embodied models.
2611.27042.summary: Simulation evaluation requires calibrated physics and diverse tasks. RoboColiseum uses recorded-command replay for sysID, links rigid/deformable sim to rendering, and achieves 0.97 real-sim score correlation over 22 configurations across eight tracks including dexterous manipulation. It reports leaderboards of agents and VLA policies.
2611.27042.why: Benchmark platform; useful only if evaluating in their sim.

2611.29096.tldr: JEPA-Tuner regularizes VLA fine-tuning with action-conditioned future latent prediction and enables asynchronous execution.
2611.29096.summary: Action-supervised VLA fine-tuning ignores how committed actions shape future observations. JEPA-Tuner trains a predictor to match guidance encoded from future observations given current guidance and committed actions, and trains the action expert on both observed and predicted guidance. Predicted guidance then supports asynchronous execution.
2611.29096.why: Predictive regularization plus asynchronous chunk execution touches real-time chunking interests.

2611.28752.tldr: VTLA-RL trains visuotactile VLA grasping policies with joint motion/force actions and sim-only RL post-training for varying loads.
2611.28752.summary: Mass and slip are hard to infer from vision, and fixed-load demos lack contact adjustments. VTLA-RL shares a visual encoder for tactile-image histories and RGB, outputs motion and bilateral force targets, pretrains on mixed real/sim demos, then applies two-stage multi-task RL in sim only and deploys zero-shot to real robots. They compare tactile representations and RL routes.
2611.28752.why: Visuotactile policies with RL fine-tuning of a BC prior and sim-to-real is squarely in the reader's interests.

2611.28512.tldr: Lifted multiple shooting with contact impulses as variables plus a parallel-in-time interior-point solver for contact-rich trajectory optimization.
2611.28512.summary: Non-smooth, multimodal contact dynamics hamper gradient-based trajectory optimization. Lifting contact impulses into decision variables lets state transitions use friction-cone-feasible impulses while consistency with the contact model is enforced separately, with implicit-differentiation sensitivities. IP-PAS, a parallel-in-time primal-dual solver, scales to long horizons and high-dimensional systems.
2611.28512.why: Contact-implicit trajectory optimization is useful for dexterous planning and demo generation.

2611.28509.tldr: AlpaSafe selects among driving-VLA candidate trajectories using a lightweight head on the VLA's prefill token predicting risk.
2611.28509.summary: Driving VLAs propose several trajectories but evaluation assumes an oracle selector. AlpaSafe reads the frozen VLA's last prompt token, fuses it with each candidate, and predicts scores and collision/offroad logits trained on closed-loop outcomes. A dominance rule then picks the safest high-scoring candidate.

2611.28707.tldr: IRIS pretrains an eye-in-hand inverse dynamics model on random exploration data to ground video-planned subgoals into actions.
2611.28707.summary: Imagine-then-execute pipelines are bottlenecked by IDMs trained on few task demos and by scarce eye-in-hand video. IRIS pretrains an execution-aware IDM on task-agnostic random exploration with eye-in-hand sensing to generalize action grounding. This decouples video planning from precise execution.
2611.28707.why: Video-planner + IDM pipelines are a key route for using video models in manipulation.

2611.28616.tldr: SWAN learns a multimodal action-chunk policy (mixture of factor analyzers) with advantage-aware improvement to guide MPPI in MBRL.
2611.28616.summary: MPPI planning latency grows with refinement iterations, and action-level planner imitation misses full H-step proposals. SWAN combines multimodal k-MPPI with an MFA action-chunk policy and advantage-aware target improvement. This yields stronger guidance with fewer planning iterations.
2611.28616.why: Action-chunk policies distilled from planners link TD-MPC-style RL with chunking.

2611.28697.tldr: TacitTouch distills a visuotactile diffusion/flow teacher into a vision-only student by matching denoising predictions and action features.
2611.28697.summary: Tactile sensors add hardware burden, and tactile-imagination methods propagate reconstruction errors. TacitTouch has a frozen visuotactile teacher supervise the vision-only student's denoising predictions and intermediate action representations at matched noisy action and flow time, so the student behaves as if it could feel touch. It targets contact-rich manipulation without tactile sensors at deployment.
2611.28697.why: Combines tactile sensing, contact-rich manipulation and flow/diffusion policy distillation, all core interests.

2611.28762.tldr: THAW adds a separately weighted temporal residual to CFG during early denoising to boost motion in video diffusion.
2611.28762.summary: Scalar CFG treats averaged and frame-varying differences equally, so raising it saturates colors. THAW amplifies the temporal component with a relative dose during a warm-up window without extra network evaluations. It raises VBench dynamic degree by about 14-15 points across five video models.

2611.28551.tldr: PhysPPF gives VLAs compact 3D physical tokens covering what/where/how plus past and future dynamics.
2611.28551.summary: VLAs model spatial and temporal reasoning separately. PhysPPF distills perception teachers into What-Where-How token groups at training time and models past/future transitions in the same physical token space. This targets precise 3D contact and long-horizon tasks without test-time 3D encoders.
2611.28551.why: Another VLA representation add-on; moderate relevance.

2611.28756.tldr: PSC-Gen uses an agent to plan and verify physical keyframes, injecting their low-frequency dynamics into video generation training-free.
2611.28756.summary: Video diffusion models produce physically implausible motion. A physics agent iteratively plans and verifies keyframes, interpolates them, and injects only low-frequency components as conditioning. This improves physical plausibility without training.

2611.28867.tldr: LIBERO-MOR benchmarks VLA robustness to 22 perturbations across vision, language, proprioception, action and environment.
2611.28867.summary: High clean success hides robustness gaps. LIBERO-MOR applies 22 perturbations at three severities on 40 LIBERO tasks with paired clean/perturbed protocol and evaluates seven VLAs. It reveals shared vulnerabilities and model-specific failure patterns.
2611.28867.why: Useful robustness diagnostics for VLA researchers.

2611.28839.tldr: SG-LL predicts a spatially grounded near-future latent relative to the present to guide VLA action generation.
2611.28839.summary: Future prediction in VLAs is often not grounded in control-relevant spatial state. SG-LL distills geometric priors into spatial tokens, learns a current-conditioned bottleneck latent of future information, and predicts it to guide actions. It improves precise manipulation.

2611.28675.tldr: A contact-adaptive low-DoF anthropomorphic hand plus a swing-twist motion glove performs complex teleoperated manipulation without tactile sensing.
2611.28675.summary: Replicating human hands involves trade-offs among DoF, force and durability. The authors design a hand with contact-adaptive fingers, slender form and sustained grip, plus a quaternion swing-twist motion glove and forearm interface for teleoperation. Demonstrations show complex tasks with limited active DoF.
2611.28675.why: Hand hardware and teleop interface relevant to dexterous data collection.

2611.29002.tldr: Explains CFG in autoregressive image models: shared logits encode token repetition, while the CFG difference carries sparse texture information.
2611.29002.summary: CFG works in AR image models but its mechanism is unclear. They show texture info lives in the conditional-unconditional logit difference while both logits are dominated by previous-token repetition, and prove via training dynamics of shallow transformers that this stems from texture sparsity. CFG thus removes shared repetition semantics.
2611.29002.why: Rigorous guidance theory; relevant to generative-model understanding, though for AR not diffusion.

2611.28717.tldr: ReCoRain couples content transfer and noise correlation by correspondence reliability for event-guided video deraining with diffusion.
2611.28717.summary: Ambiguous event correspondences can transfer wrong content in diffusion restoration. ReCoRain estimates reliability from RGB, events and motion consistency to weight feature aggregation and initial-noise sharing in residual flow matching. It improves deraining.

2611.28485.tldr: VICA detects and localizes AI-generated video by masking regions and checking agreement with frozen V-JEPA context predictions.
2611.28485.summary: Holistic detectors miss local artifacts while region methods miss context. VICA uses V-JEPA to predict masked region representations from context with complementary masking and measures disagreement. It unifies detection and localization.

2611.28963.tldr: LandWM learns a rain-actioned world model of land-surface water from satellite data with physical observation operators.
2611.28963.summary: Earth forecast models lack interpretable, counterfactual state. LandWM ties latent state to soil water via observation operators and mass-conserving balance, trained on SMAP and CYGNSS. It tracks in-situ probes as well as SMAP L4 and responds sensibly to counterfactual storms.

2611.28878.tldr: Paintress couples an executable code geometry proxy with a persistent 3D Gaussian appearance memory for consistent world generation.
2611.28878.summary: Video world models forget appearance of revisited places. Paintress pairs a code proxy for structure with a Gaussian memory separated into writer and refined reader copies conditioning generation, and introduces the Expedition-33 retention benchmark. It improves appearance consistency over long routes.
2611.28878.why: Memory for generative world models; tangential to manipulation.

2611.28723.tldr: AERIN is a UAV visual world model with a compact target-conditioned latent for aerial instance navigation.
2611.28723.summary: High-altitude search makes targets tiny and verification hard. AERIN uses action-conditioned prediction in a fixed-size latent to approach targets and adjust viewpoint. It beats baselines on target approach.

2611.29101.tldr: DUO Policy splits a skill into a human-video-pretrained hand policy for free-space motion and a robot policy for precise corrections, with a learned gate.
2611.29101.summary: Co-training on human and robot data treats sources as equally useful everywhere. DUO observes human data helps where precision demands are low, while robot data matters near precision-critical states; it uses a hand policy from human video, a robot policy from sparse in-hand data, and a gate learned from interventions. This enables fine-grained tasks like insertion with little robot data.
2611.29101.why: Clear insight on leveraging human video for precise manipulation, a core interest.

2611.28943.tldr: SANA-Robot is a 4.5B world action model with hybrid linear/sliding-window memory that runs in real time on edge devices.
2611.28943.summary: World action models are slow and lack long-term memory. SANA-Robot uses linear attention for constant-size global memory plus sliding-window softmax, and varies noise on action vs video tokens to act as policy or simulator. It supports minute-level memory tasks at constant inference speed with full-stack infrastructure.
2611.28943.why: Unified video-action models with long memory are in the reader's world-model interests.

2611.28803.tldr: Counterfactual Action Steering uses action differences under counterfactual instructions to fix trajectory hijacking when instructions switch mid-execution.
2611.28803.summary: VLAs and WAMs fail to redirect when instructions change mid-episode. CAS identifies interfering tasks, queries the policy with counterfactual instructions and steers away using target-counterfactual action differences, training-free. It improves on LIBERO-Goal-Switch and CALVIN-Custom-Switch across five policies.
2611.28803.why: CFG-like inference-time steering for policies; moderately interesting.

2611.28732.tldr: Entangle is an in-context world-action model that imitates a single human video, trained with video-to-video generated human contexts.
2611.28732.summary: Human-video in-context learning faces misaligned pairs and shortcut learning. Entangle converts robot videos into matched human contexts via video generation, adds real pairs, and uses variable-length windows with an intra-task contrastive loss. It generalizes to unseen tasks and contexts.
2611.28732.why: Learning from human videos with WAMs aligns with human-data and world-model interests.

2611.28585.tldr: AsyncMixVLA learns when to switch asynchronously to a heavier VLA policy for recovery under perturbations.
2611.28585.summary: Switching policies can stall or act on stale observations. AsyncMixVLA uses a learned trigger to escalate, overlaps inference with committed actions, and aligns context to the takeover state. It improves LIBERO-Long success under mid-rollout perturbations.
2611.28585.why: Asynchronous execution ideas are mildly relevant to real-time chunking.

2611.28809.tldr: RadAG builds a CFG-style reference by perturbing one block's attention logits against a reward, steering toward reward without full backprop.
2611.28809.summary: Extrapolation guidance is cheap but reward-agnostic; reward guidance needs full backprop. RadAG adversarially perturbs attention logits in a single block against the reward to form the guidance reference. It achieves efficient inference-time alignment.
2611.28809.why: Inference-time reward steering could transfer to diffusion policies.

2611.28628.tldr: Proves near-minimax sample complexity O(SAH^4/eps^2) for sample-based NPG in tabular finite-horizon MDPs with a matching lower bound.
2611.28628.summary: It asks whether direct policy optimization reaches the statistical limit. Sample-based NPG with backward sweeps achieves last-iterate guarantees under three schedules, and an information-theoretic lower bound matches up to logs. This settles NPG's sample efficiency in this setting.

2611.28939.tldr: T-Tac is a thin active thermal tactile sensor that identifies materials in-grasp from transient thermal responses.
2611.28939.summary: Vision struggles with similar-looking materials. T-Tac integrates a film heater and ionic temperature sensor, modeled with transient plane source theory, and classifies materials with thermal descriptors plus CNNs. It works under applied forces.
2611.28939.why: Tactile hardware, but material ID is peripheral to dexterous control.

2611.28438.tldr: LoKiTO optimizes UAV trajectories with Chebyshev polynomials and an online neural ESDF.
2611.28438.summary: Gradient planners struggle with map memory and dynamic limits. LoKiTO embeds kinodynamic constraints in the cost and uses a 1 MB neural ESDF from LiDAR. It achieves over 99.4% dynamic feasibility.

2611.28520.tldr: VG3R turns a pretrained video generation model into a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model.
2611.28520.summary: Video models capture depth and camera motion but not in reconstruction-ready form. VG3R adds clip-level shift prediction and a multi-layer camera head. It reconstructs faster than iterative methods.

2611.28873.tldr: NAT is a causal neural action tokenizer trained on 49k hours of cross-embodiment actions, beating FAST on unseen embodiments.
2611.28873.summary: Autoregressive VLAs need a universal action tokenizer. NAT is trained on robot, handheld, sim and human action data with a causal decoder enabling execution as tokens stream. It beats FAST/FAST+ across benchmarks and a real robot and narrows the gap to flow-matching heads with lower first-action latency.
2611.28873.why: Relevant to action representation choices vs. flow-matching heads in VLAs.

2611.29195.tldr: FunGrasp-Zero trains an RL graph-attention policy conditioned on object-centric contact-map potential fields for zero-shot cross-embodiment functional grasping.
2611.29195.summary: Functional grasping methods tie task representation to one hand via retargeted poses. FunGrasp-Zero represents intent as a cross-embodiment contact map mapped onto heterogeneous hands, builds attractive/repulsive hand-object potential fields, and conditions a graph attention RL policy on them. It enables zero-shot transfer to unseen hand morphologies.
2611.29195.why: Cross-embodiment dexterous functional grasping is squarely in the reader's core area.

2611.29553.tldr: Shows learned critics and world models detect VLA danger but cannot rank candidate action chunks, limiting sample-and-filter safety.
2611.29553.summary: Sampling several VLA action chunks and filtering with a world model can improve safety: with the simulator as exact model, safety rises 11.5-25.7 points on LIBERO. But learned critics reach pooled AUROC 0.864 for detection yet only ~0.55 within-decision ranking, and dynamics/video models do no better; 3.18 mm state error removes 70% of the gain. Selection, not detection, is the bottleneck.
2611.29553.why: Sharp analysis relevant to test-time selection and world-model-based evaluation of chunked policies.

2611.29279.tldr: A2I-VLA aligns force-tactile representations to semantics with future-wrench prediction, then integrates them into a VLA.
2611.29279.summary: Integrating force and touch into VLAs is hampered by representational gaps. Stage I learns aligned force-tactile features with cross-modal alignment, hierarchical fusion, and future wrench plus action prediction; Stage II integrates them into a VLA. It targets contact-rich manipulation.
2611.29279.why: Force/tactile VLAs are relevant, though the recipe is incremental.

2611.29383.tldr: Adapts Predict-and-Perturb self-refinement of flow samples to VLAs, improving SmolVLA on LIBERO by 5.3 points without ensembles.
2611.29383.summary: Test-time scaling for flow VLAs usually needs large candidate sets or external correctors. They adapt P&P, a mode-seeking self-refinement procedure from video generation, with modifications for action data. Over 400 LIBERO episodes with SmolVLA it improves the baseline by 5.3 points.
2611.29383.why: Noise-space refinement of flow policies relates to steering diffusion policies at test time.

2611.29618.tldr: Mass Forcing branches continuations from student-generated prefixes to make DMD distillation of AR video mass-aware and avoid mode collapse.
2611.29618.summary: DMD's reverse-KL objective collapses AR video students to few modes, and coverage-oriented initialization is transient. Mass Forcing moves on-policy supervision to individual states by branching several continuations from shared prefixes. It preserves diversity and dynamics.
2611.29618.why: Insight into mode-seeking distillation; relevant to few-step generative models generally.

2611.29610.tldr: A time-reversed curriculum with coordinated resets lets a PPO MLP policy learn diverse multimodal dexterous grasps with closed-loop robustness.
2611.29610.summary: Generative grasp methods are diverse but open-loop, while RL policies are robust but collapse to few strategies. Dr. Grasp-RL uses a time-reversed curriculum and coordinated resets so a simple PPO policy captures multiple grasp-pose modes while remaining closed-loop. Experiments show both diversity and robustness.
2611.29610.why: Simple RL trick for diverse dexterous grasping; directly usable.

2611.29646.tldr: JKO-GRPO augments Flow-GRPO for flow-matching VLAs with Wasserstein proximal (JKO) steps using transport targets from group advantages.
2611.29646.summary: Flow-GRPO and pi_RL reweight sampled actions by advantage but ignore distances between them. JKO-GRPO treats each state's action group as an empirical distribution, builds transport targets via a soft discrete c-transform of group-relative advantages, and regresses the deterministic flow sampler onto them alongside clipped Flow-GRPO without KL. It improves RL fine-tuning of pi0/pi0.5-style VLAs.
2611.29646.why: RL fine-tuning of flow VLAs with optimal transport is a core RL+generative-policy topic.

2611.29609.tldr: JEPA-Shield adds conformal uncertainty tubes and a backup shield to diffusion-style MPC with a frozen JEPA world model.
2611.29609.summary: Latent world model predictions don't guarantee constraint satisfaction. JEPA-Shield predicts motion from imagined rollouts, calibrates errors with split conformal prediction into tubes, and screens plans with a backup shield, proving probabilistic constraint satisfaction. Evaluated on a new vehicle parking benchmark.
2611.29609.why: Safe planning with world models; vehicle domain limits relevance.

2611.29377.tldr: Contact Harness guides a VLM agent with optimized skills and compliant force control to perform zero-shot contact-rich insertion.
2611.29377.summary: VLM agents lack contact-state awareness. Contact Harness interprets force/tactile feedback via reusable prompt skills and compliant execution, with no fine-tuning or demos. It achieves 90.7% full insertion across 15 connector types on real robots.
2611.29377.why: Zero-shot contact-rich skill via agents; an alternative to learned policies.

2611.29240.tldr: Tacinf is an open-source tactile stack spanning sim data, benchmark, VTLA policy learning, handheld collection and sim-to-real evaluation.
2611.29240.summary: Force-aware manipulation lacks integrated tactile infrastructure. Tacinf combines Tabero sim benchmark, VTLA policy training, Tacumi handheld data collection with the deployment gripper, and Taco sim-to-real evaluation. A model fine-tuned only on tactile sim data transfers zero-shot to real.
2611.29240.why: Open tactile infrastructure is practically useful for tactile policy research.

2611.29813.tldr: HR-AH is a two-timescale recurrent action head for tiny VLAs, separating slow task context from fast motor state.
2611.29813.summary: Tiny VLAs lack capacity for deliberation. HR-AH maintains fast low-level and slow high-level latent states exchanging information via nested updates before committing actions. It improves small VLAs without large latency.
2611.29813.why: Minor architecture work for small VLAs.

2611.29417.tldr: MSBench benchmarks script-controlled multi-shot text-to-video generation with 11 sub-metrics across 14 systems.
2611.29417.summary: Multi-shot video control from text is unmeasured. MSBench uses Scene-Entity-Shot scripts specifying timing, camera, content and transitions, scoring visual, dynamic, semantic and cross-shot consistency. Results show visual quality outpaces controllability.

2611.29431.tldr: HorizonFlow separates static and motion components of the DMD gradient and adds VAE-frame and layout constraints for fast video distillation.
2611.29431.summary: DMD motion lags because static gradients have higher SNR, and it lacks intra-latent motion and final-step layout signals. HorizonFlow addresses each, distilling few-step video models in about 600 iterations. It reduces stutter and drift.

2611.29662.tldr: Compares mixture density, tokenized and flow-matching skill-effect models for multimodal object-pose outcomes of contact-rich skills.
2611.29662.summary: Deterministic models average over distinct outcomes like sliding vs toppling. The authors learn multimodal distributions over object pose changes from partial point clouds and actions with three model classes plus latent dynamics. Multimodal models better predict which outcome occurs and reduce floating/interpenetration artifacts.
2611.29662.why: Multimodal contact-outcome modeling relevant to contact-rich planning.

2611.29693.tldr: HandiVid is a 200K-clip curated egocentric dataset with hand annotations for hand-driven interactive video generation.
2611.29693.summary: Egocentric datasets lack diversity, interactions and reliable hand annotations simultaneously. HandiVid merges public, online and synthetic videos with quality filtering, SAM 3-aided hand detection, 3D hand reconstruction and VLM interaction validation. It supports hand-conditioned interactive video models.
2611.29693.why: Hand-object video data may help human-to-robot dexterous learning.

2611.29518.tldr: Shows the episode reset threshold during PPO training changes which co-designed morphologies rank best.
2611.29518.summary: Co-design benchmarks rank bodies after training under a fixed protocol. Training 100 UNIMAL bodies with different fall-reset thresholds, rankings under Strict and Reset-free correlate only 0.21 vs 0.89 expected from seed noise. Protocol choices thus confound morphology selection.
2611.29518.why: Methodological caution for RL co-design; tangential.

2611.29732.tldr: Warm-starts DQN with LLM-generated advice-policy demos and a value warmstart robust to suboptimal advice.
2611.29732.summary: Demonstrations are costly and often suboptimal. They use an LLM-written advice policy to generate demos, warm-start DQN, guide exploration, and initialize values to recognize promising states without copying actions. They systematically perturb sub-skills to test robustness.
2611.29732.why: Discrete-action RL from suboptimal demos; low relevance.

2611.29771.tldr: Structured RL with sparse interaction edges, gated transport and hinted paths enables humanoid whole-body transport, including bed-to-wheelchair transfer.
2611.29771.summary: Whole-body humanoid manipulation suffers from high dimensionality, contact and long horizons. Three structural additions guide exploration while leaving strategy free, generalizing from objects to human transport. They show the first autonomous humanoid bed-to-wheelchair transfer of a mannequin.
2611.29771.why: Whole-body contact-rich RL; somewhat transferable ideas.

2611.29453.tldr: Decomposes latent world-model prediction error into shared offset and action-dependent parts to design slow-fast test-time training.
2611.29453.summary: Test-time training of world models helps planning but what it corrects is unclear. On PushObj, the shared offset accounts for 91% of AdaJEPA's gain and is partly episode-specific; sft-JEPA uses fast episodic and slow persistent learners accordingly. This improves planning under shift.
2611.29453.why: Clean analysis of TTT for world-model planning.

2611.29208.tldr: Force2Act plans motion and relative force per action chunk and uses a mixture of force experts for reactive compliance within chunks.
2611.29208.summary: Force-aware policies reproduce demonstrated force levels and fail when more force is needed. Force2Act plans motion and force relative to measured interaction once per chunk and uses a Mixture of Force Experts to regulate force each control step. It introduces Force2Act-Bench with five contact-rich tasks.
2611.29208.why: Combines action chunking with reactive force control for contact-rich manipulation.

2611.29178.tldr: Shows adaptive vector step sizes must be incorporated into eligibility traces for deep streaming RL and proposes such methods.
2611.29178.summary: Replay buffers are memory-heavy and slow at credit assignment, while eligibility traces enable streaming updates. The authors show adaptive vector step sizes must be part of the trace to keep forward-backward equivalence, and derive corresponding optimizers. This advances deep streaming RL.

2611.29125.tldr: SilentWAM plans driving trajectories from hidden states of masked future tokens in a diffusion world model without decoding frames.
2611.29125.summary: Reading WAM futures usually requires costly frame generation. SilentWAM pretrains masked world modeling on driving video and attaches planning queries to masked future positions. It reaches 92.0 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 at 60 ms latency.
2611.29125.why: Driving; idea of reading masked futures could transfer but low relevance.

2611.29483.tldr: Shows REPA-style feature alignment for VLAs rarely helps and proposes a behavioral structure metric to pick teachers.
2611.29483.summary: VLA representation alignment teachers are chosen heuristically. Across 14 teachers and 16 tasks, no encoder improves pi0.5 clean success by more than 1 point and all reduce perturbed success by 10-39 points. A behavioral structure metric, measuring whether feature-near states have similar expert actions, predicts which teachers help.
2611.29483.why: Rigorous negative result on a popular VLA fine-tuning trick.

2611.29339.tldr: Redirects VLA latent visual reasoning from predicting future frames to motion-oriented interaction latents for better generalization.
2611.29339.summary: Latent foresight aligned to future frames binds VLAs to training-scene appearance. Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning uses semantic latents for stage planning and motion latents capturing how the scene should evolve. It generalizes better to scene changes.

2611.29230.tldr: InfoField3D builds a differentiable analytic information field for constrained task-oriented camera view planning.
2611.29230.summary: View planning methods struggle with constraints or need many candidates. InfoField3D uses spherical harmonics and analytic Gaussian occupancy line integrals so viewpoint selection becomes continuous constrained optimization. It enables efficient constrained search.

2611.29749.tldr: CarlHOI uses a counterfactual relational latent world model to adapt multi-humanoid cooperative transport to unseen obstacles.
2611.29749.summary: Cooperative humanoid policies don't adapt to new constraints. CarlWM, trained on counterfactual sim rollouts, imagines futures under waypoint commands so teams can plan detours without retraining. It handles unseen environments.

2611.29205.tldr: DriveTTO refines driving trajectory proposals at test time via scorer-guided local search and fusion.
2611.29205.summary: Learned scorers can pick poor trajectories from fixed pools. DriveTTO searches around proposals and perturbs controls, accepting updates only when frozen scorers agree. It recovers nonzero PDMS in 51% of zero-score Navtest cases.

2611.29259.tldr: REINFORCE Look Back uses counterfactual world models' returns as baselines to separate action effects from environmental luck.
2611.29259.summary: In stochastic environments, imagining whole trajectories is hard. Counterfactual world models transform observed trajectories under alternative actions, and RLB uses counterfactual returns as baselines with proven unbiasedness and variance reduction. When dynamics are harder than action effects, this beats standard world-model RL.
2611.29259.why: Novel policy-gradient variance reduction; of RL fundamentals interest.

2611.29123.tldr: PlanNudge freezes a diffusion driving planner and trains an MLP RL policy to output small speed/curvature nudges.
2611.29123.summary: RL fine-tuning diffusion planners is complicated by iterative denoising and receding horizon. Observing small adjustments avert many failures, PlanNudge learns a lightweight residual nudge policy. It improves closed-loop safety while preserving pretrained behavior.
2611.29123.why: Residual RL on frozen diffusion policies is transferable to manipulation despite driving domain.

2611.29156.tldr: ARC adaptively controls rollout admission and completion in synchronous LLM RL to reduce idle compute.
2611.29156.summary: Synchronous LLM RL waits on variable-length group rollouts. ARC uses streaming backfill, deferred group completion and adaptive control to avoid wasted generation. It improves training throughput.

2611.30898.tldr: Native LAM turns a pretrained video diffusion transformer into both inverse and forward dynamics, extracting compact latent actions via dynamics registers.
2611.30898.summary: Latent action models train IDM/FDM from scratch, trading reconstruction against latent capacity. Native LAM uses one pretrained video DiT as both, bridged only by learnable dynamics registers, trained on counterfactual pairs differing only in motion, so registers distill compact latent actions. They also propose a pretraining paradigm using these latents for action-free video.
2611.30898.why: Latent actions from video world models are a promising route to learning from human/egocentric video.

2611.30477.tldr: OVOGO does offline RL for flow VLAs by separating offline critic learning from on-policy resampling of the generative process.
2611.30477.summary: Collecting new robot interactions for flow-VLA improvement is costly, but fresh generation trajectories can be resampled cheaply at replay observations. OVOGO learns a Return-Anchored Ranking Critic combining in-sample distributional value learning with guarded local ranking, then optimizes the flow policy on-policy over generated actions. It improves flow VLAs from logged experience.
2611.30477.why: Offline RL fine-tuning of flow-matching policies is a core RL+generative topic.

2611.31164.tldr: Analyzes standalone FlowMap distillation for AR video and adds anti-drifting and motion-aware guidance, working with pi-Flow, MeanFlow and consistency distillation.
2611.31164.summary: Few-step AR video models still need DMD, losing diversity and requiring a bidirectional teacher. The authors add anti-drifting guidance (an auxiliary model mimicking student drift as a negative branch) and motion-aware skip-layer guidance on motion patches. This improves quality and reduces drift for 1.3B AR teachers across several flow-map methods.
2611.31164.why: Flow-map/MeanFlow distillation for autoregressive generation relates to one-step and streaming flow policies.

2611.30490.tldr: EgoStudy runs controlled experiments on how egocentric human data scale, diversity and processing affect VLA and world-action-model pretraining.
2611.30490.summary: The value of egocentric human data for robots is unclear due to embodiment gaps. Holding robot data fixed, they vary egocentric scale, diversity, processing and co-training for VLAs and WAMs. Diversity, trajectory alignment and detailed language matter most, with scaling effects differing between VLAs and WAMs.
2611.30490.why: Systematic study on learning from human egocentric data, central to dexterous data scaling.

2611.30328.tldr: Draft Forcing uses target-guided feature-level drafting and a learned verifier for speculative decoding of AR video diffusion.
2611.30328.summary: Off-the-shelf draft models diverge from the target and verification is weak. Draft Forcing conditions drafts on target hidden states and trains an on-policy feature-space verifier with calibrated frame-wise scores. It speeds streaming video generation.

2611.30907.tldr: DexLatentWorld learns a 3D cross-embodiment latent-action world model from retargeted human point-cloud demos and plans with MPC in latent space.
2611.30907.summary: World models need action labels and are embodiment-specific. A contrastive objective learns continuous latent actions from point clouds of retargeted human demos; MPC samples latent actions predicting particle futures, and robot commands are recovered from predicted geometry without an embodiment decoder. This enables zero-shot manipulation on unseen embodiments.
2611.30907.why: Human-demo-driven cross-embodiment world models for dexterous manipulation.

2611.30516.tldr: JEPA-ICL predicts progress-aligned JEPA latent plans that guide actions and retrieve relevant demo stages for in-context manipulation.
2611.30516.summary: Demonstrations differ in embodiment and speed, making relevant guidance hard to locate. JEPA-ICL predicts ordered future JEPA states to subtask completion, using them to guide actions and align demo stages as context. It reaches 80.0% seen-task success on Imitator Game, 12 points above Zero-WAM.
2611.30516.why: In-context imitation with predictive latents; moderate relevance.

2611.30209.tldr: RoboAda keeps a frozen policy's plan but corrects commands by inferring the robot's command-to-motion mapping at test time.
2611.30209.summary: Invisible physics changes (heavy objects, weak joints, lag) make correct plans execute poorly. RoboAda uses an inverse-dynamics view after each action chunk to infer how commands map to motion and corrects execution, without altering the plan or risking harmful gradient updates. It adapts frozen policies to unseen physics.
2611.30209.why: Test-time execution adaptation for chunked policies is practical for contact-rich deployment.

2611.30572.tldr: VeriTouch generates synthetic visuo-tactile trajectories with a joint video-tactile world model and verifies them for policy learning.
2611.30572.summary: Visuo-tactile data is costly to collect. VeriGen jointly generates dual-view videos and tactile sequences from an initial image and instruction using a tactile expert plus pretrained video model, and VeriEval filters for visual and tactile plausibility. Verified synthetic data improves visuo-tactile policy learning.
2611.30572.why: Synthetic tactile data from video generation (DreamGen-style) matches both tactile and world-model interests.

2611.30495.tldr: DexDuet learns contact-preserving bimanual dexterous RL policies from a single human demo with interaction rewards and an assisted curriculum.
2611.30495.summary: Object-tracking rewards let robots contact wrong parts or slide fingers. DexDuet adds two interaction rewards preserving human hand-object contacts, factorizes bimanual control into weight-sharing per-hand policies conditioned on each other, and uses assisted reference-state initialization. It is evaluated across four bimanual benchmarks.
2611.30495.why: Bimanual dexterity from human demonstrations with RL is exactly the reader's core area.

2611.30145.tldr: RMR adds an explicit recurrent memory-reasoning step to VLAs, doubling RoboMME success and refining memory tokens with GRPO.
2611.30145.summary: History-dependent tasks require acting on vanished cues. RMR has the VLA infer events, revise task state and ground subgoals as text carried across updates, with GRPO refining memory decisions. It doubles success on RoboMME over a non-recurrent baseline.
2611.30145.why: History-conditioned policies are an interest area; this uses text memory.

2611.30291.tldr: W3H-VLA adds spatial distance and geometric structure perception with adaptive guidance on top of VLM semantics.
2611.30291.summary: VLM features identify which entities matter but not where or how. W3H-VLA adds distance and geometry perception plus adaptive weighting. It improves precise manipulation.

2611.30083.tldr: MotionServe schedules shared-GPU LoRA VLA inference across robots by exploiting action-chunk execution slack.
2611.30083.summary: Dedicated GPUs per robot are costly; batching consumes execution slack. MotionServe dispatches requests to balance batching efficiency against stalls and replanning. It improves multi-robot serving.
2611.30083.why: Systems; mildly relevant to chunked execution timing.

2611.31184.tldr: CodecOPSD prunes redundant condition tokens using video-codec cues and on-policy self-distillation, halving denoising cost.
2611.31184.summary: Conditioning tokens dominate compute in all-in-one video models. Codec-based pruning removes 66% of condition tokens across 16 modalities and an OPSD-trained adapter avoids quality loss. Denoising becomes 2x faster.

2611.30534.tldr: DelayOPSD distills a synchronous flow-VLA teacher into an asynchronous delayed student on the policy's own rollouts for real-time execution.
2611.30534.summary: Asynchronous chunk execution conditions on stale observations; actions differ little on expert data but diverge on the policy's own delayed rollouts. DelayOPSD trains the delayed student, seeing an earlier frame plus pending actions, to imitate the synchronous teacher on on-policy rollouts. This recovers performance under latency.
2611.30534.why: Directly addresses real-time/asynchronous action chunking, a core interest.

2611.30178.tldr: LoopQ calibrates ultra-low-bit VLA quantization on the quantized policy's own rollouts with readout-aligned fine-tuning.
2611.30178.summary: PTQ collapses at 2 bits due to offline calibration shift and poor reconstruction proxies. LoopQ calibrates on-policy and fine-tunes lookup tables to align action-head readout with the teacher. It enables ultra-low-bit VLA deployment.

2611.30363.tldr: SOAR is a one-step generative policy that directly predicts DCT coefficients of action chunks to capture temporal structure.
2611.30363.summary: Multi-step diffusion/flow policies are slow, and velocity-parameterized one-step flows recover actions indirectly. SOAR predicts an observation-conditioned DCT representation across frequency bands and directly generates clean action trajectories, enabling structural calibration. It improves one-step action quality at one-step cost.
2611.30363.why: Fast one-step generative policies with action chunk structure are a core interest.

2611.29913.tldr: MoMa-NMP trains a scene-scale neural motion planner for mobile manipulators on millions of generated whole-body trajectories.
2611.29913.summary: Generating training data for room-scale neural motion planning is hard. MoMa-DemoSmith splits global path discovery from local refinement to synthesize trajectories, and MoMa-NMP is trained with BC then privileged on-policy distillation. It achieves 87.0% sim and 77.5% real success.
2611.29913.why: Large-scale BC from planner demos; mobile manipulation is adjacent.

2611.31239.tldr: Lyris generates long camera-controlled walkthroughs anchored by persistent point-cloud memory and VLM-authored 3D layouts.
2611.31239.summary: Memory-based video lacks anchors beyond seen regions and layouts need manual authoring. Lyris combines persistent point-cloud memory with VLM-generated 3D layouts. It yields consistent long videos.

2611.30659.tldr: ActField is a continuous-time JEPA world model integrating an action-conditioned latent vector field over physical time.
2611.30659.summary: Discrete-interval JEPA world models leave action-effect dynamics implicit. ActField separates action-independent and action-induced evolution in a continuous latent ODE with reference conditioning and multi-step loss. It improves prediction on LIBERO, DROID and BEHAVIOR.
2611.30659.why: Continuous-time latent dynamics for manipulation world models.

2611.30632.tldr: GeoMerge-OPD integrates heterogeneous VLA skills via response-space regularization, parameter merging and on-policy distillation.
2611.30632.summary: Joint fine-tuning or merging skill experts causes unintended actions. Analysis reveals opposing expert responses in shared high-energy directions; GeoMerge-OPD constrains update gains, merges and distills on-policy. It preserves individual skills in whole-body tasks.

2611.30550.tldr: RoboHarness-Zero wraps a frozen VLA with a VLM that selects targets and tracks progress without task-specific preparation.
2611.30550.summary: 43% of a VLA's failures involve wrong targets or lost progress. The harness lets a VLM handle target choice and progress while the frozen VLA executes contact-rich motion, without per-task prep or policy redesign. It improves multi-skill task completion.

2611.30463.tldr: Multi-trajectory MPC decouples safety and exploitation for UAV navigation in unknown environments.
2611.30463.summary: LiDAR gives partial, time-varying constraints. mt-MPC optimizes multiple future trajectories in one problem, separating constraint satisfaction from cost minimization. It navigates UAVs safely.

2611.30111.tldr: RoboThink lets a reasoning agent correct a running policy through instruction and learned feedback channels.
2611.30111.summary: Policies can't follow new instructions mid-task or fix motion drift. RoboThink rewrites instructions training-free and trains a feedback channel via agent-labelled DAgger with role tokens and counterfactuals. Robots correct themselves mid-execution.

2611.31126.tldr: WeaveVLA encodes task-relevant 3D relations with a recurrent sparse graph to condition the VLA action expert.
2611.31126.summary: VLAs implicitly handle 3D relations. WeaveVLA uses a task-conditioned sparse GNN with recurrent edge states and learned-query readout, plus geometry reconstruction. It improves relational manipulation.

2611.31079.tldr: Wrist Video Policy predicts future wrist-camera views and recovers end-effector poses via a stitched 3D pose estimator.
2611.31079.summary: Generalist policies need cross-task and cross-embodiment transfer. WVP represents motion as wrist-camera trajectories, pairs a wrist-view video generator with a pretrained 3D pose estimator, and stitches latents directly into the estimator. Task knowledge scales with video data while geometric estimation is reused.
2611.31079.why: Video-generation-as-policy with clean action recovery is relevant to world-model policies.

2611.30636.tldr: ABI learns actor-free, reward-free multi-horizon action-chunk representations for zero-shot test-time guidance of BC policies.
2611.30636.summary: Offline RL couples critics to actors or needs task rewards. ABI notes behavior-policy action evaluation preserves value ordering across target policies and learns successor-style chunk representations from unlabeled data; lightweight task readouts guide frozen chunked BC policies at test time. This enables zero-shot task generalization.
2611.30636.why: Test-time value guidance of action-chunk BC policies is relevant to RL+generative policies.

2611.30308.tldr: ConsisX enforces cross-view 3D association and entity coherence in multi-view VLAs.
2611.30308.summary: VLMs associate views by 2D similarity, causing misassociation. ConsisX adds 3D proximity constraints and entity coherence organization. It improves physically consistent manipulation.

2611.30986.tldr: iTDM identifies baseline-induced gradient drift in forward diffusion RL and fixes it via instantaneous trajectory distribution matching.
2611.30986.summary: Forward diffusion RL methods are signed reward-weighted regression whose baseline subtraction assumes policy velocity equals behavior marginal velocity, violated under CFG, off-policy updates and imperfect self-consistency. iTDM takes the infinitesimal limit of trajectory distribution matching to remove this mismatch. It stabilizes diffusion RL alignment.
2611.30986.why: Clear theoretical insight into RL for diffusion/flow models, transferable to diffusion policies.

2611.30372.tldr: ColonoWorld generates camera-controlled full colonoscopy videos conditioned on a coarse 3D colon tube.
2611.30372.summary: Autonomous colonoscopy needs a world model. ColonoWorld conditions on camera trajectory and colon geometry, places polyps and events, and cuts trajectory error 32% and FVD 29%. It generalizes to unseen colon shapes.

2611.31002.tldr: RoboUniverse-10K provides 10,807 real-to-sim verifiable environments for agentic code-as-policy robotics.
2611.31002.summary: Agentic robotics lacks large executable environments. An automated Real2Sim pipeline from real videos builds resettable environments plus a 500-task verified benchmark; frontier models reach 85.8% vs open models at 2.6-10%. It targets post-training of coding agents.

2611.30120.tldr: AxE Bench tests video world model generalization by varying agent and environment factors in controlled pairs.
2611.30120.summary: Video world model evaluations emphasize quality over systematic generalization. AxE organizes condition changes along eight factors and pairs originals with controlled variants, also extending WBench. It reveals generalization gaps.
